雅思口语 · 话题与表达
80
话题 63  /  在团队中工作
PART 3
1. Why would someone choose to work alone?
为什么有人更愿意独自工作？ 从节奏控制和沟通成本解释选
择，避免把独立工作说成不合群。
Working alone gives people control over their pace and
methods. They don't have to wait for agreement on every
small decision, which can help with tasks requiring
concentration. A writer, for example, may need
uninterrupted time to develop an idea. That preference
doesn't necessarily mean they dislike people; the task
may simply suit independent work.
独自工作能让人掌握自己的速度和方法，不必每个小决定都
等人同意，适合需要专注的任务。例如，写作者可能需要不
被打断的时间展开想法。这种偏好不一定表示不喜欢别人，
也许只是任务适合独立完成。
uninterrupted time 不被打断的时间
2. What can a leader do to earn team members'
support?
领导者怎样做才能让成员愿意跟随？ 把支持建立在公平分工
和兑现承诺上，用困难时承担责任作证据。
A leader needs to be clear, fair and willing to do their
share of difficult work. People are more likely to
cooperate when they understand the goal and believe
their concerns will be heard. Following through on
promises also matters. If a leader accepts responsibility
when something goes wrong, trust is easier to maintain.
领导者需要说清方向、公平处事，也愿意承担自己那份困难
工作。成员理解目标，并相信自己的顾虑会被听见时，更愿
意合作。兑现承诺同样重要。出了问题时，领导者愿意承担
责任，就更容易维持信任。
follow through on promises 兑现承诺
3. Should pupils be taught how to work in groups?
学生应该学习团队合作吗？ 说明协商和分工需要练习，再指
出评价办法要避免少数人包办。
Yes, because cooperation involves skills that don't
appear automatically, such as dividing tasks and
disagreeing politely. Group projects give students a safe
place to practise those skills. Teachers should make
individual responsibilities visible, though. Otherwise,
one student may do everything while others receive the
same credit, which teaches frustration rather than useful
teamwork.
应该，因为分配任务、礼貌表达不同意见等能力不会自动出
现。小组项目能让学生在相对安全的环境里练习。不过教师
应让个人责任清楚可见，否则可能一人包办、大家同得评价，
学生学到的就只是挫败感。
divide tasks 分配任务
4. What kinds of schoolwork involve a group?
学校里有哪些需要小组完成的任务？ 列出不同学科中能合作
的具体任务，并说明不是坐在一起就算合作。
Students may prepare presentations, carry out science
experiments or produce a short play together. Sports
events and school exhibitions also require shared
planning. The best group tasks need different
contributions to form one result. Simply asking several
pupils to sit together and finish identical worksheets
doesn't create much reason for them to cooperate
meaningfully.
学生可以合作准备展示、做科学实验或排短剧，运动会和学
校展览也需要共同安排。好的小组任务要把不同贡献合成一
个成果。只是让几个学生坐在一起做相同练习卷，并不能提
供真正合作的充分理由。
shared planning 共同规划

sections.title: 帮助他人的时刻
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
朋友、聚会与互相帮助
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
81
话题 64
PART 2
帮助他人的时刻
Helping someone solve a problem
Describe a time when you helped another person deal with a problem.
描述一次你帮助别人解决问题的经历。
1. When it happened
发生在什么时候
2. Who needed your help
你帮助了谁
3. What the problem was and how you solved it
是什么问题以及怎样解决
4. How you felt about helping
你对此有何感受
审题与选材：帮助不一定是紧急救援，小问题也能讲得完整。先说明对方卡在哪一步，再按你检查和处理的顺序写动作。让
对方也参与尝试，结果才不只是你单方面完成。感受可联系对方重新掌握事情后的反应，避免空泛赞美自己。
叙述顺序
A 交代上个月帮邻居做照片备份 - B 说明手机空间不足引发焦虑 - C 描述检查储存并复制照片 - D 让邻居亲自确认文件已
保存 - E 说明看到她安心后的满足感
A Introduce helping my neighbour with her phone - B Explain her worry about losing family photographs - C Describe
checking storage and copying the pictures - D Show her confirming the backup by herself - E Connect her relief with my
own satisfaction
示例回答
Last month, I helped my neighbour, Mrs Wu, with a problem on her phone. It kept warning her that the storage
was full, and she was afraid to delete anything because it contained several years of family photographs. She
mentioned it when we met by the lift. I said I could have a look, and we arranged a time the following evening.
At her kitchen table, I first checked what was taking up space. There were many duplicate videos from group
chats, but her biggest concern was the photographs of her grandchildren. We connected the phone to her laptop
and copied the pictures into folders labelled by year. I didn't simply tell her the copying was finished. I asked her
to open several photographs on the laptop herself, so she could see they were really there. Then we made an
additional copy on a drive she already owned before removing unnecessary duplicates from the phone. The
whole thing took about an hour. By the end, her phone had room again, and she knew where to find her pictures.
I felt pleased, mainly because she looked so much less worried. It wasn't a complicated technical achievement
for me, but slowing down and explaining each step made a real difference to her.
中文对照：上个月，我帮邻居吴阿姨解决了手机问题。手机一直提醒储存空间满了，但里面有好几年的家庭照片，她不敢
删。我们在电梯旁碰面时，她向我提起了这个让她担心的问题，我说自己可以抽时间帮她检查一下，约了第二天晚上。在
她家餐桌旁，我先检查什么占空间：群聊里有许多重复视频，但她最担心的是孙辈的照片。我们把手机连到她的笔记本电
脑，按年份建文件夹复制照片。我没有只说复制好了，而是让她亲手在电脑上打开几张，确认真的保存了。之后又用她已
有的硬盘多存一份，才从手机删除不需要的重复内容。整个过程约一小时。最后手机有空间了，她也知道去哪里找照片。
我很高兴，主要因为她明显不再那么担忧。对我而言技术并不复杂，但放慢速度、解释每一步，确实帮到了她。
自然表达
take up space
占用空间
have a look
看一看；检查一下
make an additional copy
再备份一份
make a real difference
带来切实的改变
串题 话题 65 给别人建议
可沿用吴阿姨的手机储存困难，把重点转到先备份再删除的建议，并解释为什么需要多存一份，而不是只列操作步骤。
Before we removed anything from her phone, I advised her to make another copy of the family photographs.

82
话题 64  /  帮助他人的时刻
PART 3
1. Do people generally enjoy offering help?
人们通常喜欢帮助别人吗？ 承认帮助别人带来的满足，同时
说明时间和实际能力会影响意愿。
Many people do, especially when they understand the
problem and can see that their effort is useful. Helping
can create a sense of connection and satisfaction.
Willingness still depends on time, ability and the size of
the request. Someone who declines a demanding favour
may be exhausted rather than uncaring, so context
matters.
许多人喜欢，尤其在了解问题、看得出自己的付出有用时。
帮助别人能带来联系感和满足感。不过意愿仍取决于时间、
能力和请求的大小。有人拒绝费力的帮忙，可能只是很疲惫，
并非不关心别人，所以要看处境。
a demanding favour 费时费力的帮忙请求
2. Is it important that parents teach children to help
other people?
父母教孩子帮助别人重要吗？ 从家庭示范解释学习过程，给
出孩子能完成而不承担过重责任的事。
Yes, because children often learn what is normal by
watching their parents. Small actions, like carrying a
neighbour's shopping or checking on a relative, show
what consideration looks like. Children can join in with
manageable tasks. The aim should be understanding
another person's needs, rather than being praised for
every helpful act they perform.
重要，因为孩子常通过观察父母了解什么是日常行为。帮邻
居提东西、关心亲属等小事，能展示体贴是什么。孩子可以
参与力所能及的部分。重点应是理解他人的需要，而不是每
做一件好事就获得夸奖。
manageable tasks 力所能及的任务
3. Is teaching by parents alone sufficient for
children?
只由父母来教育孩子就足够了吗？ 承认父母作用，再说明学
校同伴能提供家庭无法覆盖的合作场景。
Parents are important, but children also need
opportunities to practise outside the home. Teachers can
guide cooperation between classmates, and community
activities let children meet people with different needs.
Those experiences make helpful behaviour less
dependent on family instructions. It also helps when
adults in different settings give consistent messages
about respect and responsibility.
父母很重要，但孩子还需要在家外实践的机会。教师能引导
同学合作，社区活动让孩子接触不同需要的人。这样，助人
就不只依赖父母的指示。不同场合的成人对尊重与责任传达
一致信息，也会有帮助。
outside the home 在家庭之外
4. What everyday difficulties commonly require help
from others?
日常生活中哪些困难常需要别人帮助？ 把短时实际困难和需
要解释的事情分别举例，说明帮助不等于代办。
People often need help with unfamiliar technology,
moving heavy objects or understanding complicated
forms. Temporary situations matter too: someone
recovering from an illness may need groceries collected.
Help doesn't always mean taking over the whole task.
Sometimes a clear explanation or an extra pair of hands
is enough for the person to manage independently
afterwards.
人们常需要帮助操作陌生技术、搬重物或看懂复杂表格。暂
时的情况也算，比如病后恢复时需要别人代买食品。帮助不
一定是全盘接手，有时解释清楚，或多一个人搭把手，就能
让对方以后自己处理。
an extra pair of hands 多一个帮忙的人
5. Are people less ready to help strangers now than in
the past?
与过去相比，如今人们更不愿意帮助陌生人吗？ 区分谨慎与
冷漠，说明陌生关系和风险顾虑如何改变帮助方式。
I wouldn't confidently say people care less now. In busy
places, they may feel unsure about a stranger's request or
worry about becoming involved in something they don't
understand. That can look like unwillingness. People
may still help in lower-risk ways, such as giving
directions or calling the appropriate service, rather than
stepping in directly.
我不能确定现在的人更不关心别人。在繁忙场所，人们可能
不确定陌生人的请求是否可靠，或怕卷入不了解的事情，看
起来像不愿帮忙。但他们仍可能指路、联系合适的服务，用
风险较低的方式提供帮助，而不直接介入。
step in 介入并提供帮助

sections.title: 给别人建议
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
朋友、聚会与互相帮助
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
83
话题 65
PART 2
给别人建议
Advice I gave to someone
Describe an occasion when you offered advice to another person.
描述一次你给别人建议的经历。
1. When you gave the advice
什么时候给的建议
2. Who you advised
给谁提建议
3. What you suggested
建议的具体内容
4. Why you decided to offer this advice
为什么要给这项建议
审题与选材：建议题需要交代你为什么有资格提出这个办法，不必把自己写成专家。先听对方遇到的具体困难，再给一两条
可执行的改变，并说明为什么适合他的情况。结果可以简短补充，但不能代替解释当时给建议的动机。
叙述顺序
A 交代表弟开学后询问通勤安排 - B 说明每天赶车影响早课精神 - C 提出前晚整理与固定出门时间 - D 解释建议来自自己
的迟到经历 - E 补充尝试后的实际变化
A Introduce my cousin asking about his commute - B Explain how rushed mornings affected early classes - C Suggest
evening preparation and a fixed departure - D Connect my advice with my own earlier mistakes - E Describe the practical
changes after he tried it
示例回答
I gave my cousin some practical advice shortly after he started college last September. He was living at home
and taking a bus to campus, but he kept arriving at his first class feeling rushed and tired. We talked about it
over dinner one evening. At first, he said the buses were the problem. When I asked him to describe a normal
morning, though, it turned out that he often spent ten minutes looking for his student card or deciding what to
pack. I suggested putting everything he needed into his bag the night before, including his card and a water
bottle. I also advised him to choose a fixed time to leave home rather than waiting until he felt ready. We
checked the timetable together and picked a bus that would give him a small margin if traffic was slow. I offered
those suggestions because I'd made almost exactly the same mistakes during my first term. I knew that simply
saying 'get up earlier' wouldn't solve all the little delays. A week later, he told me the new routine was helping.
He still didn't enjoy early mornings, but he wasn't starting every day in a panic. I was glad the advice was useful,
especially because it involved small changes he could actually keep doing.
中文对照：去年九月，表弟刚上大学不久，我给过他一些实用建议。他住在家里，坐公交去学校，但第一节课常常赶得很
急，又很累。一天晚饭时我们聊起来。一开始，他觉得早晨的麻烦都是公交车造成的。于是我请他从头描述一个普通早晨
是怎样度过的，才发现他经常花十分钟找学生卡或决定带什么。我建议前一晚把需要的东西放进包里，包括学生卡和水瓶；
还建议固定出门时间，不要等自己觉得都准备好了才走。我们一起查时刻表，选了一班能给堵车留点余地的车。我这样建
议，是因为自己大一时也犯过几乎一样的错，知道单说早点起床，解决不了所有小耽搁。一周后，他说新习惯有用。虽然
还是不喜欢早起，但不再每天一开始就慌张。我很高兴，因为这些是他真的能持续做的小改变。
自然表达
a fixed time
固定时间
the night before
前一天晚上
a small margin
一点余地
in a panic
慌慌张张
串题 话题 64 帮助他人的时刻
同一次通勤建议也帮助表弟解决早晨慌乱，可保留前晚收包和提前出门，补清自己怎样确认问题及一周后的改善和感受。
Those small changes helped him solve the morning problem that had been making his first classes so stressful.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
84
话题 65  /  给别人建议
PART 3
1. Should someone prepare before offering advice?
给别人建议前应该做准备吗？ 说明准备先是了解情况，再是
核实信息，按影响大小决定谨慎程度。
Yes, especially if the decision could seriously affect
someone's money, work or relationships. Preparation
starts with understanding the person's circumstances, not
just collecting impressive information. Asking what
they've already tried can prevent useless suggestions. For
a small everyday problem, preparation may take only a
few questions, but confident advice based on guesses can
easily mislead.
应该，尤其是会明显影响金钱、工作或关系的决定。准备首
先是了解对方处境，而不只是收集显得专业的信息。问清已
经试过什么，能避免无用建议。小问题可能只需问几句，但
仅凭猜测就自信给建议，很容易误导。
based on guesses 基于猜测
2. Is seeking advice from strangers on the internet a
good idea?
向网上的陌生人寻求建议好吗？ 区分收集经验与依赖结论，
指出匿名信息缺少背景时怎样看待。
It can be useful for gathering experiences you wouldn't
hear from your immediate circle. Someone may describe
a practical problem with a course or product before you
choose it. But strangers don't know your full
circumstances, and their expertise may be unclear. I'd
treat their advice as a starting point to check, rather than
a final decision.
这有助于听到身边人没有的经历。例如，选择课程或产品前，
别人可能说明实际遇到的问题。不过陌生人不了解你的全部
情况，专业程度也未必清楚。我会把建议当成需要核实的起
点，而不是直接当最终决定。
a starting point 起点；初步参考
3. What personality traits suit people who advise
others professionally?
以提供建议为工作的人适合具备哪些性格特点？ 将耐心和不
急于判断联系到听清问题，补充承认不确定的重要性。
They need patience, curiosity and the ability to stay calm
when someone is anxious. A good adviser listens before
deciding what the problem is and can explain options
without sounding superior. Being comfortable admitting
uncertainty matters too. People may trust an honest limit
more than a confident answer that later turns out to be
wrong.
他们需要耐心、好奇心，也要能在别人焦虑时保持平静。好
的顾问会先听，再判断问题，并能解释选择而不摆出高人一
等的姿态。愿意承认不确定也重要。人们可能更信任坦诚说
明局限，而非后来证明错误的自信回答。
admit uncertainty 承认不确定
4. What difficulties can come from asking too many
people for advice?
向太多人征求建议可能带来什么问题？ 解释意见冲突为什么
增加犹豫，再说明应按经验相关性筛选。
Too many opinions can make a decision feel more
complicated instead of clearer. Different people may
assume different priorities, so their recommendations
pull in opposite directions. Someone choosing a job
might hear advice based on salary, location or prestige. It
helps to decide what matters personally and ask a few
people with relevant experience.
意见太多可能让决定更复杂，而不是更清楚。不同人默认的
优先事项不同，建议就会相互冲突。选工作的人可能听到分
别看工资、地点或名望的建议。先弄清自己看重什么，再问
几位有相关经验的人，会更有帮助。
pull in opposite directions 指向相反的方向
5. Why might someone prefer advice from friends to
advice from parents?
为什么有人更愿听朋友的建议，而不是父母的？ 用共同处境
和担心被评判解释偏好，同时承认父母经验有适用范围。
Friends may understand the immediate situation better,
especially when they share the same school or
workplace. People can also feel less worried about
disappointing them. Parents may bring useful
experience, but their advice sometimes reflects different
conditions or priorities. The best source depends on the
question, rather than one group always understanding
everything more accurately.
朋友可能更了解眼前处境，尤其同校或同单位时。人们也可
能较少担心让朋友失望。父母有有用的经验，但建议有时反
映的是不同条件或优先考虑。向谁请教最好，取决于问题，
而不是哪一群人永远懂得更多。
the immediate situation 眼前的具体处境
6. When might older adults ask younger people for
advice?
年长者什么时候可能向年轻人请教？ 选择年轻人近期熟悉的
事，说明请教来自经验差别而非能力高低。
They might ask about unfamiliar digital tools, newer
courses or services younger people use regularly. For
example, someone booking through an app for the first
time may ask a younger relative to explain the steps. It
isn't simply about age or intelligence. People turn to
whoever has recent, relevant experience with the
particular task.
他们可能请教陌生数字工具、新课程，或年轻人经常使用的
服务。例如第一次用应用预约的人，会请年轻亲属解释步骤。
这不只是年龄或智力的问题。谁对具体任务有近期、相关经
验，谁就可能提供有用建议。
relevant experience 相关经验

sections.title: 一个比你年长且让你佩服的人
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
85
话题 66
PART 2
一个比你年长且让你佩服的人
An older person I admire
Describe a person older than you for whom you have great admiration.
描述一位比你年长、你很佩服的人。
1. Who this person is
这个人是谁
2. What this person does
从事什么工作或活动
3. What their personality is like
性格怎样
4. Why you admire them so much
你为什么特别佩服对方
审题与选材：人物题中年龄只是条件，佩服的理由需要具体行为来支撑。可以从熟悉的家人切入，用一次处理困难的经历呈
现耐心、认真等特点。先说职业再讲做法，最后解释这些做法为什么超出你的预期，不要把年长本身当成佩服理由。
叙述顺序
A 介绍比自己年长的裁缝阿姨 - B 说明她经营小店修补衣服 - C 用婚礼前改衣展示耐心负责 - D 描述她教我拆线处理失误
- E 解释佩服她认真而不急躁
A Introduce my aunt and her small tailoring shop - B Describe the clothes she repairs for customers - C Recall her patience
with an urgent wedding alteration - D Show how she taught me to undo mistakes - E Explain my admiration for her steady
approach
示例回答
Someone older than me whom I really admire is my aunt Lan. She's in her late fifties and runs a small clothing
repair shop near the market. People bring her trousers to shorten, jackets with broken zips and clothes they can't
quite bear to throw away. She's calm and practical, but she also has a very dry sense of humour. I've spent
afternoons helping her sort buttons and thread, so I've seen how she deals with customers when things get
stressful. Once, a woman arrived in tears because the dress she planned to wear to her son's wedding wouldn't
fasten properly. The wedding was the next morning. My aunt didn't promise a miracle. She examined the seams,
explained what she could change and asked the woman to return later. Then she worked carefully through the
afternoon until the dress fitted comfortably. I admire that combination of kindness and honesty. She wants to
help, but she doesn't give people unrealistic expectations. She's patient with beginners too. When I once made a
messy repair, she showed me how to undo the stitches instead of taking the work away from me. Being around
her makes difficult tasks feel manageable. I hope I can develop the same habit of looking closely at a problem
before getting upset about it.
中文对照：有一位比我年长、我确实特别佩服的人，就是兰阿姨。她五十多岁，在市场附近开小改衣店。顾客拿来要改短
的裤子、拉链坏了的外套，以及舍不得扔的衣服。她性格冷静，也很务实，也有一本正经讲笑话的幽默。我有好几次下午
帮她整理纽扣和缝衣线，见过她如何应对忙乱。有一次，一位女士哭着进来，因为准备参加儿子婚礼的那条裙子怎么也没
法好好扣上，而婚礼就在第二天早晨。阿姨没有保证奇迹，而是检查缝线，解释能改哪里，请她晚些回来，然后认真做了
一下午，直到裙子合身。我佩服她既善良又诚实：想帮人，却不制造不切实际的期待。她对初学者也耐心。有次我缝得乱，
她教我拆线重做，而不是把活拿走。待在她身边，难事也显得可以解决。我希望学会像她一样，先仔细看问题，再决定要
不要着急。
自然表达
bear to throw something away
舍得把某物扔掉
a dry sense of humour
一本正经的幽默感
unrealistic expectations
不切实际的期待
undo the stitches
拆开缝线
串题 话题 67 为家人感到骄傲
阿姨是家人，可保留婚礼前改裙子的事件，转题时明确自己在哪一刻感到骄傲，以及为何她的耐心负责特别触动自己。
I felt especially proud of my aunt when I saw how calmly she handled that customer's urgent problem.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
86
话题 66  /  一个比你年长且让你佩服的人
PART 3
1. What can younger people learn from older
generations?
年轻人可以向老一辈学习什么？ 选需要长期实践的经验，并
说明听懂适用条件比照搬做法重要。
Older people can pass on practical skills and the
experience of handling setbacks over time. They may
explain how they managed a household budget or
repaired something instead of replacing it. The useful
part isn't simply copying every old method. Young
people can ask why it worked and decide whether the
same conditions still apply.
年长者可以传授实用技能，以及长期应对挫折的经验。例如
怎样安排家庭开支，或修好东西而不是换新。有用的地方并
不是照搬每个旧方法。年轻人可以问清当时为何有效，再判
断同样的条件现在是否仍成立。
handle setbacks 应对挫折
2. What might older people learn from younger
generations?
年长者可以向年轻一代学习什么？ 把科技操作和新视角分开
举例，强调耐心交流而非单向教导。
Younger people may introduce unfamiliar technology,
new ways of studying or different views about work and
relationships. For instance, they can show an older
relative how to compare travel options online. Learning
works best when neither side feels embarrassed. A
patient explanation and a chance to try something
independently are more useful than doing everything for
them.
年轻人可能带来陌生技术、新学习方法，以及对工作和关系
的不同看法。例如教年长亲属在网上比较出行方案。双方都
不觉得难堪时，学习更顺利。耐心解释并让对方独自尝试，
比全部代办更有帮助。
try something independently 独自尝试某事
3. Is there a large gap between generations today?
现在年轻人与年长者之间的代沟大吗？ 说明差异常来自成长
条件，补充共同需要和实际交流能缩小隔阂。
There can be noticeable differences, especially in
communication habits and expectations about careers.
People who grew up under different conditions may
disagree about what counts as a secure future. Still, that
doesn't mean they have nothing in common. Spending
time on an actual problem together often reveals shared
concerns that broad arguments about generations hide.
差异可能很明显，尤其在交流习惯和职业期待上。成长条件
不同的人，对什么算安稳未来可能意见不同。但这不表示彼
此毫无共同点。一起处理实际问题，常能发现共同关心的事，
而笼统争论代际差别会把它们遮住。
have something in common 有共同之处
4. What part do older adults play in a traditional
family?
年长者在传统家庭里通常扮演什么角色？ 列出照顾和传承的
实际工作，同时承认长者自己也有生活需要。
They often help care for grandchildren, keep family
stories alive and organise important gatherings. Some
also offer financial or practical support when younger
relatives are starting out. Those contributions can be
substantial, but they shouldn't be treated as automatic
duties. Older family members have their own interests
and may need support themselves at different times.
他们常帮忙照顾孙辈、讲述家族故事、安排重要聚会。有些
也在年轻亲属起步时提供经济或实际支持。这些贡献很大，
但不应被当成理所当然的义务。年长家人也有自己的兴趣，
不同时期也可能需要照顾。
keep family stories alive 让家族故事继续被记住
5. How have older people's roles or status changed
over time?
与过去相比，老年人的地位或角色怎样变了？ 比较共同居住
与分开居住带来的变化，避免把权威减少等同不受尊重。
In some families, older people no longer make all the
major decisions as younger adults live separately and
manage their own households. Their role may shift
towards advice and emotional support. At the same time,
many still provide childcare. Less authority doesn't
necessarily mean less respect; families can value an
older person's contribution without expecting complete
obedience.
有些家庭中，年轻人分开居住、独立持家，长者不再决定所
有大事，角色可能转向建议和情感支持。同时，许多人仍在
帮忙带孩子。权威减少不一定表示不受尊重，家庭可以重视
长者贡献，而不要求完全服从。
manage their own households 独立管理自己的家庭生活

sections.title: 为家人感到骄傲
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
87
话题 67
PART 2
为家人感到骄傲
Feeling proud of a relative
Describe an occasion when something a family member did made you feel proud.
描述一次家人的行为让你感到骄傲的经历。
1. When this happened
发生在什么时候
2. Which family member it was
是哪位家人
3. What the person did
对方做了什么
4. Why it made you feel proud
为什么让你感到骄傲
审题与选材：这题要聚焦一个时刻，不能整篇都在介绍家人优秀。先交代对方原本的困难，再挑能看到努力的准备过程，最
后写你亲眼见到的结果。骄傲的理由应与这份努力对应，不一定依靠奖项、名次或特别大的成就。
叙述顺序
A 交代父亲去年参加社区朗读活动 - B 说明他一向害怕当众讲话 - C 描述每天在厨房练习的过程 - D 讲述上台停顿后继续
读完 - E 解释为何比获奖更让我骄傲
A Introduce my father's reading at a community event - B Explain his long-standing fear of public speaking - C Describe
his daily practice in our kitchen - D Recall how he continued reading after pausing - E Connect my pride with his personal
effort
示例回答
I felt proud of my father last November, when he read a short piece at our community centre's storytelling
evening. It wasn't a competition. What mattered was that he'd always been uncomfortable speaking in front of a
group. He'd written about the small grocery shop his parents used to run. When the organiser invited him to read
it aloud, his first reaction was to refuse. A few days later, though, he decided to give it a try. For two weeks, I
heard him practising in the kitchen after dinner. He marked places to pause on the page and asked me whether
he was speaking too quickly. Once, he lost his place and became frustrated, but the following evening he was
back at the table. At the event, his hands were shaking slightly as he held the paper. Halfway through, he
stopped for a moment. I thought he might leave the stage, but he took a breath, found the next line and
continued. By the end, people were smiling at his description of my grandfather giving children extra sweets. I
was proud because I knew how much effort that ordinary-looking reading had required. Afterwards, my father
said he was glad he'd done it. His relieved smile meant far more to me than any certificate could have.
中文对照：去年十一月，爸爸在社区中心的故事分享晚会上朗读自己的短文，我特别为他骄傲。那不是比赛，关键是他一
直不敢当众讲话。他写了一篇短文，内容是祖父母以前经营的那家小杂货店。组织者请他读出来时，他起初拒绝了，几天
后却决定试试。接下来的整整两周，我都会听见他晚饭后在厨房练习朗读。他在纸上标停顿，还问我是不是读太快。有一
次练习时，他忽然找不到自己读到了哪里，他很沮丧，但第二晚又坐回桌边。活动时，他拿纸的手有点抖。读到一半停了
下来，我以为他要下台，他却吸一口气，找到下一行继续。结尾讲到爷爷多给孩子糖，在场的听众都露出了笑容。我骄傲，
是因为知道这场看似普通的朗读花了他多少努力。事后爸爸说很庆幸自己做了。他释然的笑容，对我比任何证书都更有意
义。
自然表达
give something a try
试一试
lose one's place
读到或做到一半忘记位置
take a breath
吸一口气
in front of a group
在一群人面前
串题 话题 75 做困难事情并成功的人
可沿用父亲完成朗读的经历，改讲克服困难而成功的人时，多解释他怕什么、怎样练习与坚持，再用读完全篇说明结果。
For my father, finishing that short reading successfully meant overcoming a fear he had carried for years.

话题 67  /  为家人感到骄傲
PART 3
1. What kinds of moments make parents proud of
their children?
哪些时候父母会为孩子感到骄傲？ 不只提成绩，用独立处理
问题和关心别人体现成长的多种表现。
Parents may feel proud when children achieve something
difficult, but also when they show kindness or
independence. A child who admits a mistake and tries to
repair it can give parents real satisfaction. These
moments suggest growth in character, not just
performance. Different parents notice different things,
depending on what they value and what their child finds
challenging.
孩子完成困难任务时，父母可能骄傲；表现出善意或独立时
也一样。孩子承认错误并设法弥补，能让父母很欣慰。这些
时刻体现的是品格成长，不只是表现。父母重视什么、孩子
觉得什么难，会影响他们看重的进步。
admit a mistake 承认错误
2. Should parents give their children rewards very
frequently, and why?
父母应该很频繁地奖励孩子吗？为什么？ 把具体鼓励与频繁
物质奖励分开，解释孩子为何可能开始只看奖品。
I don't think every useful action needs a prize. If rewards
become automatic, children may start asking what they'll
receive before helping or practising. Parents can still
notice effort and give specific encouragement. Saving
material rewards for occasional milestones makes them
feel meaningful, while everyday appreciation helps
children understand exactly what they did well.
我觉得不必每个有用行为都给奖品。如果奖励成了惯例，孩
子可能帮忙或练习前先问能得到什么。父母仍可关注努力、
具体鼓励。物质奖励留给偶尔的重要进步，才更有意义；日
常肯定则让孩子知道自己哪里做得好。
specific encouragement 具体的鼓励
3. Is rewarding children too often beneficial, and
why?
过于频繁地奖励孩子有益吗？为什么？ 从奖励效果讨论，而
非重复父母该不该，指出注意力可能转向比较。
Frequent rewards can lose their impact, particularly if
each one has to be bigger than the last. Children may
focus on comparing prizes rather than enjoying the
activity or noticing their improvement. That doesn't
make all rewards harmful. A small, well-timed
celebration can encourage persistence when it recognises
a real effort the child has made.
奖励太频繁可能失去效果，尤其每次都得比上次更大时。孩
子可能只比较奖品，而不享受活动或注意自己的进步。这不
表示所有奖励都有害。适时的小庆祝若肯定了孩子真实的努
力，也能鼓励坚持。
lose their impact 失去原本的效果
4. When might adults feel proud of their own
achievements?
成年人在哪些时候会为自己感到骄傲？ 从自己曾经做不到的
事解释成就感，避免只把升职收入当成功。
Adults often feel proud when they manage something
they once found difficult, whether that's finishing a
course, handling a demanding project or becoming more
independent. The achievement doesn't need public
recognition. Someone who finally learns to swim may
feel enormous satisfaction because they know the fear
and effort involved, even if nobody else considers it
remarkable.
成年人完成以前觉得困难的事，常会感到骄傲，比如修完课
程、处理棘手项目或变得更独立。成就不必得到公众认可。
终于学会游泳的人可能非常满足，因为清楚其中的害怕和努
力，即使别人不觉得特别了不起。
public recognition 公众认可
5. Can rewards help children improve?
奖励能帮助孩子进步吗？ 说明奖励何时能鼓励重复好行为，
同时补上反馈比奖品更能指路。
They can, if the reward clearly connects with a useful
behaviour the child can repeat. Recognising steady
practice may encourage more effort than rewarding only
the highest result. But a prize alone doesn't explain how
to improve. Children also need practical feedback,
chances to try again and some freedom to enjoy the
activity for its own sake.
能，前提是奖励明确对应孩子可以重复的有益行为。肯定持
续练习，可能比只奖励最高成绩更能鼓励努力。但奖品本身
不会说明如何进步。孩子还需要实际反馈、重试机会，以及
为活动本身的乐趣参与的空间。
steady practice 持续稳定的练习
6. How do you view children studying hard only to
get good grades?
你怎么看孩子只为好成绩而努力学习？ 承认分数提供目标，
但用学完就忘的例子说明动机过窄的问题。
Grades can give children a clear short-term goal, so I
understand why they matter. The problem comes when
marks become the only reason to learn. A student may
memorise an answer and forget it immediately after the
test. Connecting lessons with real questions can help
children see value in knowledge beyond the number on a
report.
分数能给孩子明确的短期目标，所以我理解它的重要性。问
题在于分数成了学习的唯一理由。学生可能背下答案，考完
马上忘记。把课堂内容和真实问题联系起来，能让孩子看到
成绩单数字以外的知识价值。
a short-term goal 短期目标

sections.text:

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
89
话题 68
PART 2
一个很开心的人
A happy person I know
Describe someone you know who seems to be a happy person.
描述一位你认识、生活中很开心的人。
1. Who the person is
这个人是谁
2. Their noticeable qualities
有哪些明显的性格特点
3. Why you think they are so happy
你认为对方为什么这么开心
4. How you feel about this person
你对这个人的感觉
审题与选材：开心的人也会有不顺，写他怎样面对小麻烦反而更有说服力。先介绍关系，再选择日常习惯和一次受挫后的反
应，解释快乐的来源。避免仅靠笑得多来判断，也不要替对方断言从无烦恼；感受应来自你与他的真实互动。
叙述顺序
A 介绍周末常见面的表姐小宁 - B 描述她注意日常小乐趣的习惯 - C 讲述野餐被雨打断的反应 - D 说明人际联系与爱好带
来快乐 - E 解释与她相处为何感觉轻松
A Introduce my cousin Ning and our weekend visits - B Describe her habit of noticing small pleasures - C Recall her
response when rain interrupted our picnic - D Connect her happiness with hobbies and close relationships - E Explain why
her company helps me relax
示例回答
My cousin Ning is one of the happiest people I know. She's a few years older than me and works in a small
bookshop. We meet at weekends, sometimes for a walk and something cheap to eat. She's curious, easy to talk to
and very good at noticing small pleasures. She'll stop to show me a strangely shaped cloud or tell me about a
customer who finally found a book they'd been searching for. None of these stories is dramatic, but she tells
them with real enjoyment. Her happiness doesn't disappear the moment something goes wrong. We once
planned a picnic, and it started raining just as we reached the park. I was annoyed because we'd carried
everything there. Ning suggested taking our food back to her flat and spreading the picnic blanket on the living
room floor. We ended up eating sandwiches beside her sofa and laughing at our muddy shoes. I don't think she
has a perfect life. She gets tired and worries about money like anyone else. But she makes time for people she
likes and keeps a few inexpensive hobbies going. Being around her makes me feel less rushed. She reminds me
to notice what's enjoyable in an ordinary afternoon, rather than constantly waiting for a bigger event.
中文对照：表姐小宁是我认识的人中很开心的一位。她比我大几岁，在小书店工作。我们通常周末见面，有时只散散步、
吃点便宜的东西。她好奇、好聊，也善于发现小乐趣：会停下来给我看形状奇怪的云，或讲某位顾客终于找到一直寻觅的
书。事情不惊人，她讲这些事情的时候，却能让人听出真实的快乐。我最喜欢的是，事情不顺时她的快乐不会立即消失。
有次刚到公园准备野餐就下雨了，我想到费了劲把所有东西带来这里，就觉得很恼火。她建议回家，把野餐垫铺在客厅地
上。结果我们坐在沙发旁吃三明治，对着沾泥的鞋子发笑。我不觉得她生活完美，她也累，也为钱担心。但她会留时间给
喜欢的人，并保持几个便宜的爱好。和她待在一起时，我觉得自己不再那么匆忙，提醒我发现普通下午的乐趣，而不是一
直等更大的事情。
自然表达
notice small pleasures
留意生活中的小乐趣
make time for someone
留出时间陪伴某人
end up doing something
最后做了某事
feel less rushed
感觉不那么匆忙
串题 话题 69 一个受欢迎的人
可保留表姐的幽默和把雨天变野餐的做法；受欢迎题还需补上其他人的真实反应，说明大家为何主动约她相处和活动。
Her ability to make an ordinary afternoon enjoyable is also one reason people like spending time with her.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
90
话题 68  /  一个很开心的人
PART 3
1. Do you often mention this person in conversation?
你经常在聊天时提到这个人吗？ 承接前面人物，用谈什么时
会提她说明频率，不必夸成人人都认识。
I mention Ning occasionally, usually when someone is
feeling disappointed about a plan going wrong. Her
indoor picnic idea is an example I like because it's
practical rather than preachy. I don't describe her as
someone who's cheerful every minute. What I talk about
is her ability to find another enjoyable option when
circumstances change.
我偶尔会提小宁，通常是有人因计划出问题而失望时。我喜
欢讲她的室内野餐主意，因为实际又不说教。我不会说她每
分钟都快乐，而是会说她怎样在情况改变后找到另一种能享
受的选择。
an enjoyable option 让人愉快的另一种选择
2. What helps students feel happy at school?
哪些事情会让学生在学校开心？ 把朋友归属和能看见的进步
分别说明，强调安全参与比奖项更基础。
Having friends and feeling accepted are major parts of it.
Students also enjoy seeing themselves improve at
something, whether it's reading, sport or a practical
project. Small classroom routines matter too. When
children can ask questions without being laughed at,
school feels safer, and they have more energy to enjoy
learning and spending time together.
有朋友、感到被接纳，是重要原因。学生也喜欢看到自己在
阅读、运动或实践项目上进步。课堂的小习惯同样重要。能
提问而不被嘲笑时，学校更让人安心，他们也有更多精力享
受学习和共同相处。
feel accepted 感到被接纳
3. What about students who put in effort but still get
poor results?
那些很努力却仍然成绩不好的学生怎么办？ 先回应挫败感，
再从具体错误和学习方法解释怎样获得有用帮助。
They need support that recognises their effort without
pretending the difficulty isn't real. A teacher can look at
specific mistakes and check whether the study method
suits the task. More hours aren't always the answer.
Setting a smaller goal, such as understanding one type of
problem, can make progress visible and reduce the
feeling of failure.
他们需要努力被看见，也需要困难被认真对待。教师可以看
具体错误，检查方法是否适合任务。增加时间并不总是答案。
把目标缩小，例如先弄懂一类题，能让进步看得见，也减少
总觉得失败的感受。
make progress visible 让进步看得见
4. Is it more important to enjoy your job?
喜欢自己的工作更重要吗？ 在题目比较对象不明确时说明重
要程度，结合收入与工作条件作限定。
Enjoying your work is very important because it
occupies so much of the week. Interest can make
difficult tasks feel worthwhile and encourage learning.
Still, it isn't the only consideration. A job also needs to
provide acceptable pay and conditions. Liking the work
won't fully compensate for constant exhaustion or an
employer who treats people badly.
喜欢工作很重要，因为它占据一周很多时间。兴趣能让困难
任务显得值得，也鼓励学习。但这不是唯一因素，收入和条
件也要可以接受。即使喜欢内容，也无法完全抵消长期疲惫
或雇主对人的恶劣态度。
feel worthwhile 觉得值得投入
5. Do people who dislike their work feel that their
time is being wasted?
不喜欢工作的人会觉得自己在浪费时间吗？ 承认部分人的浪
费感，同时用养家和为未来作准备解释不同看法。
Some do, particularly when they can see no purpose or
future in what they're doing. Others view an unenjoyable
job as a practical way to support their family or prepare
for another opportunity. The feeling depends partly on
having a reason to continue. Disliking daily tasks doesn't
automatically mean believing the whole period of work
is worthless.
有些人会，尤其看不到所做事情的意义或前景时。另一些人
把不喜欢的工作看作养家或准备下一次机会的实际办法。感
受部分取决于有没有继续的理由。不喜欢日常任务，并不自
动等于认为整段工作时间毫无价值。
a reason to continue 继续下去的理由

sections.title: 一个受欢迎的人
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
91
话题 69
PART 2
一个受欢迎的人
A popular person
Describe someone who is liked by a great many people.
描述一位很受大家欢迎的人。
1. Who this person is
这个人是谁
2. What the person does
平时做什么
3. How you feel about their popularity
你怎样看待对方受欢迎这件事
4. Why you believe they are so popular
你认为对方为什么这么受欢迎
审题与选材：受欢迎需要别人对他的反应作证据，不能只说自己喜欢他。可以选熟悉的小圈子人物，用招呼新人、记住需要
等行动解释大家愿意接近他的原因。你的感受应明确回应他的受欢迎是否合理，再用亲眼见过的细节支撑。
叙述顺序
A 介绍社区羽毛球组织者阿明 - B 说明他安排场地并照顾新手 - C 描述新人不敢加入时他的做法 - D 用大家主动报名体现
受欢迎 - E 解释自己认为这份欢迎有道理
A Introduce Ming who organises our badminton group - B Describe his bookings and support for beginners - C Recall how
he included a nervous newcomer - D Show popularity through the willingness of people to return - E Explain why I think he
deserves it
示例回答
A popular person in my neighbourhood is Ming, who organises our Sunday badminton sessions. He works in an
office during the week, so this is simply something he does in his spare time. About a dozen people usually join
us at the local sports hall. Ming handles the bookings and brings spare rackets, but that isn't the main reason
people like him. He's very good at making newcomers feel included. He remembers names and notices when
someone has been waiting too long for a game. I remember a woman who joined us for the first time and kept
saying she wasn't good enough to play. Ming paired up with her, showed her how to serve and made a joke
about his own terrible first lesson. Within twenty minutes, she was playing quite happily. He didn't make a big
performance of helping her; he just treated her as part of the group. People respond to that. They volunteer to
help him book courts, invite their friends and keep coming back even when the weather is miserable. I think his
popularity is deserved. He isn't the loudest person in the room or our strongest player. He simply makes the
activity easier and more pleasant for everyone else, which gives people a good reason to enjoy his company.
中文对照：我们社区很受欢迎的人是阿明，他组织周日羽毛球活动。平时他在办公室工作，组织活动其实只是他利用业余
时间做的事情。一般有十来个人到附近体育馆参加。他会负责处理场地预约，并且带来备用的羽毛球拍，但大家喜欢他，
主要不是因为这些。他很会让新人融入：记住名字，也会注意谁等了太久没打上。有位女士第一次来，一直说自己打得太
差。阿明和她组队，教她发球，还拿自己第一次上课的糟糕表现开玩笑。二十分钟后，她就打得挺开心。他没把帮助她当
成表演，只把她当作团队一员。大家也回应这种体贴：自愿帮忙替他预订球场，带朋友来，天气很差仍会参加。我觉得他
受欢迎很有道理。他不是最吵闹的人，也不是最强的选手，只是让大家的活动更容易、更愉快，所以人们愿意和他相处。
自然表达
in one's spare time
在业余时间
feel included
感到被接纳、能融入
pair up with someone
与某人搭档
enjoy someone's company
喜欢与某人相处
串题 话题 68 一个很开心的人
阿明让新人自在的做法可以保留；若转开心的人，还需讲他的日常快乐来源或面对不顺的反应，不能只用别人喜欢证明。
Alongside making others feel welcome, he seems to get a lot of enjoyment from these ordinary Sunday games.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
92
话题 69  /  一个受欢迎的人
PART 3
1. Which types of children tend to be popular at
school?
什么样的孩子在学校通常受欢迎？ 区分吸引注意与让人愿意
长期相处，用共同活动中的行为说明。
Children who are friendly, confident or good at a shared
activity often attract attention. But lasting popularity
may depend more on how they treat others. A pupil who
includes classmates in games and doesn't make people
feel foolish can be easy to like. Being loud or talented
doesn't guarantee that other children feel comfortable
around you.
友好、自信，或擅长大家一起做的活动的孩子，常会吸引注
意。但长久受欢迎可能更取决于怎样待人。愿意邀请同学玩、
不让别人难堪的学生很容易招人喜欢。嗓门大或有才华，并
不保证其他孩子相处时自在。
lasting popularity 长久的受欢迎程度
2. Should well-liked children help their classmates?
受欢迎的孩子应该帮助其他同学吗？ 说明人人有责任，再指
出受欢迎者一句邀请可能改变群体行为。
Yes, although helping others is a responsibility for all
children, not only popular ones. Well-liked pupils may
have extra influence over what the group considers
acceptable. If they invite a lonely classmate into a game,
others may follow their example. Teachers should
support that behaviour without turning one child into an
unpaid classroom assistant.
应该，不过帮助别人是所有孩子的责任，不只属于受欢迎者。
受欢迎的学生可能更能影响群体接受什么行为。如果他们邀
请孤单同学一起玩，别人也可能效仿。教师应支持这种行为，
但不把某个孩子变成无偿助教。
follow someone's example 效仿某人的做法
3. Why might people described as introverted or
unpopular in childhood, such as Elon Musk, achieve
success later?
为什么像埃隆·马斯克这样被描述为童年内向或不受欢迎的
人，后来也可能成功？ 不替名人确认童年细节，转向人气与
成年任务要求并不相同的解释。
I can't judge the childhood of a particular public figure,
but school popularity isn't the same as adult ability.
Someone quiet may spend time developing a strong
interest or learning independently. Later, those skills
may suit a particular job. Success also depends on
opportunity, support and persistence, so childhood social
status doesn't reliably predict a person's future.
我无法判断某位公众人物的童年，但学校里的人气并不等于
成年后的能力。安静的人可能投入兴趣或独立学习，这些技
能后来也许适合某份工作。成功还取决于机会、支持和坚持，
因此童年的社交地位不能可靠预测未来。
learn independently 独立学习
4. Is it beneficial to be popular among colleagues?
在公司里受同事欢迎是好事吗？ 说明同事间信任便于合作，
同时区分真正可靠与只想讨好大家。
It can make cooperation easier because colleagues are
more comfortable asking questions and sharing
information with someone they like. That helps work
move along. But popularity is only useful if it's
supported by reliability and competence. An employee
who agrees with everyone but never finishes their tasks
may be pleasant company without being a helpful
teammate.
有好处，因为同事更自在地向喜欢的人提问和分享信息，工
作也更易推进。但受欢迎需要可靠和能力支撑才有用。员工
若总附和大家，却从不完成任务，也许相处愉快，但算不上
有帮助的队友。
move along 继续推进
5. Is it desirable for a manager to be popular?
经理受欢迎是好事吗？ 比较容易沟通的好处与必须作困难决
定的责任，重点放在公正。
A well-liked manager may find it easier to hear honest
feedback and keep a team motivated. Still, being liked
shouldn't become the main goal. Managers sometimes
need to make unpopular decisions, such as changing an
unrealistic deadline or addressing poor work. Fairness
and clear explanations matter more than keeping
everyone happy in the short term.
受欢迎的经理可能更容易听到真实反馈，也更能鼓舞团队。
但被喜欢不应成为主要目标。经理有时要作不受欢迎的决定，
例如调整不现实的期限或处理工作不到位的问题。公平和解
释清楚，比短期让所有人高兴更重要。
honest feedback 真实坦诚的反馈
6. What is your general view of popular people?
你总体上怎样看待受欢迎的人？ 不把人气当品质结论，说明
观察对象应是他们如何对待不显眼的人。
I don't automatically admire or distrust someone because
they're popular. I want to know what people appreciate
about them. Some are genuinely considerate, while
others are simply entertaining or highly visible. How
they treat someone who has little influence tells me more
than the size of their social circle or the attention they
receive.
我不会因为一个人受欢迎就自动佩服或怀疑他。我想知道大
家欣赏什么。有些人确实体贴，有些只是有趣或常被看见。
比起社交圈多大、获得多少注意，我更看重他怎样对待没有
什么影响力的人。
a social circle 社交圈

sections.title: 一个有条理的人
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
93
话题 70
PART 2
一个有条理的人
A well-organised person
Describe someone you know who manages things in an organised way.
描述一位你认识的做事很有条理的人。
1. Who this person is
这个人是谁
2. When you first got to know them
你何时认识对方
3. Why they need to be organised
为什么对方需要有条理
4. How you feel about this person
你对这个人的感觉
审题与选材：别把有条理只写成桌子整齐，要说明对方同时处理哪些事，因此需要安排。用一次变化出现时的反应展示安排
如何发挥作用。本例把清单、提前确认和留出余地放到活动现场，感受也由自己少慌乱这一结果来解释。
叙述顺序
A 交代大学社团认识负责人小雅 - B 说明课程与社团事务都要兼顾 - C 描述清单和提前确认的习惯 - D 展开教室临时关闭
后的安排 - E 解释自己佩服且愿意跟她合作
A Introduce Ya whom I met at university - B Explain her classes and club responsibilities - C Describe her lists and checks
before events - D Recall her response when our room became unavailable - E Explain why working with her feels
reassuring
示例回答
The most organised person I know is Ya, whom I met when I joined a university reading club three years ago.
She was responsible for arranging our fortnightly meetings while keeping up with her own coursework. She
didn't carry a complicated planner or colour-code every minute. Instead, she kept a short list of what needed
doing, who was doing it and when it should be finished. Before each meeting, she'd confirm the room booking
and send everyone the same clear message about the time and reading. Her organisation really showed one
afternoon when our usual classroom was unexpectedly closed for repairs. Several members had already arrived
and were standing outside looking confused. Ya checked the list of available rooms she'd saved earlier,
contacted the office and found another space nearby. Within ten minutes, she'd put a note on the old door and
guided everyone to the new room. She needed to be organised because the club involved many people whose
time could easily be wasted by one missing detail. I admire her because her preparation makes things calmer for
others, not just tidier for herself. Working with her also taught me that a useful plan should include room for
changes. I've started checking important arrangements the day before, rather than assuming everything will
work out.
中文对照：我认识最有条理的人是小雅。三年前加入大学读书会时认识她，她负责协调每两周一次的活动，同时还要完成
自己的课程。她不用复杂手账，也不把每分钟都标颜色，只列简短清单：要做什么、谁负责、何时完成。每次活动前，她
确认教室预约，再把时间和阅读内容清楚发给大家。有天下午，常用教室临时维修关闭，几位成员到了门外，不知怎么办。
她查看提前存好的空教室列表，联系办公室，在附近找到新场地。十分钟内，她就在原门上贴好说明，把大家带过去。她
需要有条理，因为读书会涉及很多人，一处遗漏就可能浪费大家时间。我佩服她，是因为准备让别人也更从容，不只是让
自己整齐。和她合作还让我明白，有用的计划要允许变化。我也开始提前一天检查重要安排，而不是默认一切自然会顺利。
自然表达
keep up with coursework
跟上课程作业进度
confirm a booking
确认预约
room for changes
调整的余地
the day before
前一天
串题 话题 63 在团队中工作
可沿用读书会临时换教室的合作场景，但团队题要补上自己负责什么、与谁配合及为何需要合作，不能只夸小雅安排周到。
Working with Ya on the reading club showed me how much a clear division of responsibilities can help.

身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
94
话题 70  /  一个有条理的人
PART 3
1. Why is being organised useful in everyday life?
在日常生活中，做事有条理为什么有用？ 用寻找物品和记住
约定说明节省的精力，再解释如何减少焦虑。
It reduces the effort spent remembering small details or
searching for things. If bills, appointments and important
documents have a clear place, people can focus on what
they actually need to do. Organisation can also reduce
last-minute stress. It doesn't require a perfect system; a
few reliable habits often prevent the most frustrating
everyday problems.
它能减少记小细节、找东西所耗的精力。账单、约定和重要
文件有明确位置，人们就能专心做真正需要做的事，也能减
少临时赶工的紧张。不必有完美系统，几个可靠习惯常就能
避免最烦人的日常问题。
last-minute stress 临到最后的紧张压力
2. Do children need to develop organisational skills?
孩子需要培养做事有条理的能力吗？ 把要求限制在适龄小任
务，说明独立感而不是整齐本身的重要性。
Yes, at a level that fits their age. A young child might
learn where toys belong, while an older child can prepare
a schoolbag using a short checklist. These routines help
them become more independent. Adults should leave
space for play and mistakes, though, rather than
expecting children to manage every minute like busy
professionals.
需要，但应符合年龄。小孩子可以学玩具放哪，大孩子可以
照着简短清单准备书包。这些习惯有助于独立。不过成人也
应留下玩耍和犯错的空间，而不是要求孩子像忙碌职业人士
一样管理每一分钟。
fit their age 适合他们的年龄
3. Should parents help children learn to be
organised?
父母应该教孩子做事有条理吗？ 说明示范和共同练习的作用，
提醒代收拾不能教会孩子独立操作。
Parents should, because home provides daily
opportunities to practise. They can show children how to
put things away or prepare for the next morning, then
gradually let them take responsibility. Doing all the
organising for a child won't teach much. Simple
instructions and consistent places for belongings are
usually more useful than repeated complaints about
mess.
应该，家庭每天都有练习机会。父母可以示范收东西、准备
第二天早晨，再逐渐让孩子负责。如果每次全替孩子安排，
孩子其实并不能从中学会多少东西。简单指示和固定的物品
位置，通常比反复抱怨凌乱更有效。
take responsibility 承担责任
4. Are organised children more likely to succeed
later?
有条理的孩子以后更容易成功吗？ 解释准备充分可能带来优
势，同时承认能力兴趣与机会也影响结果。
They may have an advantage because they are less likely
to forget materials or leave every task until the last
moment. That can make learning more consistent. But
organisation alone doesn't guarantee success. Curiosity,
confidence, support and opportunities matter too, and a
child who is currently messy can still learn better habits
as they grow.
他们可能有优势，因为不太容易忘带材料，或把每件事拖到
最后，学习因而更稳定。但有条理本身不保证成功。好奇心、
自信、支持和机会也重要；现在凌乱的孩子，长大过程中也
能学会更好的习惯。
have an advantage 具有优势

身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
95
话题 70  /  一个有条理的人
PART 3
5. How important is organisation for employees?
员工做事有条理有多重要？ 围绕交接和期限说明个人遗漏如
何影响同事，不只谈个人效率。
It's important because most jobs involve commitments to
other people. An employee who keeps track of deadlines
and files makes it easier for colleagues to continue the
work. Small omissions can cause avoidable delays. The
exact method can vary, but others should be able to
understand what has been done and what still needs
attention.
很重要，因为多数工作都涉及对别人的承诺。员工记清期限、
保存好文件，同事才容易接着做。小遗漏也会造成原本能避
免的延误。具体方法可以不同，但别人应能看懂什么完成了、
什么还需要处理。
keep track of deadlines 掌握并跟进截止时间
6. Do managers also need to be well organised?
经理也需要很有条理吗？ 把经理对多人的安排与员工个人任
务区分，强调检查负担和避免冲突。
Yes, and their organisation affects the whole team.
Managers need to coordinate priorities, notice when
someone has too much work and make sure different
tasks fit together. If they change instructions without
keeping track, employees may duplicate work or miss
something essential. Clear planning should make
responsibilities understandable while still allowing
adjustments when circumstances change.
需要，而且他们的安排影响整个团队。经理要协调轻重缓急，
留意谁负担过重，确保不同任务衔接。如果改指示却不记清，
员工可能重复劳动或遗漏要事。清晰计划应让责任易懂，同
时允许情况改变后的调整。
duplicate work 重复劳动
7. What practical steps can help someone become
more organised?
人们可以采取哪些实际方法让自己更有条理？ 从常见失误选
一个可持续习惯，避免同时引入复杂工具增加负担。
I'd start with one recurring problem rather than
redesigning an entire life. If someone keeps losing keys,
choosing one place for them is a useful first step. A short
daily list and a weekly check of upcoming commitments
can help too. The method needs to be easy enough to use
when you're tired, not just when you're motivated.
我会先选一个反复出现的问题，而不是重做整套生活安排。
总丢钥匙的人，可以先固定一个放置位置。每日短清单、每
周查看后续约定也有帮助。方法要简单到累了也能用，而不
只是在有动力时才做得到。
upcoming commitments 接下来已经约定的事情

sections.title: 拥有健康作息与习惯的人
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
96
话题 71
PART 2
拥有健康作息与习惯的人
A person with healthy routines
Describe someone you know who follows a regular routine and has healthy habits.
描述一位你认识、作息规律并有健康习惯的人。
1. Who this person is
这个人是谁
2. What a normal day looks like for them
日常作息怎样
3. The healthy habits they follow
有哪些健康习惯
4. Why you consider their way of life healthy
为什么你认为这种生活方式健康
审题与选材：作息题先给出一天的大致顺序，再把睡眠、饮食和活动穿插进去，不必报满二十四小时。评价健康时讲规律、
适量和可持续的观察，不凭外表判断，也别虚构医学效果。一个忙碌时怎样保持习惯的例子，能说明安排确实可行。
叙述顺序
A 介绍住在同栋楼的朋友小梅 - B 按早晨通勤工作交代日常作息 - C 说明午餐散步与晚间放松习惯 - D 描述加班后怎样适
当调整活动 - E 解释规律且不过度带来的感受
A Introduce Mei who lives in my building - B Outline her morning routine and working day - C Describe her meals, walks
and evening relaxation - D Show how she adjusts plans on busy days - E Explain why the routine seems balanced and
sustainable
示例回答
My friend Mei, who lives in the same building as me, has a routine I find sensible and healthy. She works
locally and usually gets up around seven, leaving enough time for breakfast before catching the bus. She
prepares lunch the evening before, usually something simple with rice, vegetables and an egg or some beans. At
lunchtime, she takes a short walk rather than remaining at her desk for the whole break. I've joined her a few
times, and we just walk around nearby streets and chat. In the evening, she cooks, deals with any small chores
and then leaves some time to read. She tries to go to bed at roughly the same time instead of staying up because
one more video has appeared on her phone. What I appreciate is that she isn't rigid about it. If work runs late, she
takes a shorter walk or has an easier dinner. She doesn't try to make up for a missed activity by exhausting
herself the next day. I think her lifestyle is healthy because it includes ordinary movement, varied meals and a
regular chance to rest. It also seems possible to maintain. When we're together, she usually looks comfortable
and alert, which makes her routine more appealing to me than an extreme fitness plan.
中文对照：和我住同一栋楼的朋友小梅，有一套在我看来既合理、又健康的日常作息。她在附近办公室工作，通常七点左
右起床，有时间吃早饭再坐公交。她在前晚准备午餐，一般是米饭、蔬菜，再加鸡蛋或豆类。午休时，她会出去走一小段，
不会整个休息都坐在桌前。我陪过几次，就是在附近街道边走边聊。晚上她做饭、处理小家务，再留点时间读书。她尽量
在大致固定的时间睡觉，而不是因为手机又推来视频就一直熬。让我欣赏的是她对这套安排并不死板。如果那天工作拖得
比较晚，就少走一会或把晚饭做简单些，不会为了补一次没做的活动，第二天把自己累坏。我觉得她健康，是因为有日常
活动、多样饭菜和固定休息机会，也确实能坚持。相处时她通常自在、精神清醒，这使她的生活安排比极端的健身计划更
能吸引我去尝试。

leave enough time for
为某事留足时间
stay up
熬夜；迟迟不睡
make up for
弥补
a regular chance to rest
固定的休息机会

小梅准备午餐与规律安排可用于有条理的人，补上何时认识、为何工作家务需要安排；重点转到准备步骤，不再主要评价健
康。
Her regular routine also shows how organised she is, especially in the way she prepares for the next day.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
97
话题 71  /  拥有健康作息与习惯的人
PART 3
1. How important are communities that encourage
healthy living?
鼓励健康生活的社区重要吗？ 把环境便利与个人选择联系，
说明场地和费用影响能否实际参加。
They're important because surroundings can make
everyday healthy choices easier or harder. Safe paths,
welcoming public spaces and affordable activities give
people practical opportunities to move and meet others.
A community doesn't need an expensive gym to help.
Even a well-maintained walking route can be useful if
residents feel comfortable using it regularly together.
重要，因为环境会让日常健康选择更容易或更难。安全道路、
友善的公共空间和负担得起的活动，让人有机会活动并见到
别人。社区不必靠昂贵健身房，维护良好的步道，只要居民
愿意经常一起使用，也很有用。
affordable activities 负担得起的活动
2. Can communities focused on health create a sense
of belonging?
注重健康的社区能让人有归属感吗？ 用重复见面和被惦记说
明归属感，同时指出活动要欢迎不同能力者。
Yes, shared activities can turn neighbours from strangers
into familiar faces. Someone who joins a regular walking
group may begin exchanging greetings and noticing
when another member is absent. That creates a small but
meaningful sense of connection. Activities should
welcome different ages and abilities, though, or the
people most needing company may feel excluded.
能，共同活动会让陌生邻居变成认识的面孔。参加固定散步
小组的人，会开始互相打招呼，也会注意谁没来，这能形成
不大却有意义的联系。但活动应欢迎不同年龄和能力的人，
否则最需要陪伴的人可能被排除。
familiar faces 熟悉的面孔
3. Does government have a part in creating healthy
communities?
政府在建设健康社区中有作用吗？ 列出个人难以提供的设施
和维护，再说明居民反馈有助于实际使用。
Yes, governments can provide and maintain things
individuals can't easily create themselves, such as safe
crossings, parks and accessible community facilities.
They can also listen to residents when deciding where
improvements are needed. Building a sports area is only
part of the job. Lighting, maintenance and reasonable
access matter if people are actually going to use it.
有，政府能提供维护个人难以独自建设的设施，例如安全过
街处、公园和方便使用的社区场所，也能听居民意见决定哪
里该改善。建运动区只是其中一步；照明、维护和合理使用
条件，同样决定人们会不会去。
community facilities 社区设施
4. Are younger people's lifestyles healthier than those
of older people?
年轻人的生活方式比年长者更健康吗？ 比较可能的各自优势
和困难，避免把体力好直接等同生活习惯好。
I wouldn't judge that by age alone. Young people may
have more energy for exercise, but irregular work or
late-night screen use can disrupt their routines. Older
people may keep steadier schedules, though physical
limitations can make some activities harder. A healthy
lifestyle depends more on daily habits and available
support than simply being young or old.
我不会只看年龄。年轻人可能更有精力运动，但不规律工作
或深夜用屏幕会打乱作息。年长者可能时间更稳定，不过身
体限制让某些活动困难。生活方式是否健康，更取决于日常
习惯和可获得的支持，而不只是年轻或年长。
steady schedules 稳定的时间安排
5. Which unhealthy habits do teenagers commonly
develop?
青少年常见哪些不健康习惯？ 选熬夜和久坐等日常行为，解
释压力与环境原因而不指责自制力。
Staying up late on phones, sitting for long periods and
skipping regular meals are habits some teenagers fall
into. These aren't always just failures of self-control.
Homework, early school starts and social expectations
can shape their choices. It helps to understand the routine
around a habit instead of simply telling young people to
be more disciplined.
有些青少年容易养成玩手机熬夜、久坐和不按时吃饭的习惯。
这不总是自制力不足，作业、上学时间早和社交期待都会影
响选择。了解习惯周围的日常安排，比只叫年轻人更自律更
有帮助。
fall into a habit 逐渐养成某种习惯

sections.title: 帮助他人提升健康的人
sections.titleEn: Someone who helped another person's health
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
98
话题 72
PART 2
帮助他人提升健康的人
Someone who helped another person's health
Describe a person who helped someone else improve their health.
描述一位帮助他人改善健康的人。
1. Who the helper is
提供帮助的人是谁
2. Who received the help
帮助了谁
3. What the helper did
采取了什么具体行动
4. How successful the help turned out to be
帮助取得了怎样的效果
审题与选材：要分清帮助者和被帮助者，讲清持续支持的做法，而不是只给一句健康建议。结果用观察到的行为和对方反馈
描述，例如开始规律活动、感觉精神好些，不把普通生活改变夸成治愈疾病。结尾也可承认改变有起伏，显得更可信。
叙述顺序
A 介绍姐姐帮助久坐的父亲活动 - B 说明父亲想改变却难以开始 - C 描述短途散步与固定邀约 - D 讲清雨天和忙碌时怎样
调整 - E 用持续参加及本人感受评估效果
A Introduce my sister supporting our inactive father - B Explain why starting a new habit felt difficult - C Describe short
walks and her regular invitations - D Show their adjustments for rain and busy evenings - E Assess progress through
consistency and his own feedback
示例回答
My older sister helped our father become more active last spring. He works from home and had got into the
habit of sitting at his desk long after finishing his work. He often said he wanted to move more, but never
seemed to find a good time to start. My sister didn't give him a complicated fitness programme. She asked him
to join her for a short walk after dinner, to the garden at the end of our street and back. At first, she came to our
flat twice a week so he wouldn't have to begin alone. She also made the walks pleasant rather than competitive.
They talked about family news, stopped to look at plants and occasionally chose a different route. On rainy
evenings, they didn't force themselves outside; they arranged another day. Gradually, my father started
suggesting walks himself, including on days when she wasn't visiting. After a couple of months, he said he felt
less stiff after work and enjoyed having a clear end to his working day. I can't put a number on the health
improvement, but his routine changed. He was moving regularly and seemed pleased with himself. I think my
sister succeeded because she made the first step small and gave him company until the habit felt natural.
中文对照：去年春天，我姐姐帮助我们的爸爸在日常生活里增加了身体活动。爸爸在家工作，做完事仍习惯长时间坐在桌
前。他常说想多动，却一直找不到合适的开始时间。姐姐没给复杂健身计划，只邀请他饭后走到街尽头的小花园再回来。
起初，她每周两次来家里，让他刚开始建立这个习惯时，不必一个人独自行动。她还让散步愉快而不带竞争：聊家庭近况、
停下看植物，偶尔换条路。下雨也不硬出门，另约一天即可。渐渐地，爸爸会主动提议散步，甚至姐姐不来探望的那些日
子，他自己也会提议出去走走。几个月后，他说工作后没那么僵硬，也喜欢下班有明确结束点。我无法用一个具体的数字
来衡量他健康改善了多少，但他的作息确实变了：开始规律活动，也对自己满意。我觉得姐姐成功在于把第一步变得很小，
再陪着他，直到习惯自然形成。
自然表达
get into the habit of
养成……的习惯
a clear end to
明确的结束点
suggest a walk
提议去散步
feel pleased with oneself
对自己的表现感到满意
串题 话题 66 一个比你年长且让你佩服的人
可以保留年长姐姐陪父亲建立散步习惯的故事，补上她的职业与性格，明确佩服耐心陪伴和灵活调整，不必另造帮助事件。
My older sister is someone I admire because she supports people patiently without making them feel under pressure.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
99
话题 72  /  帮助他人提升健康的人
PART 3
1. What can people do nowadays to remain healthy
and fit?
如今人们可以做什么来保持健康和体能？ 把答案放在可持续
日常习惯而非昂贵项目，兼顾休息与个人条件。
I'd focus on ordinary habits people can keep doing:
regular movement, varied meals and enough opportunity
to rest. Building activity into a commute or lunch break
may be more realistic than planning an ambitious
routine. Needs differ, so the aim shouldn't be copying
someone else's schedule exactly, but finding a
manageable pattern that fits everyday life.
我会关注能持续的普通习惯：规律活动、多样饮食和足够的
休息机会。把活动放进通勤或午休，也许比宏大的计划更实
际。每个人需要不同，目标不应是照抄别人的日程，而是找
到适合日常生活、能做到的安排。
a manageable pattern 可以持续做到的安排
2. How can people look after both their body and
their mental well-being?
人们怎样兼顾身体与心理状态？ 用一项同时含活动和陪伴的
日常安排说明联系，补充求助而非硬撑。
Some everyday activities can support both, such as
taking a comfortable walk with a friend or setting aside
time to unwind after work. Regular rest and contact with
supportive people also matter. There isn't one perfect
routine for everyone. If difficulties persist, recognising
the need for appropriate help is more useful than trying
to push through everything alone.
有些日常活动能兼顾两者，例如和朋友轻松散步，或下班后
留时间放松。固定休息和与支持自己的人联系也重要。没有
适合所有人的完美作息。如果困难持续，意识到需要合适的
帮助，比凡事独自硬撑更有用。
set aside time 专门留出时间
3. Are people healthier today than people in earlier
times?
现在的人比过去更健康吗？ 分别比较可得到的照护与日常习
惯，说明健康不能只按年代判断。
It's a mixed picture. People may have better access to
healthcare and information, which can help with
problems that were harder to manage before. At the same
time, some daily routines involve more sitting and less
movement. Health also varies greatly between
communities, so comparing whole generations with one
simple label misses those differences.
情况并不单一。人们可能更容易获得医疗服务和信息，有助
于处理过去较难应对的问题。同时，一些人的日常生活坐得
更多、活动更少。不同社区的健康状况也差别很大，用一个
简单判断比较整代人，会忽略这些差异。
a mixed picture 有好有坏、并不单一的情况
4. Besides sport, what else can help people keep fit?
除了体育运动，人们还能怎样保持体能？ 先给非竞技活动，
再说明生活安排能支持坚持，避免把休息当替代运动。
Movement doesn't have to take the form of a sport.
Walking to nearby places, gardening and doing active
household tasks can all make a day less sedentary. Food
and rest are also part of looking after yourself. The
useful idea is to notice opportunities throughout an
ordinary day, rather than treating fitness as something
confined to a gym.
活动不一定以体育运动的形式出现。步行去附近、园艺和需
要身体活动的家务，都能减少一天中的久坐。饮食和休息也
是照顾自己的一部分。关键是发现普通一天里的机会，而不
是把体能维护只局限在健身房。
be confined to 局限于
5. For a healthy life, does diet matter more than a
regular exercise plan?
健康生活中，饮食比规律运动计划更重要吗？ 不生硬排名，
解释两者处理不同需要，再落到最缺的一项可先改。
I wouldn't make one replace the other, because they
address different everyday needs. Eating reasonably
doesn't remove the need to move, and exercise doesn't
automatically make every food choice sensible. For
someone deciding where to begin, the more neglected
habit may deserve attention first. A routine that includes
both is more practical than arguing for one winner.
我不会让一个替代另一个，因为它们对应不同的日常需要。
吃得合理并不意味着不用活动，运动也不会自动使所有食物
选择都合理。决定从哪里开始的人，可以先关注更被忽视的
习惯。把两者都纳入生活，比硬分胜负更实际。
deserve attention 值得关注

sections.title: 想从事医药行业的人
sections.titleEn: Someone interested in a medical career
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
100
话题 73
PART 2
想从事医药行业的人
Someone interested in a medical career
Describe a person you know who hopes to work in the medical field.
描述一位你认识、希望从事医疗行业的人。
1. Who this person is
这个人是谁
2. How you know them
你们怎样认识
3. When this career interest began
何时开始产生这个职业想法
4. Why they want to enter this field
为什么希望进入医疗行业
5. What you think about their choice
你怎样看待这个职业选择
审题与选材：五个提示点都要覆盖，尤其别漏掉想法何时产生。可用一次家人的就医经历说明动机，再讲对方为选择做了什
么了解。区分想从事与已经从事，不替尚未入行的人安排真实诊疗工作；你的评价应兼顾兴趣和实际准备。
叙述顺序
A 介绍一起长大的表妹小雨 - B 交代高中探望外公时产生想法 - C 说明护士解释与照顾给她的触动 - D 描述了解课程和实际
工作的准备 - E 表达支持并承认学习过程辛苦
A Introduce Yu who grew up alongside me - B Date her interest to visiting our grandfather - C Explain the nurse whose care
impressed her - D Describe her research into courses and daily work - E Express support while recognising the demanding
preparation
示例回答
My cousin Yu would like to become a nurse. We grew up in the same neighbourhood and spent many school
holidays together, so we've often talked about what we might do in the future. Her interest began during her
second year of high school, when our grandfather spent some time in hospital. She visited after school and
noticed how one nurse explained things to him. He was worried about unfamiliar routines, and the nurse would
check that he understood what was happening instead of simply rushing away. Yu told me that this combination
of practical work and patient communication appealed to her. She likes biology, but she wants a job where
speaking clearly and noticing someone's discomfort are useful skills. Since then, she's looked at nursing course
information and spoken to a family friend who works in a hospital. That conversation helped her understand that
the job involves paperwork, tiring shifts and plenty of routine tasks as well as meaningful moments. I support her
choice because she seems interested in the actual work, not just the image of helping people. She's careful, patient
and willing to ask questions when she doesn't understand something. Of course, training will be demanding, but I
think she's taking sensible steps to find out whether the career really suits her.
中文对照：表妹小雨想当护士。我们在同一个社区长大，许多学校假期都是一起度过的，因此常聊未来工作。她的兴趣始
于高二，当时外公住了一阵院。她放学去探望，留意到一位护士怎样解释事情。外公对陌生流程不安，那位护士会确认他
听懂了，而不是匆匆离开。小雨说，实际操作与耐心沟通相结合，很吸引她。她喜欢生物，也希望工作用得到清楚表达、
留意别人不适的能力。此后她查看护理课程信息，并与一位在医院工作的家庭朋友交谈。谈过后，她知道工作除了有意义
的时刻，也有文书、疲惫的轮班和大量日常任务。我支持她作出的这个职业选择，因为她似乎对实际工作感兴趣，而不只
喜欢助人的形象。她细心耐心，不懂就问。当然培训会辛苦，但我觉得她正在踏实了解，这个职业是否真的适合自己。
自然表达
appeal to someone
吸引某人
tiring shifts
令人疲惫的轮班工作
take sensible steps
采取务实合理的步骤
patient communication
耐心的沟通
串题 话题 117 改变观点的经历
可沿用小雨了解到的护理文书与轮班细节，改讲这些信息怎样改变自己的看法；须补清先前想法、获知时间与感受，不能代
用她的愿望。
Hearing about the paperwork and tiring shifts changed my view of what nursing actually involves from day to day.


25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
101
话题 73  /  想从事医药行业的人
PART 3
1. Is becoming a doctor easy or challenging?
成为医生容易还是困难？ 区分书本知识学习与对真实病人负
责，解释长期实践训练为何必要。
I'd say it's challenging because learning information is
only part of the job. Future doctors also need supervised
practice, careful judgement and the ability to
communicate with worried patients. They must keep
learning as their work develops. The responsibility can
be demanding too, since decisions affect real people
rather than simply a mark on an exam.
我认为很有挑战，因为学习知识只是工作的一部分。未来医
生还需要受指导的实践、谨慎判断，以及和担忧的病人沟通
的能力，工作发展后也要继续学习。责任同样沉重，因为决
定影响的是真实的人，而不只是考试分数。
supervised practice 有人指导监督的实践
2. Beyond medical knowledge, what qualities does a
good doctor need?
除了医学知识，好医生还需要哪些品质？ 把耐心和细致对应
到听病人说明与解释选择，补充团队沟通。
Patience and careful listening are essential because
patients may struggle to describe what is wrong. Doctors
also need to explain options clearly and remain
respectful when someone is frightened or confused.
Teamwork matters as well. A knowledgeable doctor who
communicates poorly with colleagues can make the
whole experience harder for both patients and other staff.
耐心和认真倾听很必要，因为病人可能难以描述问题。医生
还需解释清楚不同选择，在对方害怕或困惑时仍保持尊重。
团队合作也重要。知识丰富却不善于和同事沟通的医生，会
让病人和其他工作人员都更难配合。
careful listening 认真倾听
3. What attracts some young people to careers as
doctors or nurses?
什么吸引一些年轻人去当医生或护士？ 给出助人和学科兴趣
两种动机，说明了解日常职责能检验理想。
Some are drawn to work that has a clear purpose in
helping other people. Others enjoy science or want a
practical career with continual learning. A personal
experience of receiving care can also spark interest.
Ideally, young people should explore the daily
responsibilities as well as the inspiring moments before
deciding that the profession is right for them.
有些人被明确助人的工作意义吸引，有些喜欢科学，或想做
能持续学习的实务职业。亲身接受照护的经历也可能引起兴
趣。理想情况下，年轻人决定前应同时了解日常职责与鼓舞
人的时刻，判断是否适合。
spark interest 激发兴趣
4. Are healthcare workers respected where you live?
在你生活的国家，医护人员受到尊重吗？ 以个人观察谨慎回
应，再把口头认可与实际工作待遇区分开。
In my experience, many people respect medical workers
because they recognise the skill and responsibility
involved. Families can feel especially grateful after
receiving patient, helpful care. Still, respect shouldn't be
limited to praise. Listening to staff concerns and treating
them politely during stressful appointments are everyday
ways people can show that appreciation in practice.
按我的经验，很多人尊重医护人员，因为认识到工作需要技
能、承担责任。家属得到耐心有效的照顾后，尤其会感激。
但尊重不应只有赞美。听取工作人员的顾虑，在紧张的就诊
中仍礼貌相待，都是实际表达感谢的日常方式。
show appreciation 表达感谢与认可

sections.title: 成功的企业家
sections.titleEn: Someone who runs a successful business
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
102
话题 74
PART 2
成功的企业家
Someone who runs a successful business
Describe someone you know about whose business is successful.
描述一位你了解的、把生意经营得很成功的人。
1. How you learned about this person
你是怎样知道这个人的
2. The type of business they run
对方经营哪类生意
3. How long the business has operated
这门生意已经经营多久
4. Why you consider the business successful
你为什么认为这门生意很成功
审题与选材：选一家你熟悉的小店，比介绍大企业更容易说清成功原因。先交代认识店主的经过和经营年限，再用一次具体
服务展示他怎样留住顾客。成功可以表现为稳定的回头客、合理收入和可靠口碑，不必编造营业额或夸大规模。
叙述顺序
A 从修理自行车认识店主 - B 交代店铺经营已有六年 - C 描述他检查刹车的过程 - D 说明报价透明带来回头客 - E 用稳定
经营解释他的成功
A Meet the owner through a bicycle repair - B Explain his six years in business - C Describe how he checked my brakes
- D Show how clear prices build trust - E Connect steady business with real success
示例回答
Mr Chen runs a bicycle repair shop near my old school. I first met him when my bike chain came off on the way
home, and I've taken my bike there ever since. His business has been open for about six years. It's a tiny place,
with tyres hanging above the doorway and a wooden bench for waiting customers. He repairs bikes, sells basic
parts and sometimes fixes children's scooters. There are no expensive displays, but he always seems to have the
right tool. What makes the shop successful, I think, is the way he treats people. Last month, I thought my brakes
needed replacing. He checked them, tightened a cable and explained that the pads were still fine. The repair cost
much less than I'd expected. He could easily have sold me new parts, but he didn't. He also gives a clear price
before starting work and calls customers if anything changes. That means people know what to expect. Several
of my neighbours now use his shop because I recommended it. I don't know his exact income, but he has regular
customers and has kept the business going for years. To me, that's a convincing kind of success: earning a living
by doing a useful job well.
中文对照：陈先生在我以前学校附近开了一家自行车修理店。一次放学回家时，我的车链掉了，因此认识了他，后来修车
一直找他。他的店已经开了大约六年。店面很小，门口上方挂着轮胎，顾客坐在木凳上等。他修自行车、卖常用零件，有
时也修儿童滑板车。店里没有昂贵的陈列，但他似乎总有合适的工具。我觉得他的成功在于待客方式。上个月，我以为刹
车需要更换。他检查后拧紧了一根线，告诉我刹车片还好，费用远低于我的预期。他本可以卖给我新零件，却没有这样做。
他开工前会报清价格，有变化就打电话，所以顾客心里有数。我推荐后，几位邻居也开始光顾。我不知道他的具体收入，
但他有稳定的回头客，生意多年持续经营。在我看来，靠认真做好有用的工作谋生，就是令人信服的成功。
自然表达
come off
脱落
regular customers
常客
know what to expect
知道会发生什么
earn a living
谋生
串题 话题 121 好的购物服务
上月修刹车的经历可直接转成优质服务题，保留先检查、报价透明和省下费用；重点讲那次到店过程与感受，减少六年经营
介绍。
The brake repair also illustrates good service, because he explained the problem and avoided selling me unnecessary
parts.


25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
103
话题 74  /  成功的企业家
PART 3
1. What helps a person become successful?
哪些因素能帮助一个人取得成功？ 把成功落到持续改进，解
释听取顾客反馈怎样减少重复犯错。
I think people succeed when they keep improving
something that others actually need. Effort matters, but
listening matters too. A baker might work very hard on
fancy cakes, yet lose customers if the bread is unreliable.
Paying attention to complaints and fixing small problems
can turn ability into lasting success.
我认为，不断改进别人真正需要的东西，才容易成功。努力
重要，倾听也重要。面包师可能很用心做漂亮蛋糕，但如果
面包质量不稳定，还是会流失顾客。认真听取投诉、解决小
问题，才能把能力变成持久的成功。
pay attention to 认真关注
2. Why do some new businesses fail?
为什么有些创业项目会失败？ 区分有好点子和能付账，用每
月开店租金说明现金不足的后果。
Some owners underestimate how long it takes to earn
enough money. They spend heavily on decoration, then
struggle to cover the rent before regular customers
arrive. Others never check whether people want their
product. Starting small and testing demand won't
guarantee success, but it can prevent an expensive early
mistake.
有些店主低估了赚到足够收入所需的时间。他们把大量钱花
在装修上，常客还没积累起来，就付不起租金。另一些人根
本没确认市场需求。小规模起步、测试需求虽然不能保证成
功，却能避免代价高昂的早期错误。
cover the rent 支付租金
3. How difficult is it to set up a business?
创办一家企业有多难？ 先分清开办和日常经营，再用接单之
后的具体责任说明经营难处。
Getting started can be fairly simple for a small online
service. Keeping it running is usually harder. Once
orders arrive, you have to manage payments, solve
complaints and deliver on time, often without much help.
The difficulty also depends on the business: opening a
restaurant involves more practical requirements than
selling drawings online.
小型线上服务起步可能比较简单，持续经营通常更难。一旦
有了订单，就要收款、处理投诉、按时交付，而且常常没多
少人帮忙。难度也取决于业务：开餐馆需要满足的实际要求，
比在网上卖画更多。
deliver on time 按时交付
4. Should public support be available to everyone
starting a business?
政府应该支持所有想创业的人吗？ 把人人可用的指导与有限
补助分开，说明资金需要认真审核。
Basic advice should be available to everyone, because
clear information can prevent avoidable mistakes.
Financial support needs more careful checks, though.
Public money shouldn't automatically fund every idea. I
would offer free training first, then consider small grants
for applicants who can explain their costs, customers and
realistic plans for staying open.
基础指导应该向所有人开放，因为清晰的信息能减少可避免
的错误。但资金支持需要更谨慎的审核，公共资金不应自动
资助每个点子。我会先提供免费培训，再考虑给能说明成本、
客户和持续经营计划的人小额补助。
public money 公共资金


25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
104
话题 74  /  成功的企业家
PART 3
5. Should profitable businesses contribute to society?
企业盈利后应该回馈社会吗？ 先谈企业每天对人的责任，再
举与自身业务相关的具体贡献。
Yes, particularly because businesses depend on local
workers, public services and customers. Giving back
doesn't have to mean a huge donation. A profitable repair
company could offer apprenticeships or repair
equipment for a community centre. Paying staff fairly
and treating suppliers properly should come first,
because public generosity cannot excuse poor everyday
behaviour.
应该，因为企业依靠本地员工、公共服务和顾客。回馈不一
定是巨额捐款，盈利的维修企业可以提供学徒岗位，或帮社
区中心修设备。公平付薪、善待供应商应放在前面，因为公
开做善事不能掩盖日常经营中的不当行为。
give back 回馈
6. Do customers sometimes ask for too much?
消费者有时会提出过分的要求吗？ 区分应有服务和额外索取，
以自己损坏商品后要求换新为例。
Some do, especially when they expect an immediate
solution to every problem. Asking for a safe product and
an honest description is reasonable. Demanding a free
replacement after damaging something yourself is
different. Companies should explain their policies
clearly, while customers need to recognise that a low
price cannot include unlimited personal service.
有些会，尤其是要求每个问题都立刻解决的人。要求产品安
全、描述真实很合理；自己弄坏东西后还要求免费换新，就
不同了。企业应该讲清规则，消费者也需要理解，低价格不
可能包含无限的个别服务。
an honest description 真实的描述
7. Should businesses put profit or customers' needs
first?
企业应该优先考虑利润还是消费者需求？ 说明两者互相依赖，
同时指出长期亏损就无法维持正常服务。
Customers' needs should guide what a business offers,
but the price must still cover its costs. A café that ignores
customers will lose them; one that sells everything at a
loss will close. I would prioritise useful, reliable
products and then find a sustainable way to provide them
at a fair price.
顾客需求应该决定企业提供什么，但价格仍须覆盖成本。咖
啡馆忽视顾客会失去客源，每件东西都亏本卖也会关门。我
会优先提供有用、可靠的产品，再找到一种能长期维持、价
格又合理的供应方式。
at a loss 亏本

sections.title: 做困难事情并成功的人
sections.titleEn: Someone who succeeded at a difficult task
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
身边榜样与生活习惯
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
105
话题 75
PART 2
做困难事情并成功的人
Someone who succeeded at a difficult task
Describe someone you know who successfully completed something difficult.
描述一个你认识的、成功完成困难事情的人。
1. Who the person is
这个人是谁
2. What difficult thing they did
对方做了什么困难的事
3. What helped them succeed
对方为什么能够成功
4. How you feel about this person
你对这个人的感受
审题与选材：困难要有具体限制，例如工具不足、时间紧或过去没有经验。按问题、尝试和结果讲，才能让成功有可信依据。
介绍人物后选一件完整事情，不要把多年成就列成清单。最后说明你欣赏的是哪种做法，并让这个评价对应前面的行动。
叙述顺序
A 介绍开修车店的陈先生 - B 说明他接到特殊修车请求 - C 解释零件难找造成的困难 - D 讲他试装调整并完成修理
- E 说明自己佩服他的耐心
A Introduce Mr Chen and his repair shop - B Describe a request involving an unusual bicycle - C Explain why finding parts
was difficult - D Follow his careful testing and adjustments - E Explain my respect for his patience
示例回答
Someone who comes to mind is Mr Chen, who owns the bicycle repair shop near my old school. I know him
because he has repaired my bike several times. The difficult task was restoring an old three-wheeled bicycle for
an elderly customer. The customer used it to carry vegetables home, so a standard replacement bike wouldn't
have suited her. Unfortunately, a small part in the braking system had broken, and the same model was no longer
sold locally. Mr Chen could have refused the job. Instead, he measured the damaged part, contacted several
suppliers and found something similar. It didn't fit perfectly, so he made a small adjustment to the bracket. He
then tested the brakes with heavy bags in the basket, rather than assuming an empty bike was enough. I
happened to visit during the final test. He pushed the loaded bicycle slowly across the yard while another worker
checked that both rear wheels stopped properly. A few days later, I saw the customer riding it again. I think he
succeeded because he combined practical experience with patience. He didn't rush just to clear space in the
shop. I really admire that approach, especially because the job was small but made someone's daily life easier.
中文对照：我想到的是陈先生，他在我以前学校附近开自行车修理店，给我修过几次车。那次困难的任务是为一位年长顾
客修复旧三轮车。她靠它把蔬菜运回家，普通新自行车并不适合。问题是刹车装置里的小零件坏了，本地又买不到同款。
陈先生本可拒接，却量了旧零件，联系几家供应商，找到相近的替代品。零件不完全合适，他便微调了支架。之后，他把
重袋子放进车篮测试刹车，没有只试空车。我去店里时刚好看到最后的测试。他慢慢推着载重的三轮车穿过院子，另一名
工人检查两个后轮能否正常停住。几天后，我看见那位顾客又骑上了它。我认为他能成功，是因为有经验，也有耐心。他
没有为了腾出店里的空间就草草收工。我很佩服这种做法，这虽是件小事，却让一个人的日常生活方便了。
自然表达
come to mind
想到
refuse the job
拒绝接下这份工作
fit perfectly
完全合适
clear space
腾出空间
串题 话题 74 成功的企业家
陈先生修车的故事能连接成功经营者题，但须补充店铺业务、开店年限和稳定客源；一次维修成功本身不能证明生意长久成
功。
This repair shows his working style; his years in business and returning customers would explain the shop's success.

106
话题 75  /  做困难事情并成功的人
PART 3
1. Is running a business difficult nowadays?
如今做生意困难吗？ 同时考虑网络带来的便利与竞争，用小
店价格透明说明压力。
It can be, because customers can compare prices and
reviews very quickly. A small shop may face
competitors far beyond its own street. At the same time,
inexpensive online tools make advertising and taking
orders easier. The main challenge is giving people a
clear reason to choose you and then meeting their
expectations.
可能很难，因为顾客能迅速比较价格和评价，小店也可能面
对街区之外的竞争者。同时，便宜的网络工具让宣传和接单
更方便。主要挑战是给顾客一个明确的选择理由，然后真正
达到他们的期望。
meet their expectations 达到他们的期望
2. What can businesses do to protect the
environment?
企业可以怎样保护环境？ 从采购和包装的实际浪费切入，说
明重复使用需要怎样配合。
They can start by measuring what they waste, then
change the routines causing it. A food business could
order smaller amounts more often and offer reusable
containers. Manufacturers could design products that are
easier to repair. These steps matter because they change
everyday operations, rather than simply putting a green
message on the packaging.
企业可以先记录浪费了什么，再改变造成浪费的做法。食品
店可以少量多次进货，提供可重复使用的容器。制造商可以
让产品更容易维修。这些做法改变的是日常经营，而不仅是
在包装上写环保口号。
everyday operations 日常经营
3. Does having money mean being successful?
有钱就等于成功吗？ 承认收入能体现部分成果，再用工作意
义和生活时间补足判断。
Money can show that someone's work is valued, and
having enough certainly reduces practical worries. Still,
it isn't a complete measure of success. A teacher may
earn modestly while helping struggling pupils become
confident readers. I would also consider whether a
person enjoys their work and has time for the people
they care about.
金钱可以说明一个人的工作受到认可，有足够的钱也确实能
减少实际烦恼，但它不是成功的全部标准。老师收入可能普
通，却帮助学习困难的孩子自信地阅读。我还会看一个人是
否喜欢工作，以及有没有时间陪伴在乎的人。
a complete measure of 全面衡量……的标准

sections.title: 本地名人
sections.titleEn: A well-known person in my area
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
名人、广告与体育赛事
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
107
话题 76
PART 2
本地名人
A well-known person in my area
Describe someone who is well known in your local area.
描述一位你所在地区的知名人物。
1. Who the person is
这个人是谁
2. What they have done
对方做过什么
3. Why local people like them
为什么受当地人欢迎
4. How you feel about them
你对这个人的感受
审题与选材：本地知名不必等于全国明星，可以选择居民认识的主持人、教练或社区工作者。先用传播范围说明知名程度，
再讲具体贡献。受欢迎的原因应是大家看得见的行为，自己的感受则可来自一次现场观察，避免只说他很有名。
叙述顺序
A 介绍本地电台主持人林女士 - B 交代她主持社区故事节目 - C 描述她帮助保存老店故事 - D 解释居民喜欢她耐心倾听
- E 用一次见面说明自己的敬意
A Introduce a familiar local radio presenter - B Explain her programme about neighbourhood stories - C Describe her
interviews with older shopkeepers - D Connect her patient listening with local popularity - E Recall a meeting that earned
my respect
示例回答
In my area, a radio presenter called Ms Lin is quite well known. She isn't a national celebrity, but people
recognise her voice from a weekly programme about our neighbourhood. She visits old shops, talks to long-term
residents and records stories that might otherwise disappear. One programme was about a small noodle shop that
had moved three times. Rather than discussing only the food, she asked the owner how the street and its
customers had changed. I first noticed her work because my grandmother listened while preparing dinner. Later,
I went to a community exhibition where some of those interviews were playing through headphones. There were
ordinary family photographs beside them, which made the stories feel close to home. I think people like Ms Lin
because she takes ordinary lives seriously. She lets interviewees finish their thoughts and doesn't try to make
every conversation dramatic. Older residents especially seem comfortable talking to her. I met her briefly at that
exhibition. When a visitor corrected the name of an old street, she wrote it down and thanked him. That small
reaction impressed me. She was more interested in getting the story right than in appearing knowledgeable, and
that's why I respect her work.
中文对照：我们这里有位挺出名的电台主持人林女士。她不是全国明星，但居民听过她每周介绍社区故事的节目，很熟悉
她的声音。她走访老店，采访长期居住的居民，记录可能被遗忘的故事。有一期讲一家搬过三次的面馆，她不只谈食物，
还问店主街道和顾客发生过什么变化。外婆做晚饭时会听节目，我因此关注她。后来我去社区展览，戴耳机听到这些采访，
旁边摆着普通家庭的照片，让故事显得很亲近。我觉得大家喜欢她，是因为她认真对待普通人的生活。她让受访者把话说
完，不刻意追求戏剧效果，年长居民尤其愿意和她交谈。我在展览上和她短暂见过面。一位观众纠正了旧街道的名称，她
记下来并道谢。这个小反应打动了我。她更在乎故事是否准确，而不是显得自己什么都知道，因此我尊重她的工作。
自然表达
long-term residents
长期居民
close to home
让人感到亲近
take ordinary lives seriously
认真对待普通人的生活
get the story right
把事情讲准确
串题 话题 77 想见的名人
沿用林女士的节目与社区活动，可转成想见的名人；补充希望再次在哪里见面、还想问什么，不能把已经知道的贡献当见面
愿望。
I'd like to meet her again at a community event and ask how she chooses whose stories to record.

108
话题 76  /  本地名人
PART 3
1. Is being popular at school always a good thing?
在学校受欢迎总是好事吗？ 先说交友便利，再解释维持形象
可能让学生不敢表达不同意见。
Not always. Popular students may find it easier to make
friends and organise activities, which can be enjoyable.
But they may also feel pressure to please everyone. If a
student agrees to every invitation or hides an unusual
interest to protect their image, popularity starts to limit
them rather than making school life better.
不总是。受欢迎的学生可能更容易交朋友、组织活动，这很
快乐，但也可能觉得必须讨好所有人。如果学生为维持形象
而接受每次邀请，或隐藏特别的兴趣，受欢迎反而开始限制
自己，而不是改善校园生活。
please everyone 让所有人满意
2. What makes certain students popular?
为什么有些学生很受欢迎？ 把显眼才能和让同学舒服的日常
行为分开，重点解释后者的作用。
Some attract attention through sport, music or a good
sense of humour. Lasting popularity often comes from
how they treat others, though. A student who remembers
names, includes quiet classmates and shares useful notes
is pleasant to be around. People are more likely to stay
friendly when they feel noticed rather than judged.
有些人因运动、音乐或幽默感吸引注意，但持续受欢迎常与
待人方式有关。记得名字、邀请安静同学参与、分享有用笔
记的学生，让人愿意相处。别人感到被关注而不是被评判时，
更愿意保持友好关系。
a good sense of humour 幽默感
3. Why do people enjoy following local celebrities?
人们为什么喜欢关注本地名人？ 从共同地点与生活经验解释
亲近感，不把同乡自动等同优秀。
Local celebrities feel easier to relate to because they
know the same places and may share familiar
experiences. Hearing a singer mention your town's
market can create a small sense of connection. Their
achievements can also give residents pride, although
being local alone isn't enough; people still care about
their work and behaviour.
本地名人更容易让人产生共鸣，因为大家熟悉相同地点，也
可能有相似经历。听歌手提起家乡市场，就会有一点亲近感。
他们的成就也能让居民自豪，但仅仅是本地人还不够，大家
仍在意作品和行为。
relate to 产生共鸣
4. How can well-known local people affect their
hometown?
本地名人能给家乡带来什么影响？ 举吸引游客和支持社区的
实际途径，同时说明知名度可能添堵。
They can draw attention to places that visitors might
otherwise miss. A well-known chef could introduce a
local market, bringing customers to small stalls. They
can also support community events by attending or
speaking about them. The effect isn't always positive:
sudden attention may create crowds that a small
neighbourhood isn't ready to handle.
他们能让原本被忽略的地方受到关注。知名厨师介绍一个市
场，可能给小摊带来顾客，也可以通过出席或宣传支持社区
活动。但影响并非总是正面：突然增加的关注可能带来小社
区无法应付的人潮。
draw attention to 让人关注
