sections.title: 想见的名人
sections.titleEn: A famous person I would like to meet
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
名人、广告与体育赛事
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
109
话题 77
PART 2
想见的名人
A famous person I would like to meet
Describe a famous person you hope to meet.
描述一位你希望见到的名人。
1. Who this person is
这个人是谁
2. How you first learned about them
你最初怎样知道对方
3. Where you would like to meet
你希望在哪里见面
4. Why you want to meet this person
你为什么想见这个人
审题与选材：见面愿望需要一个具体谈话目的，不能全篇只介绍名人的成就。交代怎样认识其作品后，选择适合交流的地点，
提出两三个与作品有关的问题。用希望、会问等表达保持未来语气，结尾解释这次交流对自己有什么吸引力。
叙述顺序
A 介绍想见的本地主持人林女士 - B 回忆第一次听她采访老店 - C 设想在图书馆活动后见面 - D 提出关于倾听和提问的问
题 - E 说明想学到自然交谈的方法
A Introduce the local presenter I admire - B Recall hearing her interview a shopkeeper - C Imagine meeting after a library
event - D Prepare questions about listening and interviewing - E Explain my interest in better conversations
示例回答
I'd be very interested in meeting Ms Lin, a radio presenter who is famous in my hometown. Her programme
introduces local people whose lives rarely appear in the news. I first heard her work at my grandmother's flat.
She was interviewing an elderly shopkeeper, and instead of asking a long list of questions, she followed up on a
tiny detail about his first customer. That led to a lovely story about someone paying for noodles with a bag of
vegetables. I'd like to meet her after a public talk at our library. A crowded street wouldn't be suitable, and I
wouldn't want to interrupt her private time. A short conversation after an event would feel more natural,
especially if visitors were invited to ask questions. I'd ask how she helps nervous people relax and how she
decides when to interrupt. I'm sometimes so busy thinking of my next question that I stop listening properly. She
seems able to make a conversation move forward without making the other person feel rushed. I wouldn't
mainly be looking for a photograph or an autograph. I'd be happy to leave with one practical suggestion about
listening. For me, that would make meeting her worthwhile, even if we only spoke for a few minutes.
中文对照：我很想见林女士，她是家乡知名的电台主持人，节目介绍那些很少上新闻的本地普通人。我第一次在外婆家听
她的节目。她采访一位年长店主时，没有逐项念问题，而是追问他提到的第一位顾客，引出了一个用一袋蔬菜付面钱的有
趣故事。我希望在图书馆公开讲座结束后见她。拥挤的街道不合适，我也不想打扰她的私人时间。活动后短聊更自然，尤
其是允许观众提问的时候。我会问她如何让紧张的人放松，又怎样判断什么时候该打断。我有时忙着想下一个问题，就没
认真听对方说话。她却能推动谈话，又不让人觉得被催促。我主要不是想要合影或签名。如果能带走一条关于倾听的实用
建议，我就很开心。即使只能聊几分钟，这样的见面也很值得。
自然表达
follow up on
进一步追问
private time
私人时间
feel rushed
感觉被催促
a practical suggestion
实用建议
串题 话题 76 本地名人
林女士的本地节目可直接用于本地名人题，保留采访普通人的做法；重点说明她做过什么及为何受欢迎，把希望见面的安排
缩短。
Her local programme also makes her a suitable hometown figure, with the focus on her work and popularity.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
110
话题 77  /  想见的名人
PART 3
1. What benefits can a child gain from being famous?
孩子成名有哪些好处？ 关注接触导师和展示机会，同时点明
需要成年人保护正常生活。
A famous child may get opportunities to develop a talent
with experienced teachers. A young actor, for example,
could learn from skilled performers and work on
interesting projects. Fame can also open doors to
scholarships or future work. Those benefits are most
useful when adults protect the child's education, rest and
friendships as well.
成名的孩子可能有机会跟经验丰富的老师培养才能。例如，
小演员能向优秀表演者学习，参加有意思的项目。名气也可
能带来奖学金或未来工作。成年人同时保护孩子的学习、休
息和友谊，这些好处才最有价值。
open doors to 带来……的机会
2. How can children become well known today?
如今孩子可以通过什么方式成名？ 列举比赛与作品传播，解
释展示特长比单纯求关注更可持续。
Children can become known through competitions,
performances or creative work shared online with adult
supervision. A child who explains science clearly might
attract an audience without appearing on television. Still,
becoming famous shouldn't be the main goal.
Developing a skill and enjoying the activity gives them
something worthwhile even if few people watch.
孩子可以通过比赛、表演，或在成年人监督下发布创作而出
名。能清楚讲解科学的孩子，即使不上电视也可能吸引观众。
不过，成名不该是主要目标。培养技能、享受活动，即使观
众很少，也能获得有价值的收获。
attract an audience 吸引观众
3. How might children make use of their fame?
孩子可以怎样利用自己的名气？ 选择与年龄相符的小行动，
避免让儿童承担公众人物全部责任。
They could use it to support something they understand,
such as encouraging reading or collecting books for a
school library. Their example may reach other children
more easily than an adult's message. But they shouldn't
be expected to comment on every public issue. Adults
need to help them choose activities that are manageable
and appropriate.
他们可以支持自己理解的事情，例如鼓励阅读，或为学校图
书馆募集图书。与成年人的话相比，他们的示范可能更容易
影响其他孩子。但不应要求孩子评论所有公共议题，成年人
要帮助他们选择能够承担、适合年龄的活动。
support something 支持某件事
4. Is talent the reason people become famous?
人们出名是因为有才华吗？ 把获得关注和长期留住观众分开，
说明机会与能力各有作用。
Talent certainly helps, but it isn't the only reason.
Timing, publicity and access to opportunities can affect
who gets noticed. Someone may become famous after
one amusing video without having a developed skill.
Keeping an audience interested is a different challenge,
and consistent, thoughtful work often matters more once
the initial excitement fades.
才华当然有帮助，但不是唯一原因。时机、宣传和机会都会
影响谁被看见。有人可能凭一个有趣视频成名，却没有成熟
技能。持续留住观众是另一种挑战，最初的新鲜感消退后，
稳定而用心的作品往往更重要。
get noticed 受到注意
5. How easy is it to become famous in your country?
在你们国家，成名容易吗？ 谨慎区分短暂传播与全国知名，
不凭空断言成名人数或概率。
I wouldn't call it easy. In China, posting something
online is accessible, but many people are competing for
attention. A clip might spread quickly, yet that doesn't
mean its creator will remain well known. Building a
lasting reputation usually requires repeated good work,
support from others and some luck with who discovers
it.
我觉得不容易。在中国，上网发布内容很方便，但争取关注
的人也很多。一个片段可能迅速传播，却不代表创作者会一
直出名。建立持久声誉通常需要持续的好作品、他人支持，
以及被人发现时的一点运气。
a lasting reputation 持久的声誉
6. Would you personally like to be famous?
你自己想成为名人吗？ 说明认可和广泛曝光的区别，用日常
生活的自由支持个人选择。
I'd enjoy being respected for something I do well, but I
wouldn't want widespread fame. I like being able to
make mistakes or have a quiet afternoon without people
watching. Having a small audience for my work would
suit me better. That would offer useful feedback and
opportunities while leaving most of my life private.
我希望因为擅长的事情受到尊重，但不想广泛出名。我喜欢
能自在犯错，或安静度过下午，不被别人盯着。作品拥有少
量受众更适合我，这既能带来反馈和机会，也能让生活的大
部分保持私密。
widespread fame 广泛的名气

sections.title: 采访一个名人的经历
sections.titleEn: An interview with a famous person
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
名人、广告与体育赛事
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
111
话题 78
PART 2
采访一个名人的经历
An interview with a famous person
Describe a time when you interviewed someone famous.
描述一次你采访名人的经历。
1. Who you interviewed
你采访了谁
2. When and where the interview happened
采访的时间和地点
3. What you asked or discussed
你问了什么或谈了什么
4. How you felt about the experience
你对这次经历有什么感受
审题与选材：把采访限定为学校或社区中的短交流，也能完整回答题目。必须说清谁授权或组织了这次采访、你具体问了什
么，以及对方如何回应。紧张和放松要有变化原因，例如对方主动等你整理问题，让感受依附于真实动作。
叙述顺序
A 介绍接受采访的本地作家 - B 交代春季书展和采访任务 - C 说明事先准备的写作问题 - D 讲对方回答引出的新问题
- E 描述从紧张转为自在的过程
A Introduce a writer known in our town - B Set the interview at a spring fair - C Explain my prepared questions about
writing - D Follow his answer with a new question - E Describe becoming comfortable after initial nerves
示例回答
Last spring, I interviewed a writer called Mr Xu for our community newsletter. He's well known locally for short
stories about family life, and he was speaking at a small book fair in the town library. The organiser gave me ten
minutes with him after his talk. We sat at a table beside a window, away from the main crowd. I had three
questions written on a card, but my hands were shaking slightly when I switched on my recorder. I first asked
where he found ideas. He said he kept notes about ordinary conversations, including things he heard while
waiting for a bus. That surprised me because I'd imagined writers needed dramatic experiences. So I put my next
prepared question aside and asked how he turned an ordinary conversation into a story. He explained that he
usually imagined what each person wanted but wasn't saying. Then he asked me to think of a recent
disagreement with a friend. Suddenly, the advice felt much easier to understand. By the end, I wasn't worried
about sounding clever. I was simply curious. I left feeling relieved and rather proud, because I'd managed to
listen and ask a useful follow-up question instead of just reading from my card.
中文对照：去年春天，我为社区通讯采访了作家徐先生。他写家庭生活短篇，在本地很有名，当时在镇图书馆的小型书展
演讲。组织者安排我在演讲后采访十分钟。我们坐在远离人群的窗边桌旁。我把三个问题写在卡片上，但打开录音机时，
手仍有点抖。我先问他哪里来的灵感。他说会记录普通谈话，包括等公交时听到的内容。我很意外，原本以为作家需要戏
剧性的经历。于是，我把下一个准备好的问题放到一边，追问如何把普通对话变成故事。他说自己通常会想象每个人想要
什么，却没有说出口。接着，他让我回想最近和朋友的一次争论，这建议一下就好理解了。到最后，我不再担心自己听起
来够不够聪明，只是很好奇。离开时，我既松了一口气，也有点骄傲，因为我认真倾听并提出了有用的追问，而不是只照
卡片念。
自然表达
put something aside
暂时放下某事
switch on
打开
sound clever
显得聪明
a follow-up question
追问

沿用徐先生的写作方法和采访后的好奇，可回答想见的名人；说明为什么希望再次交流，以及想约在哪里，不必重复整场采
访。
I'd like to meet him again and ask more about turning ordinary conversations into stories.


25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
112
话题 78  /  采访一个名人的经历
PART 3
1. Who is commonly interviewed in news reports?
新闻报道通常采访哪些人？ 按解释事件和亲历事件区分受访
者，说明名气不是唯一标准。
News reports often interview people directly involved in
an event, along with experts who can explain it. After a
transport disruption, passengers can describe what
happened to them, while an engineer may explain the
cause. Public officials and celebrities also appear, but a
useful interviewee doesn't have to be famous; relevant
knowledge matters more.
新闻常采访直接参与事件的人，以及能解释事件的专家。交
通中断后，乘客能讲述自己的经历，工程师则可能解释原因。
官员和名人也会出现，但有用的受访者不一定有名，相关知
识更重要。
directly involved in 直接参与
2. What qualities does an effective interviewer need?
优秀的采访者需要哪些素质？ 用含糊回答后的追问说明倾听
与准备的区别，兼顾礼貌和清楚。
A good interviewer needs curiosity, preparation and the
patience to listen. They should notice when an answer is
vague and ask for a concrete example without sounding
aggressive. If someone says a project was difficult,
asking which part caused trouble is more useful than
immediately moving to the next question on a list.
好的采访者需要好奇心、准备和倾听的耐心。他们应能注意
到含糊回答，并在不显得咄咄逼人的情况下索取具体例子。
如果受访者说项目很难，问清哪部分出了问题，比立刻转到
列表中的下一题更有用。
a concrete example 具体例子
3. How do interviewers prepare to interview
celebrities?
采访者在访问名人前通常怎样准备？ 从了解公开作品到设计
新问题，解释为什么不能只重复旧采访。
They usually learn about the person's work and read
previous interviews to avoid repeating obvious
questions. They also decide what their audience would
genuinely want to know. Before recording, they may
confirm the time limit and topics. Good preparation
provides direction, but the interviewer still needs enough
flexibility to follow an unexpected, interesting answer.
他们通常了解对方的作品，阅读过去的采访，避免重复显而
易见的问题，也会思考观众真正想了解什么。录制前可能确
认时间限制和话题。充分准备能给采访方向，但仍需要灵活
跟进意料之外的有趣回答。
the time limit 时间限制
4. Are famous people entitled to a private life?
名人是否有权拥有私人生活？ 把公众工作和私人日常分开，
说明观众兴趣不能自动成为采访理由。
Yes. Being recognised doesn't mean agreeing to have
every part of your life exposed. Questions about a
person's public work are reasonable, but photographing
their children or following them home can cause real
distress. There can be legitimate public interest in
serious wrongdoing, yet ordinary family routines usually
have little to do with that.
有权。被人认识不代表同意公开全部生活。询问公开工作合
理，但拍摄其孩子或跟踪回家会造成真实困扰。严重不当行
为可能涉及合理的公众利益，但普通家庭日常通常与此关系
不大。
public work 公开的工作
5. In what ways can media coverage change
celebrities' lives?
媒体报道会怎样改变名人的生活？ 把职业机会与私人压力并
列，用报道内容如何扩散说明影响。
Media coverage can introduce their work to a much
larger audience and bring new opportunities. It can also
make ordinary mistakes feel permanent, especially when
short clips spread without context. A performer might
gain bookings after a thoughtful interview but become
reluctant to speak casually after an embarrassing
sentence is repeated everywhere.
媒体能把名人的作品介绍给更多观众，带来新机会，也可能
让普通失误像永远无法摆脱一样，尤其是脱离背景的短片段
广泛传播时。表演者可能因深入采访获得邀约，却因一句尴
尬的话被到处重复，而不敢随意开口。
without context 脱离背景

sections.title: 做广告的名人
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
名人、广告与体育赛事
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
113
话题 79
PART 2
做广告的名人
An advertisement featuring a celebrity
Describe an advertisement that features a famous person.
描述一则有名人出镜的广告。
1. What the advertisement promotes
广告宣传什么
2. When and where you saw it
你在何时何地看到它
3. What the celebrity does in it
名人在广告中做什么
4. How you felt about it
你对广告的感受
审题与选材：以广告本身为中心，先交代商品、看到的场合，再描述一个可见动作或画面。名人身份只需足够辨认，不必介
绍生平。评价可以分成吸引注意和是否愿意购买两层，说明好记的画面不一定足以证明商品适合自己。
叙述顺序
A 说明地铁里看到水杯广告 - B 介绍画面中的知名男演员 - C 描述他漏水后更换水杯 - D 解释画面为何让自己记住
- E 区分喜欢广告和实际购买
A Locate the advertisement in a metro station - B Introduce the actor shown in it - C Describe the leaking cup and
replacement - D Explain why the scene caught my attention - E Separate enjoying the advertisement from buying
示例回答
One advertisement I remember was for a reusable travel cup. I saw it on a screen at a metro station last winter
while waiting for a friend. It featured a well-known actor whose face I recognised from television, although I
couldn't remember his name. The advert began with him rushing towards a bus, carrying a paper cup and a stack
of documents. The lid came loose, and a little coffee splashed onto his papers. He stopped, looked at the mess
and gave a very tired smile. The next scene showed him using the advertised cup. He put it in the side pocket of
his bag and walked away calmly. There wasn't much dialogue, just a short message about a secure lid and
carrying your own cup. I found it amusing because the first scene looked like a believable bad morning. The
actor didn't appear glamorous or perfect, which made the situation easier to relate to. I also liked that the
product's purpose was clear within a few seconds. Still, I didn't buy it immediately. I'd want to check whether it
was easy to clean and whether the lid really worked well. The famous face made me notice the advertisement,
but practical details would decide whether I spent any money.
中文对照：我记得一则可重复使用的随行杯广告。去年冬天，我在地铁站等朋友时，从屏幕上看到它。广告里是一位我在
电视上见过的知名演员，但我想不起名字。开头他拿着纸杯和一叠文件赶公交，杯盖松了，咖啡洒到文件上。他停下来，
看着污渍，疲惫地笑了笑。下一幕，他换用广告里的杯子，把它放进包侧袋，轻松走开。对白很少，只有关于牢固杯盖和
自带水杯的简短文字。我觉得挺好笑，因为第一幕像真实的糟糕早晨。演员没有显得光鲜完美，让人容易产生共鸣，而且
几秒钟就能看懂产品用途。不过，我没有立刻购买。我还想确认它好不好清洗，杯盖是否确实可靠。名人的脸让我注意到
广告，但实用细节才会决定我是否花钱。
自然表达
come loose
松脱
a secure lid
牢固的杯盖
relate to
产生共鸣
practical details
实用细节
串题 话题 109 有趣的视频
这则动态广告可转成有趣视频题，保留地铁站屏幕、漏咖啡的情节和感受；说明为何停下观看，不必为换题新增演员的个人
经历。
This short video advertisement could also fit an interesting video topic, focusing on its story and why I kept watching.


25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
名人、广告与体育赛事
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
114
话题 79  /  做广告的名人
PART 3
1. What are the main benefits and drawbacks of
advertising?
广告主要有哪些优点和缺点？ 同时讲信息帮助与购买压力，
用新店信息和虚假紧迫感作区别。
Advertising helps people discover products, services and
new local businesses. A clear advert can save time by
showing prices and opening hours. The downside is that
it may exaggerate benefits or create pressure to buy
things people don't need. Repeated messages about
limited offers can make an ordinary purchase feel
unnecessarily urgent.
广告帮助人们发现产品、服务和本地新店。清晰的广告展示
价格和营业时间，能节省时间。缺点是可能夸大好处，或让
人觉得必须买不需要的东西。反复宣传限时优惠，会让普通
购买显得没必要地紧迫。
create pressure 造成压力
2. Why do businesses hire celebrities for
advertisements?
企业为什么请名人拍广告？ 解释熟悉面孔如何先吸引注意，
再区别借来的好感和产品质量。
A familiar face can catch attention before people even
notice the product. Companies also hope that positive
feelings about a singer or actor will carry over to the
brand. Using several celebrities may reach different
groups of customers. That can increase recognition, but
it doesn't automatically persuade people who want clear
evidence of quality.
熟悉的面孔能在人们注意产品前先吸引目光。企业也希望大
家对歌手或演员的好感能延伸到品牌。请多位名人可能接触
不同顾客群体，增加辨识度，但不会自动说服那些希望看到
明确质量依据的人。
carry over to 延伸到
3. Where do you tend to encounter advertisements?
你通常会在哪里看到广告？ 把通勤与手机使用分成两个具体
场景，再指出难以识别的推广。
I see them on transport screens, shop windows and
posters near busy roads. Online, they appear between
videos, in search results and inside shopping apps. Some
are obvious, while others look like ordinary
recommendations from creators. That second kind needs
more attention, because you may not immediately realise
someone is being paid to promote something.
我在交通屏幕、橱窗和繁忙道路旁的海报上看到广告。网上
则有视频间广告、搜索结果和购物软件里的推广。有些很明
显，有些看起来像创作者的普通推荐。后者更需要留心，因
为你未必马上知道对方收钱做了宣传。
search results 搜索结果
4. How useful do you think advertisements are?
你认为广告有多大用处？ 用解决具体需求衡量实用性，避免
把广告好看直接等同有用。
They're useful when they answer a question a customer
already has. An advert showing a repair shop's location,
prices and services could help someone with a broken
phone. An attractive image with no practical information
is less useful to me. I usually treat advertising as a
starting point and check the details before deciding.
当广告回答顾客已经存在的问题时，就有用。介绍修理店地
址、价格和服务的广告，能帮助手机坏了的人。只有漂亮图
片、没有实用信息的广告对我作用较小。我通常把广告当作
起点，再核对细节后决定。
a starting point 起点
5. Are online advertisements better than
advertisements offline?
线上广告比线下广告更好吗？ 用可点击比较和本地覆盖分别
说明优势，不把效果简单归于媒介。
Online adverts are easier to update, and interested
viewers can click straight through to more information.
Offline advertising can work well for a local business
because it reaches people already nearby. A poster
outside a café may be more useful than a widely shared
video. The better choice depends on who the business
needs to reach.
线上广告容易更新，有兴趣的人可以直接点击了解更多信息。
线下广告对本地商家也有用，因为能接触已经在附近的人。
咖啡馆门口的海报可能比广泛传播的视频更有效。哪种更好，
取决于商家想接触谁。
click straight through 直接点击进入

sections.title: 一个成功的运动员
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
名人、广告与体育赛事
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
115
话题 80
PART 2
一个成功的运动员
A sportsperson who performed well
Describe a sportsperson from your country who performed well at an event.
描述一位在某场体育赛事中表现出色的本国运动员。
1. Who the sportsperson is
这位运动员是谁
2. What the event was
是什么比赛
3. What this person did during it
对方在比赛中的表现
4. Why you think they performed so well
你认为对方发挥出色的原因
审题与选材：题目不要求奥运冠军，熟悉的本国业余运动员也能讲清。选一场确实了解的比赛，描述关键动作和对队伍的作
用。发挥好的原因应对应观察到的准备、判断或配合，不要只把获胜归因于天赋，更不必堆砌赛事数字。
叙述顺序
A 介绍中国业余球员李俊 - B 交代市体育馆的篮球决赛 - C 描述他及时改变传球选择 - D 讲最后阶段如何帮助队友
- E 联系训练说明出色表现原因
A Introduce Li Jun, a Chinese amateur player - B Set the scene at a city final - C Describe his change in passing decisions
- D Explain how he supported his teammates - E Connect his performance with careful preparation
示例回答
The sportsperson I'd choose is Li Jun, a Chinese basketball player on a local amateur team. He's my cousin's
friend, so I knew a little about him before watching the team play. The event was a weekend basketball final at
our city sports centre last autumn. His team started badly. They kept trying to shoot from too far away, and the
other side collected most of the rebounds. Li wasn't the tallest player, but he stayed calm. Instead of rushing
forward every time he got the ball, he slowed things down and looked for teammates near the basket. I
remember one pass that went through a narrow gap between two defenders. His teammate caught it and scored
without having to turn around. Later, when a younger teammate missed an easy shot, Li clapped and called for
him to keep moving. That mattered because the boy looked ready to stop asking for the ball. Their team
eventually won by a small margin. I think Li did well because he read the game carefully and trusted the other
players. My cousin said they practised those short passing moves regularly. Watching them work during a close
match made me appreciate how much preparation sits behind a few apparently simple decisions.
中文对照：我会选李俊，他是中国一支本地业余队的篮球运动员，也是我表哥的朋友，所以看比赛前我就略知其人。去年
秋天的一个周末，他们在市体育中心打篮球决赛。开局很差，队员总在太远的地方投篮，篮板大多被对手拿走。李俊不是
最高的球员，却很冷静。他拿球后没有每次都急着向前冲，而是慢下来，寻找篮下队友。我记得他有一次从两名防守者之
间的窄缝传球，队友接球后不用转身就得分了。后来，一个年轻队友投丢了简单的球，他鼓掌让对方继续跑动。这很重要，
因为那个男孩看起来已经不敢再要球了。他们最后以微弱优势获胜。我觉得李俊表现好，是因为他认真观察局势，也信任
队友。表哥说他们经常练这种短传。在胶着比赛中看见训练起作用，让我理解几个看似简单的决定背后有多少准备。
自然表达
stay calm
保持冷静
read the game
判断比赛局势
by a small margin
以微弱优势
keep moving
继续跑动
串题 话题 81 现场观看体育比赛
沿用这场篮球决赛可转到现场观赛题，保留关键传球；把重点移到自己坐在哪里、听到什么及情绪变化，不只分析李俊表现。
I watched that final in person, so I could also describe the crowd and my own reactions to the match.

116
话题 80  /  一个成功的运动员
PART 3
1. Which sports are particularly popular in your
country?
你们国家哪些运动特别受欢迎？ 根据日常生活中可见的场景
谈几类运动，避免编造全国人气排名。
Basketball, badminton and table tennis are all very
visible where I live in China. You can see basketball
courts near schools and people playing badminton in
parks. Football also attracts plenty of viewers. I would
distinguish watching from participating, though, because
a sport can have a large television audience without
many people playing it regularly.
在我生活的中国地区，篮球、羽毛球和乒乓球都很常见。学
校附近有篮球场，公园里有人打羽毛球，足球也吸引很多观
众。不过，我会把观看和参与分开，因为电视观众很多的运
动，不一定有同样多人经常参与。
distinguish watching from participating 区分观看与参与
2. What would you say is your country's second most
popular sport?
你觉得你们国家第二受欢迎的运动是什么？ 承认没有可靠全
国排名，再明确按身边参与情况作有限判断。
I couldn't give a reliable national ranking, because the
answer changes depending on whether you count
viewers or players. If I judged by participation around
me, I'd probably put badminton second after basketball.
It's common in community centres and doesn't require a
large team, so friends can arrange a game quite easily
after work.
我无法给出可靠的全国排名，因为按观众还是参与者计算，
答案会不同。如果根据身边参与情况判断，我可能把羽毛球
排在篮球之后。社区中心很常见，也不用凑很大的队伍，所
以朋友下班后容易约着打。
a reliable national ranking 可靠的全国排名
3. Should children try a range of sports?
孩子应该学习多种运动吗？ 从发现兴趣与接触不同动作说明
好处，再限制训练安排的负担。
Yes, trying different sports helps children discover what
they enjoy and practise different kinds of movement.
Swimming, running and a ball game offer quite different
experiences. They don't need formal lessons in
everything, though. A few relaxed opportunities to try
each activity may be better than a crowded timetable that
makes exercise feel like another obligation.
应该，尝试不同运动能帮助孩子发现兴趣，练习不同动作。
游泳、跑步和球类带来的体验很不同，但不必每项都正式上
课。轻松尝试几种活动，可能比排满课程更好，否则锻炼也
会变成另一项义务。
different kinds of movement 不同类型的动作
4. What lessons can children learn through sport?
孩子通过运动能学到什么？ 把合作落到等待和分工，把面对
失败落到下一次练习的选择。
They can learn how to cooperate, handle disappointment
and improve through practice. In a relay race, running
fast isn't enough; passing the baton carefully matters too.
Losing can also teach children to identify one thing to
work on. Those lessons depend on adults treating
mistakes as part of learning rather than reasons for
humiliation.
孩子能学习合作、面对失望，以及靠练习进步。接力赛不只
要跑得快，还要认真交棒。输掉比赛也能让孩子找出一项需
要改进的地方。不过，前提是成年人把错误当学习的一部分，
而不是羞辱孩子的理由。
handle disappointment 面对失望
5. What abilities does a successful athlete need?
成功的运动员需要什么能力？ 区分身体技术与比赛判断，用
比分落后时的调整说明心理能力。
Physical skill is essential, but successful athletes also
need concentration and good judgement. They must
notice what is happening and adjust their decisions under
pressure. A tennis player who falls behind may need to
change tactics rather than hit harder. Listening to
coaches and recovering from mistakes are useful skills
alongside strength, speed and technique.
身体技能必不可少，但成功运动员也需要专注和判断力，能
观察情况，在压力下调整决定。网球选手落后时可能需要改
变战术，而不是更用力击球。除了力量、速度和技术，听教
练建议、从失误中恢复也很重要。
under pressure 在压力下
6. How do people use technology in sport?
科技在体育中有哪些用途？ 分开训练、判罚和观赛三种用途，
并说明收集数据不能取代判断。
Coaches use video to examine movement and show
athletes details they may not feel while playing. Timing
systems and replay tools can also help officials make
decisions. For viewers, graphics explain positions and
scores. These tools are useful, but someone still has to
interpret the information; collecting more data doesn't
automatically produce better training.
教练用视频分析动作，让运动员看到比赛时未必察觉的细节。
计时系统和回放工具能帮助裁判判定，画面图示则向观众解
释位置和比分。这些工具有用，但信息仍需要人理解，数据
更多不自动代表训练更好。
replay tools 回放工具

sections.title: 现场观看体育比赛
sections.titleEn: A match I watched in person
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
名人、广告与体育赛事
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
117
话题 81
PART 2
现场观看体育比赛
A match I watched in person
Describe a sports match you watched live at the venue.
描述一场你到现场观看过的体育比赛。
1. What kind of match it was
是什么比赛
2. When you attended
你什么时候去看的
3. What the match and atmosphere were like
比赛和现场气氛如何
4. How you felt about the experience
你对这次经历有什么感受
审题与选材：现场观看必须包含自己在场的证据，如座位、声音、视线或周围观众。选一两个比赛转折即可，不必复述全场
比分。先说明时间和赛事，再把现场细节与紧张、兴奋等感受联系起来，让听者知道这次观看为何特别。
叙述顺序
A 交代去年秋天的篮球决赛 - B 说明和表哥坐在场边看台 - C 描述球鞋声和紧张的比分 - D 讲关键传球引来全场欢呼
- E 比较现场与电视的感受
A Introduce a basketball final last autumn - B Find seats with my cousin near courtside - C Describe the sounds and close
score - D Recall a decisive pass and cheering crowd - E Explain why attending felt different from television
示例回答
Last autumn, my cousin took me to a local basketball final at our city sports centre. It was on a Saturday
afternoon, and one of his friends was playing, so we had a particular team to support. We sat about halfway up a
small stand beside the court. There weren't thousands of people, but the hall made every sound seem louder. I
could hear shoes squeaking, coaches calling instructions and the ball hitting the floor much more clearly than on
television. The match was close, especially towards the end. Our team had started poorly, then gradually caught
up by making shorter passes. With only a little time left, my cousin's friend sent the ball between two defenders
to a teammate under the basket. Almost everyone around us stood up before the shot even went in. I usually
watch sport quite quietly, but I found myself shouting with the crowd. When our team won, people were still
talking about that pass while walking towards the exit. I felt excited and surprisingly tired afterwards. Keeping
track of the whole court took more attention than following a television camera. What I enjoyed most was
sharing each uncertain moment with people nearby, even though most of them were strangers.
中文对照：去年秋天，表哥带我去市体育中心看本地篮球决赛。那是周六下午，他的朋友参赛，所以我们有明确支持的队
伍。我们坐在场边小看台的中间位置。观众没有成千上万，但体育馆把每个声音都放大了。我能清楚听到球鞋摩擦、教练
喊话和篮球落地，比电视里明显得多。比赛比分很接近，尤其到了最后。我们支持的队开局不好，后来靠短传逐渐追上。
剩余时间不多时，表哥的朋友把球从两名防守者之间传给篮下队友。球还没进，周围几乎所有人就站了起来。我平时看比
赛很安静，那天却跟着人群喊了起来。球队获胜后，大家走向出口时还在谈那次传球。赛后我很兴奋，竟然也有些疲惫，
因为自己观察整个球场比跟着电视镜头更费注意力。我最喜欢的是和附近的人一起经历那些结果未定的瞬间，尽管大多是
陌生人。
自然表达
catch up
追上
go in
投进
keep track of
持续留意
shout with the crowd
跟着人群呐喊
串题 话题 80 一个成功的运动员
这场决赛能转为本国运动员题，但须确认李俊的身份并聚焦他的传球、判断和准备；观众欢呼本身不能说明某位球员为何出
色。
The same match could introduce Li Jun, focusing on his decisions and preparation rather than my experience in the
stands.

118
话题 81  /  现场观看体育比赛
PART 3
1. Which sporting events do people often watch in
your country?
你们国家的人通常观看哪些体育赛事？ 分别谈球类联赛与综
合赛事，避免把自己爱看说成所有人偏好。
People around me often watch basketball and football
matches, along with major table tennis and badminton
competitions. Large international events attract viewers
who don't normally follow sport as well. Preferences
differ by age and friendship group. Some people watch a
particular team every week, while others only gather for
an important final involving Chinese athletes.
我身边的人常看篮球、足球，以及大型乒乓球和羽毛球比赛。
大型国际赛事也会吸引平时不看体育的人。喜好随年龄和朋
友圈而不同，有人每周追一支队，有人只在中国运动员参加
重要决赛时一起看。
follow sport 关注体育
2. What are the advantages of attending sports
events?
到现场观看体育赛事有什么优点？ 说明共同反应与自由观察
的价值，不只重复气氛好这个判断。
The atmosphere is the biggest advantage for me. You
hear the crowd react immediately and feel part of a
shared experience. You can also choose where to look,
noticing players away from the ball. Television usually
decides that for you. Even a small local match can feel
exciting when everyone nearby is following the same
uncertain moment.
对我来说，最大的优点是气氛。你能立即听见观众反应，感
觉自己参与了一场共同经历，也能自己选择看哪里，注意没
有持球的队员。电视通常替你决定视线。即使小型本地比赛，
周围人一起关注悬念时也很激动。
a shared experience 共同经历
3. What makes watching sport on television
appealing?
通过电视观看体育赛事有哪些好处？ 用回放和讲解解释比赛
为何更易理解，再补充费用和舒适度的便利。
Television gives you close views, replays and
explanations, so complicated moments can be easier to
understand. It's also cheaper and more comfortable than
travelling to a venue. Families can watch together
without worrying about weather or transport home. You
lose some atmosphere, but you often gain a clearer view
of the actual sporting action.
电视提供近景、回放和讲解，复杂场面因此更容易理解，也
比去场馆便宜、舒适。家人可以一起看，不必担心天气或回
家交通。虽然少了些现场气氛，但对比赛动作本身往往看得
更清楚。
a clearer view 更清楚的视角
4. What sporting competitions in China are
appropriate for children?
中国有哪些体育比赛适合儿童？ 按年龄与规则说明适合参加
的赛事，避免直接推荐高强度成人赛。
School relay races, short swimming events and small
team games can be suitable if they match the children's
ages and abilities. In China, a neighbourhood badminton
tournament could also work well. I'd favour simple rules,
short sessions and supportive supervision. The aim
should be giving children a positive first experience,
rather than copying adult competition exactly.
学校接力赛、短距离游泳和小队球赛，只要符合年龄能力，
就可以适合儿童。在中国，社区羽毛球比赛也不错。我倾向
规则简单、时间较短、有人支持照看的比赛，目标是让孩子
获得积极初体验，而非照搬成人赛事。
supportive supervision 给予支持的照看
5. Do children today experience a great deal of
competition?
如今孩子面临很多竞争吗？ 承认学习与兴趣活动都有比较，
再指出家庭和学校会影响压力。
Many do, in schoolwork as well as sport, music and
other activities. Even an enjoyable hobby can become
competitive when adults constantly compare results. The
pressure isn't identical for every child, though. A school
that celebrates improvement may feel very different
from one where every activity ends with a ranking
displayed for everyone to see.
很多孩子确实如此，竞争存在于学业、体育、音乐等活动。
成年人不断比较结果时，快乐的爱好也会变成竞争。不过，
并非每个孩子压力都一样。重视进步的学校，与每项活动都
公开排名的学校，感受可能很不同。
compare results 比较结果
6. Can this level of competition benefit children?
这种程度的竞争对孩子有益吗？ 区别适度挑战与长期比较，
解释评价努力怎样影响继续参与。
A manageable amount can encourage effort and help
children learn to cope with disappointment. Too much
can make them afraid to try anything they might not win.
I think competition works best when the rules are fair
and improvement matters alongside results. Children
should still have activities where they can explore
without being compared.
适量竞争可以鼓励努力，帮助孩子面对失望。过多竞争会让
他们不敢尝试可能赢不了的事。我认为，规则公平、既看结
果也看进步时，竞争最有益。孩子仍应有些不被比较、可以
自由探索的活动。
cope with disappointment 应对失望

sections.title: 擅长学习和说外语的人
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
学习技能与培养兴趣
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
119
话题 82
PART 2
擅长学习和说外语的人
Someone who learns languages well
Describe someone who is good at learning and speaking new languages.
描述一位擅长学习和使用新语言的人。
1. How you met this person
你怎样认识对方
2. How they learn a new language
对方怎样学习新语言
3. Which languages they speak
对方会说哪些语言
4. How you feel about this person
你对这个人的感受
审题与选材：外语能力不必靠流利得像母语者来证明，能完成日常交流已经具体。先讲认识经过和会用的语言，再挑两种互
相配合的学习办法，例如听短片段后录音复述。用一次交流说明方法的效果，感受则落在对方愿意开口和持续练习的态度上。
叙述顺序
A 说明在大学认识室友安娜 - B 交代她能使用三种语言 - C 描述听短录音再自己复述 - D 讲她主动询问不懂的表达
- E 解释自己佩服她敢于开口
A Introduce Anna, my former university roommate - B Name the three languages she uses - C Describe listening and
recording short spoken summaries - D Show how she asks about unfamiliar expressions - E Explain my admiration for her
willingness to speak
示例回答
My former university roommate Anna is very good at learning languages. We met when we were assigned the
same room in our first year, and I soon noticed how much she enjoyed talking to people from different places.
Her first language is Chinese, and she speaks English confidently. She can also hold everyday conversations in
Spanish, which she started learning because she enjoyed Spanish-language films. Her routine is quite practical.
She chooses a short recording, listens several times and then records herself explaining the same idea in her own
words. She doesn't try to memorise a whole page of vocabulary at once. Instead, she keeps a few useful
expressions in a small notebook and looks for chances to use them. Once, I heard her chatting online with a
Spanish-speaking friend about cooking. When she couldn't describe a kitchen tool, she explained what it was
used for and asked for its name. She wrote the word down, then continued without getting embarrassed. That's
what I admire most. She treats a missing word as a small problem to solve, rather than proof that she's bad at
languages. Watching her has made me more willing to speak English before I've worked out a perfect sentence
in my head.
中文对照：我以前的大学室友安娜很擅长学语言。大一分到同一间宿舍后，我们认识了，我很快发现她喜欢和不同地方的
人聊天。她的母语是中文，英语说得很自信，也能用西班牙语进行日常交流；她因喜欢西语电影而开始学习。她的方法很
实际：选一段短录音，听几遍，再录下自己用不同措辞复述同样内容的声音。她不会一次背整页单词，而是在小本子里记
几句实用表达，寻找使用机会。有一次，我听见她和一位说西班牙语的朋友在网上聊做饭。她不会说一种厨具的名称，就
解释用途，再问名字。她记下单词后继续聊，没有难为情。我最佩服的就是这点：她把缺少单词当作可以解决的小问题，
而不是自己语言差的证据。看她这样，我也更愿意先开口说英语，不必等脑中拼出完美句子。
自然表达
hold a conversation
进行交谈
in her own words
用她自己的话
look for chances
寻找机会
work out
想出；弄清
串题 话题 117 改变观点的经历
安娜遇到生词仍继续聊天的场景可转成改变观点题；明确自己原先认为要准备完美句子，看见她解释用途后为何愿意先开口。
Watching Anna handle a missing word changed my belief that I needed a perfect sentence before speaking.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
120
话题 82  /  擅长学习和说外语的人
PART 3
1. Do many people in your country speak foreign
languages?
你们国家会说外语的人多吗？ 区分学校学过与能交谈，用城
市工作环境解释使用机会差异。
Many people in China have studied English, but
studying a language and speaking it comfortably aren't
the same thing. People who use it at work or university
often get more practice. In my daily life, I meet some
confident speakers and others who understand written
English better than conversation, so ability varies quite
widely.
中国很多人学过英语，但学过和能自在交谈并不是一回事。
在工作或大学里使用英语的人，往往练习更多。日常中，我
既认识说得自信的人，也认识读英文比听懂对话更擅长的人，
因此能力差异很大。
get more practice 获得更多练习
2. Can speaking another language be useful at work?
会说其他语言对工作有帮助吗？ 用直接沟通减少误会解释帮
助，同时保留工作是否需要的条件。
Yes, especially when a job involves customers or
colleagues from other countries. Being able to discuss a
problem directly can save time and avoid
misunderstandings. A hotel employee, for instance, may
explain a guest's options more clearly. The benefit
depends on the role, though; not every worker needs a
foreign language every day.
有帮助，尤其是工作涉及外国客户或同事时。直接讨论问题
能节省时间、减少误会。例如酒店员工可以更清楚地向客人
解释选择。不过，好处取决于岗位，并不是每位员工每天都
需要用外语。
avoid misunderstandings 避免误会
3. Do people study foreign languages besides English?
人们会学习英语之外的外语吗？ 给出留学、工作和兴趣三类
动机，避免声称各语言学习人数排名。
Certainly. Some learn Japanese or Korean because they
enjoy films, music or games in those languages. Others
choose French, German or another language for study
and work. Personal relationships can be a strong reason
too. If someone's partner or close friend speaks a
different language, everyday communication may
provide a very clear motivation to learn.
当然。有些人因喜欢电影、音乐或游戏而学日语、韩语；也
有人为了学习和工作选择法语、德语等。个人关系也是很强
的动力。如果伴侣或好友说另一种语言，日常交流就会成为
很明确的学习理由。
a strong reason 很有力的理由
4. Why can learning new things be easier for children
than adults?
为什么孩子学习新事物有时比成年人容易？ 不把年龄当唯一
原因，重点说明练习环境和对自己出错的顾虑。
Children often have more time set aside for learning and
fewer worries about looking inexperienced. They may
repeat a game or phrase many times without getting
bored. Adults can learn effectively too, especially when
they understand the purpose. The difference often comes
from practice, confidence and available time, rather than
age being the whole explanation.
孩子通常有更多专门用于学习的时间，也较少担心显得没经
验。他们可能多次重复游戏或词句而不觉得无聊。成年人也
能有效学习，尤其理解目的时。差异常来自练习、信心和可
用时间，年龄并不能解释一切。
set aside time 留出时间
5. What are some ways people learn something new?
人们可以通过哪些方式学习新事物？ 按示范、亲手尝试和获
得反馈的顺序说明过程，用修车连接各步骤。
People learn by watching demonstrations, trying things
themselves and getting feedback. The best combination
depends on the task. To fix a bicycle puncture, a short
video might show the order of steps, but actually
handling the tyre reveals what feels difficult. Someone
experienced can then correct the mistake that the video
didn't help them notice.
人们通过看示范、自己尝试和获得反馈来学习，最佳组合取
决于任务。修自行车轮胎时，短视频能展示步骤，但亲手处
理轮胎才知道哪里困难。有经验的人随后可以指出视频没让
学习者注意到的错误。
get feedback 获得反馈

sections.titleEn: Someone who taught me a skill
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
学习技能与培养兴趣
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
121
话题 83
PART 2
教你新技能的人
Someone who taught me a skill
Describe a person who helped you learn a new skill.
描述一位教过你新技能的人。
1. Who taught you
教你的人是谁
2. What skill you learned
你学了什么技能
3. How the person taught you
对方如何教你
4. How you felt about learning it
学习这项技能让你有什么感受
审题与选材：人物题要让教法看得见：对方先示范什么、注意到你哪里做错、怎样调整难度。选择一项简单技能也可以讲得
充实。说明自己从不会到能独立完成的变化，再把感激或自信与具体结果相连，避免只夸老师耐心而没有细节。
叙述顺序
A 介绍小时候教我缝扣子的姑姑 - B 说明校服扣子掉落的起因 - C 描述她用大针和布料示范 - D 讲她怎样纠正拉线的力度
- E 用自己缝好的扣子说明感受
A Introduce my aunt as my childhood teacher - B Explain the missing button on my uniform - C Describe her
demonstration with simple practice materials - D Show her correction of my pulling technique - E Recall my pride in the
finished repair
示例回答
My aunt taught me how to sew on a button when I was about ten. She lived nearby, and I often spent Saturday
afternoons at her flat while my parents were working. One day, a button came off my school shirt. I asked her to
fix it, expecting to hand it over and go back to watching television. Instead, she suggested that I learn to do it
myself. She didn't begin with the shirt. She gave me a scrap of thick fabric, a large button and a needle that was
easy to hold. First, she showed me how to thread it and make a knot. Then she stitched slowly while explaining
where the needle should go. When I pulled the thread too tightly, the fabric gathered into a little bump. She
didn't take the work away from me. She loosened one stitch and let me try again, showing me how to leave a
little space under the button. After practising, I repaired the actual shirt. The stitches weren't perfectly neat, but
the button stayed firmly in place. I felt surprisingly capable. What I appreciated about my aunt was that she gave
me enough help to succeed without doing the whole job for me.
中文对照：我大约十岁时，姑姑教我缝扣子。她住得近，父母周六工作时，我常去她家过下午。有一天，我校服衬衫的扣
子掉了。我本想交给她修好，自己继续看电视，她却建议让我学着自己做。她没有直接拿衬衫教学，而是给我一块厚布、
一枚大扣子和一根好拿的针。她先示范穿线打结，再慢慢缝，解释针应该从哪里穿过去。我把线拉得太紧，布皱成了一个
小包。她没有拿走我的活，而是松开一针，让我重试，并教我在扣子下面留一点空隙。练习后，我修好了真正的衬衫。针
脚不算整齐，但扣子牢牢留在原处。我突然觉得自己挺能干。我感激姑姑，因为她提供了足够的帮助让我成功，却没有替
我包办整件事。
自然表达
sew on a button
缝上扣子
a scrap of fabric
一小块布料
stay in place
保持在原位
take the work away
把活拿走代做

Because I learned this at ten, the same afternoon could illustrate a practical skill I gained during childhood.

122
话题 83  /  教你新技能的人
PART 3
1. Why is it useful for children to learn new skills?
孩子学习新技能为什么有用？ 用可独立完成的小事解释自信
来源，不把所有技能都说成升学工具。
New skills give children more ways to manage everyday
situations and enjoy their interests. Learning to tie a knot
or prepare a simple snack can make them less dependent
on adults. They also discover that improvement takes
practice. That experience can build confidence, because
they remember doing something successfully that once
seemed difficult.
新技能让孩子能处理更多日常情况，也能享受兴趣。学会打
结或准备简单点心，可以减少对成年人的依赖。他们也会发
现进步需要练习。这种经历能建立信心，因为他们记得自己
成功做过原本觉得困难的事。
less dependent on 较少依赖
2. Where can children develop new skills?
孩子可以在哪里学习新技能？ 不局限培训班，分别说明家庭、
学校与社区各自能提供什么机会。
They can learn at home, at school and through
community activities. Each setting offers different
opportunities. A parent might teach basic cooking, a
school can provide science equipment, and a local club
may offer team sports. Informal learning matters too:
helping a neighbour organise books can teach sorting,
planning and working carefully with someone else.
孩子可以在家里、学校和社区活动中学习。不同地方提供不
同机会：父母教简单烹饪，学校提供科学器材，社区俱乐部
安排团队运动。非正式学习也重要，例如帮邻居整理书籍，
能学分类、安排和认真合作。
informal learning 非正式学习
3. How can parents and teachers teach children new
skills?
父母和老师可以怎样教孩子新技能？ 强调分步示范后让孩子
操作，并解释一次纠正太多为何会混乱。
Adults should break the task into small steps,
demonstrate clearly and let children try. It's tempting to
take over when progress is slow, but that removes the
practice they need. Correcting one important mistake at a
time also helps. For example, when teaching cutting,
focus first on safe handling before expecting a perfectly
straight edge.
成年人应把任务分成小步骤，清楚示范，再让孩子尝试。进
展慢时很容易想接手，但这样会剥夺必要练习。一次纠正一
个重要错误也有帮助。例如教剪东西时，先关注安全握法，
再要求边缘完全笔直。
take over 接手代做
4. How do adults usually approach learning a new
skill?
成年人通常怎样学习新技能？ 说明目标具体与时间有限如何
影响方法，用工作需要带动练习。
Adults often start with a particular problem they want to
solve, so practical courses and tutorials can be appealing.
Someone learning spreadsheets may practise with their
own household budget. Time is usually limited, which
makes short, regular sessions useful. Getting feedback
from a colleague or teacher can prevent them from
repeatedly practising the same mistake.
成年人常从想解决的具体问题出发，因此实用课程和教程有
吸引力。学电子表格的人可以拿自家预算练习。时间通常有
限，所以短时、规律的学习有用。请同事或老师反馈，能避
免反复练习同一个错误。
short, regular sessions 短时而规律的练习
5. How does learning with a teacher differ from
studying alone?
跟老师学习和自学有什么不同？ 比较及时纠错与自由安排，
说明适合方式取决于任务和基础。
A teacher can spot mistakes you don't recognise and
adjust explanations to your needs. Studying alone gives
you more control over pace, timing and materials. For a
beginner learning a physical skill, direct feedback may
be especially useful. For someone reviewing familiar
software, independent practice might be enough, with
occasional help when they get stuck.
老师能发现自己没意识到的错误，并调整解释方式。自学则
能自主控制进度、时间和材料。初学身体技能的人，可能特
别需要直接反馈；复习熟悉软件的人，独立练习也许就够了，
卡住时再偶尔求助。
get stuck 卡住；遇到困难
6. Why does learning a skill require self-discipline?
学习技能为什么需要自律？ 解释新鲜感退去后仍要重复基础
练习，用短时安排体现坚持。
Progress often depends on repeating basic exercises after
the initial excitement has worn off. Self-discipline helps
someone practise even when a video or game seems
more appealing. It doesn't have to mean a strict daily
schedule. Keeping a small promise, such as practising
guitar for ten minutes after dinner, can make learning
more consistent.
进步常需要在最初兴奋消退后继续重复基础练习。即使视频
或游戏更诱人，自律也能帮助人去练习。这不一定意味着严
格的日程。守住一个小承诺，例如晚饭后练十分钟吉他，就
能让学习更稳定。
wear off 逐渐消退

sections.title: 小时候学的新技能
sections.titleEn: A skill I learned as a child
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
学习技能与培养兴趣
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
123
话题 84
PART 2
小时候学的新技能
A skill I learned as a child
Describe a new skill you learned during childhood.
描述一项你在童年学会的新技能。
1. What the skill was
是什么技能
2. Who taught you
谁教了你
3. How they taught you
对方怎样教你
4. How you felt about learning it
你学习时有什么感受
审题与选材：童年时间点必须明确，技能应有可以验证的完成动作，例如自己缝好一枚扣子。讲清教学顺序和第一次尝试的
错误，再用实际成果说明情绪变化。不必把小技能写成重大人生转折，日常能少麻烦家人就是可信的收获。
叙述顺序
A 说明十岁学会自己缝扣子 - B 交代姑姑看到校服缺扣子 - C 描述先拿厚布练穿针缝线 - D 讲拉线过紧后重新尝试
- E 说明独立修好衣服的满足
A Identify sewing buttons as a childhood skill - B Introduce my aunt and the damaged shirt - C Practise threading and
stitching on spare fabric - D Describe correcting my overly tight stitches - E Explain the satisfaction of repairing my clothes
示例回答
A useful skill I learned as a child was sewing a button onto a shirt. I was about ten, and my aunt taught me one
Saturday afternoon at her home. It started because a button had fallen off my school uniform. Usually, I would
have waited for an adult to repair it. My aunt thought this was a good chance to show me something I could
handle myself. She found a large button and a piece of spare fabric so I wouldn't worry about ruining my shirt.
She demonstrated threading the needle, making a knot and passing the needle through two holes in the button.
Then she let me copy each step while she watched. My first attempt wasn't great. I pulled so hard that the fabric
became wrinkled, and the button wouldn't sit flat. She helped me undo a few stitches and explained that the
thread needed to be secure without squeezing everything together. Eventually, I managed to attach the real
button to my shirt. I tested it several times, half expecting it to fall off again, but it held. I felt pleased because I
had fixed a real problem, not just completed an exercise. Even now, replacing a missing button reminds me how
satisfying a small practical skill can be.
中文对照：我小时候学会的一项实用技能是给衬衫缝扣子。大约十岁时，姑姑在一个周六下午于她家教会了我。起因是校
服掉了一枚扣子。平时我会等大人修，但姑姑觉得这是教我自己处理的好机会。她找来大扣子和备用布料，让我不用怕弄
坏衬衫。她示范穿针、打结，再从扣子的两个孔来回缝，然后看着我逐步模仿。第一次并不好。我拉得太用力，布料起皱，
扣子也放不平。她帮我拆了几针，解释线需要牢固，却不能把一切挤在一起。最后，我把真正的扣子缝回了衬衫。我试了
好几次，仍有点担心它会掉，但它一直很牢。我很开心，因为解决了实际问题，而不只是完成练习。现在每次补上掉落的
扣子，我仍会想到，小小的实用技能也能让人很满足。
自然表达
spare fabric
备用布料
sit flat
平整地贴着
undo a few stitches
拆开几针
attach a button
缝上扣子
串题 话题 83 教你新技能的人
仍可使用姑姑和同一次缝扣子的学习，转为教技能的人题时，多讲她怎样观察错误、示范和鼓励，减少只讲自己反复练习的
部分。
My aunt could be the focus instead, with more detail about how she noticed mistakes and adjusted her teaching.

话题 84  /  小时候学的新技能
PART 3
1. Which skills should children learn before they
begin school?
孩子入学前应该学会哪些技能？ 优先生活自理与表达需要，
说明这些如何帮助适应集体生活。
Basic independence is more useful than getting far ahead
academically. Children benefit from washing their
hands, putting belongings away and telling an adult
when they need help. Taking turns and listening to a
short instruction also matter. These skills make the
school day less confusing and leave children more
energy for making friends and exploring.
比起在学业上提前很多，基本独立能力更有用。孩子应学会
洗手、收拾物品，并在需要时告诉大人。轮流参与、听懂简
短指令也重要。这些技能能减少校园生活中的困惑，让他们
有更多精力交友和探索。
take turns 轮流
2. Can children teach one another new skills?
孩子能从同伴那里学到新技能吗？ 用容易模仿和敢于尝试解
释同伴学习，同时指出错误也会传播。
Yes, and sometimes they're more willing to try after
watching another child. A classmate explaining a
skipping game may use simpler words than an adult
would. Practising together also makes repetition
enjoyable. Still, children can pass on mistakes, so an
adult should check activities involving tools, physical
risks or information that needs to be accurate.
能，有时看到另一个孩子做，自己更愿意尝试。同学讲跳绳
游戏，可能用比成人更简单的话，一起练也让重复更有趣。
不过，孩子也可能传递错误，因此涉及工具、身体风险或准
确知识的活动，应由成年人检查。
pass on mistakes 把错误传给别人
3. How does adult learning differ from children's
learning?
成年人学习与儿童学习有哪些主要区别？ 从已有经验、学习
目的与活动安排作比较，避免绝对化能力差距。
Adults often bring useful experience and a clear reason
for learning, but they may have less free time. Children
usually need more structure and learn well through play
and repeated practice. An adult might connect a new
budgeting skill to household bills, while a child could
understand the same idea through a pretend shop.
成年人常有可利用的经验和明确目的，但空闲时间可能较少。
孩子通常需要更多安排，通过游戏和重复练习学得不错。成
人可能把预算技能与家庭账单联系起来，而孩子可以通过模
拟商店理解同样的概念。
a clear reason 明确的理由
4. Should children learn practical skills such as
cooking and cleaning?
孩子应该学习做饭、清洁等实用技能吗？ 先肯定适龄参与，
再用准备点心与清洁桌面说明责任和安全。
Yes, with tasks suited to their age. Preparing a simple
snack or wiping a table helps children contribute to
family life and understand the work adults do. It also
makes everyday independence less intimidating later.
They need supervision around heat and sharp tools, but
being protected shouldn't mean never being allowed to
help at all.
应该，任务要适合年龄。准备简单点心或擦桌子，能让孩子
参与家庭生活，理解大人所做的劳动，也让将来的日常独立
没那么可怕。接触热源和锐利工具时需要监督，但保护不应
变成完全不让他们帮忙。
contribute to family life 参与家庭生活
5. Is home or school a better place for children to
learn skills?
孩子在家还是在学校学技能更好？ 依据技能需要的设备和练
习频率分工，不选脱离情境的单一答案。
Both have strengths. Home is ideal for routines children
can practise often, such as preparing food or organising
clothes. School offers equipment, trained teachers and
classmates to work with. A child might learn basic
sewing at school, then repair a loose button at home. The
two settings work best when they reinforce each other.
两者各有优势。家里适合经常练习的日常任务，如准备食物、
整理衣服；学校有设备、受训老师和合作同伴。孩子可以在
学校学基础缝纫，回家修松掉的扣子。两种环境相互巩固时，
效果最好。
reinforce each other 相互巩固

sections.title: 令人印象深刻的课程
sections.titleEn: A course that made a strong impression
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
学习技能与培养兴趣
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
125
话题 85
PART 2
令人印象深刻的课程
A course that made a strong impression
Describe a course that impressed you greatly.
描述一门让你印象深刻的课程。
1. What the course covered
课程教什么
2. Where you attended it
你在哪里上课
3. What you did in the course
你在课上做了什么
4. Why it made such a strong impression
它为什么让你印象深刻
审题与选材：先用一项具体学习成果说明课程内容，随后讲地点和课堂活动。令人印象深刻可以来自一个立即看见效果的小
练习，不一定是昂贵课程或知名老师。把上课前的误解与练习后的发现对照，说明课程怎样改变了你的实际做法。
叙述顺序
A 介绍社区中心的手机摄影课 - B 说明原先以为必须买相机 - C 描述窗边拍杯子的对比练习 - D 讲同学交换照片提出建议
- E 用照片变化解释课程的价值
A Introduce a community course in phone photography - B Explain my assumption about needing expensive equipment
- C Compare photographs of a cup beside windows - D Exchange pictures and suggestions with other learners - E Explain
what changed in my own photographs
示例回答
A short phone photography course at our community centre impressed me much more than I expected. It ran over
two Saturday afternoons, and I joined because my pictures often looked flat even when the scene itself was
beautiful. Before the course, I assumed better photographs mainly required a better camera. The teacher
challenged that idea with a very simple exercise. She put a plain white cup on a table and asked everyone to
photograph it from their seats. Then we moved the cup beside a window and changed our positions. The side light
made the handle and curved surface much clearer. We hadn't changed phones or used special filters, yet the
second photograph looked completely different. We also went outside in pairs to photograph something ordinary,
like a doorway or a bicycle. Afterwards, we showed each other the pictures and explained what we had chosen to
include or leave out. That discussion was useful because I began noticing distracting objects at the edges of my
photos. What impressed me was how quickly the advice became visible. There was very little technical language,
and every explanation led to something we could try ourselves. I still use the window exercise when
photographing food or small objects at home, so the course changed an everyday habit.
中文对照：社区中心的一门手机摄影短课，比我预想的更让我印象深刻。课程上了两个周六下午。我报名是因为眼前景色
很美，自己拍的照片却经常很平淡。上课前，我以为好照片主要需要好相机。老师用一个简单练习改变了我的想法：她把
白杯子放在桌上，让大家从座位拍。随后，我们把杯子移到窗边，改变拍摄位置。侧面的光让把手和弧形杯身清楚很多。
没有换手机或用特殊滤镜，第二张照片却完全不同。我们还两人一组到室外，拍门口、自行车等普通东西，再互看照片，
解释选择保留或排除什么。这种讨论很有用，我开始留意照片边缘分散注意力的东西。最让我印象深刻的是，建议的效果
很快就看得见。课程技术术语很少，每个解释都连着亲手尝试。我现在在家拍食物或小物件，仍会用窗边练习，所以课程
改变了我的日常习惯。
自然表达
look flat
看起来缺乏层次
side light
侧光
leave out
排除；不包括
distracting objects
分散注意力的物体
串题 话题 83 教你新技能的人
摄影课的窗边示范可以转到教技能的人题，保留杯子和光线变化；补充老师如何看出你的问题、指导重拍，把重点放在教法
上。
The teacher's window exercise could illustrate good teaching if I explain how she helped me correct my own photograph.


25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
学习技能与培养兴趣
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
126
话题 85  /  令人印象深刻的课程
PART 3
1. What kinds of things must people remember day to
day?
人们日常生活中需要记住哪些事情？ 把约定、任务和物品位
置分类，用忘记后的具体影响解释优先级。
People need to remember appointments, unfinished tasks
and practical details such as where they left important
items. They may also need to keep promises to others,
like collecting a child or returning a borrowed book. Not
everything deserves equal mental effort. I would write
down routine deadlines so I can focus on conversations
and current work.
人们要记住约会、未完成任务，以及重要物品放在哪里等细
节，还要记得对别人的承诺，如接孩子、还借来的书。不是
每件事都值得占用同样精力。我会写下常规截止时间，以便
专注眼前交谈和工作。
keep promises 遵守承诺
2. What lessons can studying history teach us?
学习历史能让我们得到什么启发？ 从生活变化和选择后果谈
理解，避免声称历史能直接预测未来。
History can show how ordinary lives were shaped by
decisions about work, housing and education. It also
reminds us that arrangements we consider normal were
not always the same. Looking at earlier mistakes may
improve our questions about present choices. That
doesn't mean history supplies ready-made answers,
because circumstances can be very different now.
历史能展示工作、住房和教育方面的决定怎样影响普通生活，
也提醒我们，如今习以为常的安排并非一直如此。研究过去
的错误，有助于更好地审视当前选择，但历史不提供现成答
案，因为如今情况可能很不同。
ready-made answers 现成答案
3. Why do some people remember things better than
others?
为什么有些人的记忆力比别人好？ 重点解释注意与反复使用
的差异，不把记忆表现都归于天赋。
Some differences may be individual, but attention and
practice matter a lot. People often remember information
connected to an interest because they notice details and
revisit them. A football fan may recall scores easily
while forgetting shopping items. Useful habits, such as
linking a new name to a face and reviewing it later, can
also help.
个人差异可能有影响，但注意和练习也很重要。人们容易记
住与兴趣有关的信息，因为会注意细节并反复接触。球迷能
记住比分，却可能忘购物清单。把新名字与脸联系、之后再
回想等习惯，也有帮助。
attention and practice 专注与练习
4. Do words or photographs help people remember
more effectively?
文字和照片，哪种更有助于记忆？ 依据信息类型比较，说明
照片适合外观而文字更适合准确指令。
It depends on what needs remembering. A photograph is
useful for a place, a face or the arrangement of objects.
Words are usually better for exact instructions or a
reason something happened. Combining them can work
particularly well: a photo of a museum object with a
short note may preserve more meaning than either one
alone.
这取决于要记什么。照片适合地点、人脸或物品摆放，文字
通常更适合准确指令或事情发生的原因。两者结合尤其有用：
博物馆物品照片配简短说明，可能比单独用其中一种保留更
多含义。
exact instructions 准确的指令
5. Can technology improve remembering, and how?
科技能帮助人们记忆吗？具体怎样帮助？ 区分外部提醒与真
正学会，用提醒事项和复习安排分别说明。
Yes, technology can support both reminders and
learning. A calendar alert helps someone remember an
appointment at the right moment, while a study app can
prompt them to review forgotten material. Those are
different kinds of help. Saving information isn't the same
as learning it, so people still need to pay attention and
actively recall things.
能，科技既可提醒，也可辅助学习。日历通知能在合适时刻
提醒约会，学习软件则提示复习遗忘内容。这是两种不同帮
助。保存信息不等于学会，因此人仍需认真关注，并主动回
忆内容。
actively recall 主动回忆

sections.title: 一个有趣的生物知识
sections.titleEn: Something interesting I learned about biology
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
学习技能与培养兴趣
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
127
话题 86
PART 2
一个有趣的生物知识
Something interesting I learned about biology
Describe an interesting thing you learned about biology.
描述一项你学到的有趣生物知识。
1. What you learned
你学到了什么
2. When you learned it
什么时候学到的
3. How you found out about it
通过什么方式学到的
4. Why it interested you
为什么觉得有趣
5. Whether it changed your view of nature
它是否改变了你对自然的看法
审题与选材：选择一个能准确解释的小现象，不必把答案变成科普讲座。时间和学习途径要明确，再用观察细节说明兴趣来
源。最后回答看法是否改变，可以只是从觉得植物静止不动，到开始注意它们缓慢的生长，变化不需要夸张。
叙述顺序
A 交代去年春天观察豆子发芽 - B 说明姑姑用湿纸巾做实验 - C 描述根先出现随后长出芽 - D 解释照片对比为何令人惊讶
- E 讲自己开始留意缓慢变化
A Introduce learning about germination last spring - B Describe my aunt's damp paper experiment - C Observe the root
appearing before the shoot - D Explain the surprise of comparing daily photographs - E Connect the experiment with noticing
slow changes
示例回答
Something interesting I learned about biology was how a bean seed begins to grow. I knew plants came from
seeds, of course, but I'd never paid attention to what happened before the leaves appeared. I learned about it last
spring when my aunt was growing beans on her balcony. She put a few seeds against damp paper inside a clear
container so we could watch them without digging through soil. She explained that the first little part pushing out
was a root, not a stem. I took a photograph each morning. At first, the seed only seemed slightly larger. Then its
outer covering split, a pale root appeared and, later, a shoot began growing upwards. Comparing the photographs
made the changes much easier to notice than simply staring at the container. What interested me was that so much
was happening before there was anything that looked like a familiar green plant. I'd always thought of a seed as
something inactive until leaves suddenly arrived. It changed my view of nature in a small but lasting way. I began
noticing slow processes rather than only finished results, like flowers or fruit. Now, when I walk past my aunt's
pots, I usually stop to see what's different instead of just asking when we can eat something.
中文对照：我学到的一项有趣生物知识，是豆类种子怎样开始生长。我当然知道植物来自种子，却从没注意过叶子出现前
发生什么。去年春天，姑姑在阳台种豆子，把几颗种子放在透明容器里的湿纸巾旁，让我们不用挖土也能观察。她解释，
最先伸出的小部分是根，不是茎。我每天早晨拍照。起初，种子只是稍微变大；后来外皮裂开，浅色的根出现，再后来芽
向上长。比较照片比一直盯着容器更容易发现变化。让我感兴趣的是，在它看起来像熟悉的绿色植物之前，已经发生了那
么多事。我以前觉得种子是不动的，直到叶子突然出现。这件事以小而持久的方式改变了我看自然的角度。我开始关注缓
慢过程，而不只看花和果实等结果。现在经过姑姑的花盆，我常停下看看有什么变化，不再只问什么时候能吃。
自然表达
pay attention to
留意
push out
伸出来
outer covering
外层表皮
slow processes
缓慢的过程
串题 话题 91 喜欢种植物的人
豆子发芽的观察可连接喜欢种植物的人题，保留姑姑和阳台；另须介绍她长期种哪些植物、怎样照料，以及她享受种植的原
因。
My aunt introduced this experiment, and her balcony routine could also explain why she enjoys growing plants.

学习技能与培养兴趣
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
128
话题 86  /  一个有趣的生物知识
PART 3
1. Are children interested in studying biology?
孩子对学习生物感兴趣吗？ 把具体观察和抽象背诵区分，用
种子变化解释兴趣怎样出现。
Many are curious about living things, especially when
they can observe something directly. Watching a seed
open or comparing leaves can raise questions naturally.
Interest may disappear if biology is presented only as
unfamiliar terms to memorise. I think practical
observation gives children a reason to care about the
explanation before they learn the vocabulary.
很多孩子对生命有好奇心，尤其能亲眼观察时。看种子裂开
或比较叶片，会自然产生问题。如果生物课只是背陌生术语，
兴趣可能消失。我觉得实际观察能让孩子先在意解释，再去
学习相关词汇。
living things 生物
2. Why are animals so interesting to many children?
为什么很多孩子对动物感兴趣？ 用可见动作与同人类的相似
差异解释吸引力，避免泛泛说可爱。
Animals move, make sounds and respond to their
surroundings, so they give children plenty to notice.
Some behaviour is familiar, like sleeping or caring for
young, while other behaviour seems surprising. A bird
building a nest can lead to questions about homes and
families. That mixture of familiarity and difference
makes animals engaging subjects.
动物会移动、发声、回应周围环境，给孩子很多可观察的东
西。有些行为熟悉，如睡觉、照顾幼崽，有些又令人惊讶。
一只筑巢的鸟就能引出关于住所和家庭的问题。这种熟悉与
不同的结合，让动物很有吸引力。
respond to their surroundings 回应周围环境
3. Should schools provide more biology education?
学校应该增加生物教育吗？ 把更多理解与更多课时分开，重
点给出现有课程可改进的活动。
I'd support more opportunities to understand living
things, though that doesn't necessarily mean adding more
textbook hours. A small school garden or regular
observations of local plants could make existing lessons
clearer. Children should learn to ask questions and
record what they see. That seems more valuable than
simply expanding the list of facts they must memorise.
我支持增加理解生物的机会，但未必是增加读课本的课时。
学校小花园或定期观察本地植物，可以让现有课程更清楚。
孩子应学会提问、记录观察，这比单纯增加必须背诵的事实
清单更有价值。
record what they see 记录观察到的东西
4. Can visits to zoos and museums help children learn
biology?
参观动物园和博物馆能帮助孩子学习生物吗？ 分别说明观察
活体与比较标本的作用，再给教师提问的具体价值。
Yes, if the visit includes time to observe and ask
questions. A zoo can show movement and behaviour,
while a museum can display skeletons or specimens for
comparison. Simply walking past labels may teach very
little. A focused task, such as comparing how two
animals move, helps children connect what they see with
a biological idea.
能，前提是有时间观察和提问。动物园能展示动作和行为，
博物馆则可提供骨架或标本供比较。只是走过标签可能学不
到什么。安排集中任务，如比较两种动物怎样移动，能帮助
孩子把所见与生物概念联系起来。
for comparison 供比较

sections.title: 一个喜欢历史的人
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
学习技能与培养兴趣
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
129
话题 87
PART 2
一个喜欢历史的人
Someone who enjoys history
Describe a person you know who is interested in history.
描述一位你认识的、对历史感兴趣的人。
1. Who the person is
这个人是谁
2. How you know them
你怎样认识对方
3. Which area of history interests them
对方对哪类历史感兴趣
4. Why they enjoy learning about it
对方为什么喜欢历史
审题与选材：历史兴趣最好限定到一个领域，如家乡街道、普通人的日常生活或交通变化。认识经过可以简短交代，把篇幅
留给对方如何查找和核对信息。喜欢历史的原因应来自他的说法或长期行为，不要用背得出很多年代代替兴趣本身。
叙述顺序
A 介绍退休邻居周先生的爱好 - B 交代帮他搬书时开始熟悉 - C 说明他关注本地街道历史 - D 讲旧照片和地图怎样互相核对
- E 解释他想保留普通人的记忆
A Introduce Mr Zhou, my retired neighbour - B Recall getting acquainted while moving his books - C Identify his interest in
local street history - D Describe comparing old photographs with street maps - E Explain his wish to preserve ordinary
memories
示例回答
My neighbour Mr Zhou is very interested in history, particularly the history of our town's streets. He's retired
now, and I got to know him when I helped carry some boxes of books into his flat. Among the books were old
maps and albums of local photographs. He showed me a picture of a narrow lane and asked if I recognised it. I
didn't, because the lane is now a busy road lined with shops. What he enjoys most isn't memorising rulers or
battles. He wants to understand how ordinary people lived: where they bought food, how they travelled and why
certain buildings disappeared. He compares photographs with maps and sometimes asks older residents to check
details. Once, two neighbours remembered the opening of a market differently. Rather than choosing the more
confident speaker, he looked for a dated photograph and explained what it could and couldn't prove. I liked that
careful approach. He says history helps him understand why the town looks the way it does. It also preserves
memories that younger people might never hear at home. When I walk with him, an ordinary corner can turn into
a story about a workshop, a family or an old bus stop. That's made our neighbourhood much more interesting to
me.
中文对照：我的邻居周先生很喜欢历史，尤其是本地街道的历史。他已经退休，我帮他把几箱书搬进家里时，开始和他熟
悉起来。书中有旧地图和本地照片集。他给我看一条窄巷的照片，问我认不认识。我没认出来，因为那里如今已是商铺林
立的繁忙道路。他最喜欢的不是背统治者或战争，而是了解普通人怎样生活：在哪里买食物、怎样出行，以及建筑为什么
消失。他把照片与地图对照，有时请年长居民核实细节。有次两位邻居记得的市场开业时间不同，他没有直接相信说话更
肯定的人，而是寻找有日期的照片，解释它能证明什么、不能证明什么。我喜欢这种认真态度。他说历史帮助他理解小镇
为何变成如今这样，也保存年轻人在家里未必能听到的记忆。与他散步时，普通街角会变成关于作坊、家庭或旧车站的故
事，让我觉得社区有趣多了。
自然表达
get to know
逐渐认识
check details
核实细节
a careful approach
谨慎认真的做法
preserve memories
保存记忆
串题 话题 66 一个比你年长且让你佩服的人
周先生是年长邻居，可转为佩服的老人题；保留核对照片和尊重证据的故事，重点说明这种认真做法为何值得欣赏，而非只
说爱历史。
His interest in history could introduce him, while his careful checking would explain why I admire this older neighbour.

学习技能与培养兴趣
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
130
话题 87  /  一个喜欢历史的人
PART 3
1. Do you enjoy learning about history yourself?
你自己喜欢学习历史吗？ 直接表达偏好并限定喜欢的内容，
用身边旧物说明个人兴趣。
Yes, especially when it explains familiar places or
everyday objects. I find an old street map more engaging
than a long list of dates because I can compare it with
somewhere I know. Stories about housing, transport and
family routines help me picture people's lives. I'm less
enthusiastic when learning means memorising names
without any context.
喜欢，尤其是能解释熟悉地方或日常物件的历史。旧街道地
图比长串日期更吸引我，因为能与认识的地方比较。住房、
交通和家庭日常的故事，让我想象过去的生活。如果只是脱
离背景背名字，我就没那么有兴趣。
without any context 没有任何背景
2. Do school students generally enjoy studying
history?
学生通常喜欢学校里的历史课吗？ 指出兴趣因授课方式而异，
用围绕证据的讨论与背诵任务作对照。
Some do, but much depends on how the subject is
taught. A lesson built around a letter, photograph or
disputed decision can invite curiosity and discussion.
Constantly memorising dates may feel less rewarding.
Students also have different interests, so including
ordinary life alongside political events can give more of
them a way into the subject.
有些喜欢，但很大程度取决于教法。围绕信件、照片或有争
议的决定展开的课，能激起好奇和讨论。不断背日期可能让
人缺少收获感。学生兴趣不同，在政治事件之外加入日常生
活，也能让更多人进入这个学科。
invite curiosity 激起好奇
3. Should children begin learning history while they
are young?
孩子应该从小学习历史吗？ 先肯定接触过去的价值，再把初
期内容限制为孩子能理解的人和物。
Yes, provided the material suits their understanding.
Young children can explore family photographs, old toys
or changes in their own neighbourhood. These examples
introduce the idea that life was different before they
were born. They don't need complicated political
explanations immediately. Starting with people and
objects they recognise can make later historical learning
less abstract.
应该，前提是内容适合他们理解。小孩子可以看家庭照片、
旧玩具或社区变化，理解自己出生前的生活并不一样。他们
不必立即接触复杂政治解释。从认识的人和物开始，能让以
后学历史时不那么抽象。
suit their understanding 适合他们的理解程度
4. At what age would you introduce children to
history?
你会从几岁开始让孩子接触历史？ 给出大致年龄并区分接触
故事与正式学习，不把年龄说成硬门槛。
Around four or five seems reasonable for simple stories
about the past, though children develop at different
speeds. At that age, family photographs can introduce
ideas like older and newer. More organised timelines can
come later, once they understand sequence better. I'd
choose the level by their questions and understanding,
rather than enforce one exact starting age.
四五岁左右可以开始听简单的过去故事，不过孩子发展速度
不同。那时家庭照片能帮助理解旧与新。等顺序概念更清楚
后，再用较有条理的时间线。我会根据提问和理解程度选内
容，而不规定统一的精确起始年龄。
at different speeds 以不同速度


25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
学习技能与培养兴趣
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
131
话题 87  /  一个喜欢历史的人
PART 3
5. Who can introduce history to preschool children?
学龄前儿童可以由谁来启蒙历史？ 说明家人、照护者和讲解
员各自材料来源，并提醒区分记忆与证据。
Parents, grandparents and nursery teachers can all help.
Family members can connect stories to familiar people,
while teachers may use picture books and simple objects.
Museum educators can offer activities designed for
young visitors. Adults should make clear when they're
sharing a personal memory rather than a confirmed fact,
since even vivid memories can be mistaken.
父母、祖辈和幼儿园老师都能帮助。家人可把故事连到熟悉
的人，老师可以用绘本和简单物件，博物馆讲解员能安排儿
童活动。成年人应说明哪些是个人回忆，哪些是确认的事实，
因为生动记忆也可能出错。
a personal memory 个人回忆
6. Is it important to understand how people lived in
the past?
了解过去的人怎样生活重要吗？ 把生活条件与人物选择联系，
解释为什么不能只用今天的标准判断。
Yes, because daily conditions help explain people's
choices. Understanding how long travel took or how
families earned money makes historical decisions easier
to interpret. It can also challenge the assumption that
everyone lived like we do now. Learning about ordinary
routines brings us closer to people in the past without
pretending their circumstances were identical to ours.
重要，因为日常条件有助解释人的选择。了解出行要多久、
家庭如何谋生，会让过去的决定更容易理解，也能打破人人
都像我们这样生活的假设。学习普通日常让我们接近过去的
人，同时承认他们的处境与今天不同。
daily conditions 日常生活条件
7. Should ancient history be studied before modern
history?
学习现代史之前应该先学古代史吗？ 承认时间顺序的帮助，
同时解释从熟悉问题往前追溯也能学习。
Not necessarily. Chronological order can make
long-term changes easier to follow, but a recent event or
familiar building may be a more engaging starting point.
A teacher could begin there and trace its background
backwards. What matters is helping learners understand
connections and sequence, rather than making them
finish every ancient period before discussing anything
modern.
不一定。按时间顺序学，确实更容易理解长期变化，但近代
事件或熟悉建筑可能是更有吸引力的起点。老师可从那里往
前追溯。关键是让学习者理解联系和顺序，而非学完所有古
代时期才能谈现代内容。
trace its background 追溯其背景

sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
学习技能与培养兴趣
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
132
话题 88
PART 2
擅长做手工的人
Someone who makes special objects
Describe someone who creates special objects by hand or with technology.
描述一位用手工或技术制作特别物品的人。
1. Who the person is
这个人是谁
2. How you came to know them
你怎样认识对方
3. What they make
对方制作什么
4. How you feel about this person
你对这个人的感受
审题与选材：特别之处可以是为某人定制、重新利用材料或细致的制作步骤，不必依赖昂贵技术。选一件成品贯穿答案，讲
材料怎样变成物品。评价人物时，说明你从他的设计选择或处理失败的方式中看到了什么，而不是只说手巧。
叙述顺序
A 介绍手工摊主梅女士是谁 - B 说明在社区集市认识她 - C 描述旧布封面的手工笔记本 - D 讲她按用途安排纸张和口袋
- E 解释自己欣赏耐心和巧思
A Introduce Mei, a local maker of notebooks - B Recall meeting her at a community market - C Describe handmade books
covered with reused fabric - D Explain her thoughtful choices of paper and pockets - E Express admiration for her patience
and imagination
示例回答
A person I know who makes unusual objects is Mei, a woman I met at a community craft market. Her stall was
covered with handmade notebooks, and I stopped because one had a cover made from an old checked shirt. She
uses leftover paper and clean pieces of fabric to make small books. Some are for drawing, while others have
pockets for tickets, receipts or pressed leaves. No two look exactly the same, because she works with whatever
suitable materials she has. I later visited a workshop she ran at the community centre. She showed us a notebook
she had made for someone who liked recording walks. It had thick pages for sketches, small envelopes for maps
and a cloth loop to hold a pencil. The object was simple, but every detail matched how its owner would use it.
What impressed me was her patience. She checked the page edges carefully before stitching, and when a cover
didn't lie flat, she took it apart rather than hiding the problem with decoration. I admire her because she sees
possibilities in things I might throw away. Her work also feels personal. A factory notebook may be perfectly
tidy, but hers invites you to notice the material and imagine what you could put inside.
中文对照：我认识一位制作特别物品的人，叫梅女士。我在社区手工集市遇见她，摊位上摆满手工笔记本，其中一本用旧
格子衬衫做封面，让我停下来看。她用剩余纸张和干净布料做小本子，有些供画画，有些带着放票据、收据或压平树叶的
小袋。因为材料随手边合适的东西而变，没有两本完全一样。后来我参加她在社区中心开的工作坊。她展示了一本给爱记
录散步的人做的本子，有适合画素描的厚纸、小地图信封和固定铅笔的布环。东西很简单，但每个细节都符合使用者的需
要。让我印象深刻的是她的耐心：缝合前仔细检查书页边缘，封面压不平时，她会拆开重做，而不靠装饰掩盖问题。我佩
服她能在我可能扔掉的东西里看到可能性。她的作品也很有人情味。工厂笔记本或许十分整齐，她的本子却让人想仔细看
材料，再想象里面能装些什么。
自然表达
leftover paper
剩余纸张
lie flat
平整放置
take it apart
把它拆开
see possibilities in
看出……的可能用途
串题 话题 117 改变观点的经历
同一次工作坊可转成改变观点题，保留旧布纸变成实用本子的细节；明确先前觉得这些材料该丢弃，后来发现用途以及自己
的感受。
Seeing her notebooks changed how I viewed leftover materials: things I'd throw away could become useful, personal
objects.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
133
话题 88  /  擅长做手工的人
PART 3
1. Do children usually enjoy arts and crafts?
孩子通常喜欢做美术和手工吗？ 解释材料变化和自主选择为
何有趣，也承认不喜欢脏乱的孩子存在。
Many do because they can turn simple materials into
something visible and personal. Cutting, folding and
choosing colours give them decisions to make. Some
dislike messy materials or become frustrated by difficult
instructions, though. Offering different activities helps: a
child who avoids painting may enjoy building a paper
model or arranging a collage instead.
很多孩子喜欢，因为能把简单材料变成看得见、有个人特点
的作品。剪、折和选颜色都让他们作决定。不过，有些孩子
不喜欢脏乱材料，或因指令太难而烦躁。提供不同活动有帮
助：不爱画画的孩子也许喜欢纸模型或拼贴。
messy materials 容易弄脏的材料
2. Is creativity something people are born with, or
can it develop?
创造力是天生的，还是可以培养的？ 承认个体差异，再用尝
试、比较和修改说明后天练习的具体作用。
People may begin with different interests and tendencies,
but creativity can develop through practice. Trying
several ways to solve a problem gives you more
possibilities to draw on later. Seeing other people's work
can help too, provided you explore rather than simply
copy. A supportive environment makes it easier to test
ideas that might not work immediately.
人们起初的兴趣和倾向可能不同，但创造力能通过练习发展。
尝试多种解决办法，会增加以后可用的思路。看别人的作品
也有帮助，前提是探索而非照抄。受到支持的环境，让人更
敢测试未必立刻成功的想法。
draw on 利用已有经验或想法
3. Should every child have art lessons?
所有孩子都应该上美术课吗？ 把基础接触与专业训练分开，
用表达和观察说明普遍参与的价值。
I think every child should have access to basic art
lessons, just as they encounter music and sport. Art
offers another way to observe and express ideas, even for
children who won't become artists. Lessons should allow
experimentation rather than demand identical results.
Specialised training can remain optional for those who
want to take the interest further.
我觉得每个孩子都应有机会接触基础美术课，就像接触音乐
和运动。即使不会成为艺术家，美术也提供观察和表达想法
的方式。课程应允许尝试，而不是要求相同成品。想深入发
展的孩子再自愿接受专业训练。
have access to 有机会接触
4. How does developing art and culture affect
society?
艺术和文化的发展会怎样影响社会？ 把共同讨论、记忆保存
和就业联系到具体活动，避免抽象赞美。
Art and cultural activities give people ways to share
experiences and question familiar ideas. A local
exhibition can preserve neighbourhood memories, while
a theatre production may encourage discussion about
family life. They also provide work for performers and
makers. Their value isn't only financial, though;
accessible activities can help people feel that their own
stories belong in public life.
艺术文化活动让人分享经历、重新思考熟悉观念。本地展览
可保存社区记忆，戏剧可能引发对家庭生活的讨论，也给表
演者和创作者提供工作。但价值不只是金钱；容易参与的活
动能让人觉得自己的故事也值得进入公共生活。
preserve neighbourhood memories 保存社区记忆

sections.title: 喜欢画画的孩子
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
学习技能与培养兴趣
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
134
话题 89
PART 2
喜欢画画的孩子
A child who loves drawing
Describe a child you know who enjoys drawing a great deal.
描述一个你认识的、非常喜欢画画的孩子。
1. How you know the child
你怎样认识这个孩子
2. What the child is like
孩子是什么样的人
3. How often the child draws
孩子多久画一次画
4. Why you think the child enjoys it
你认为孩子为何喜欢画画
审题与选材：先交代与孩子的关系和性格，再给出大致画画频率。用一幅画的内容解释兴趣，比说天生有艺术细胞更具体。
注意区分你观察到的行为与自己推测的原因，例如他边画边讲故事，所以你觉得画画让他表达想法。
叙述顺序
A 介绍八岁的表妹小雨是谁 - B 描述她安静却爱讲故事 - C 说明她多数晚上都会画画 - D 讲她画会飞的公交车地图
- E 解释画画怎样帮助她表达
A Introduce Xiaoyu, my eight-year-old younger cousin - B Describe her quiet but imaginative personality - C Explain her
habit of drawing most evenings - D Show her map of flying bus routes - E Connect her pictures with expressing her ideas
示例回答
My younger cousin Xiaoyu loves drawing. She's eight, and I've known her since she was a baby, although we
now see each other mainly at family gatherings. She's quiet when she first meets someone, but once she feels
comfortable, she has endless stories to tell. Drawing seems to be the easiest way for her to start those stories.
She usually spends twenty or thirty minutes drawing after dinner, and she takes a small sketchbook when the
family goes out. Her pictures aren't always of things in front of her. Recently, she showed me a map of a city
where buses could fly. There were landing places on rooftops, a stop beside a giant tree and a special route for
animals. She had even drawn a little waiting area for dogs. When I asked about it, she spent several minutes
explaining why each route went a certain way. She changed one line while we talked because she realised two
buses might crash. I think she enjoys drawing because it lets her build a world and make the rules herself. She
doesn't seem very concerned about whether a picture looks realistic. What matters is whether it tells her story. I
like that freedom, and talking about her drawings is often the best part of visiting her.
中文对照：我的小表妹小雨很喜欢画画。她八岁了，我从她还是婴儿时就认识她，不过现在主要在家庭聚会时见面。刚见
陌生人时，她很安静，熟悉后却有讲不完的故事。画画似乎是她开启故事最容易的方式。她通常晚饭后画二三十分钟，家
人外出时也带小画本。她画的不总是眼前的东西。最近她给我看一座公交车会飞的城市地图，有屋顶降落点、大树旁的车
站，还有动物专线，甚至给狗画了小候车区。我问起时，她花几分钟解释每条线路为什么那样走。聊着聊着，她发现两辆
车可能相撞，就改了一条线。我认为她喜欢画画，是因为可以建造一个由自己定规则的世界。她不太在意画得像不像现实，
更在乎能不能表达故事。我喜欢这种自由，和她聊画作常常是探望她时最快乐的部分。
自然表达
feel comfortable
感到自在
a waiting area
等候区
make the rules
制定规则
look realistic
看起来逼真
串题 话题 88 擅长做手工的人
小雨亲手画的飞行公交地图可直接转到制作特别物品的人题；保留认识经过、独特车站和修改线路，减少频率介绍，突出成
品与感受。
Her imaginary city map is also a special handmade object, so I could focus on what she creates.

学习技能与培养兴趣
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
135
话题 89  /  喜欢画画的孩子
PART 3
1. When is a good age for children to start drawing?
孩子从几岁开始学画画比较合适？ 区别自由涂画与正式训练，
用兴趣和操作能力替代固定年龄要求。
Children can begin making marks as soon as they can
handle suitable materials safely and show interest.
Formal lessons can wait until they're ready to follow
simple guidance without losing the pleasure of
experimenting. I wouldn't choose one exact age for
everyone. Early drawing should mainly offer room to
explore colours, shapes and different movements.
孩子能安全使用适合的材料、表现出兴趣时，就可以开始涂
画。正式课程可以等到他们能听简单指导、又不失去探索乐
趣时再上。我不会规定统一年龄。早期画画主要应给孩子探
索颜色、形状和不同动作的空间。
show interest 表现出兴趣
2. Why do children tend to draw more often than
adults?
为什么孩子通常比成年人画画更频繁？ 比较活动安排和自我
评价，解释成年人怕画不好为何减少尝试。
Drawing is often built into children's play and school
routines, so materials and encouragement are readily
available. Adults may have less free time and judge their
results more harshly. If they think a picture must look
impressive, starting can feel pointless. Children are often
happier to draw simply because they want to explore an
idea.
画画常融入儿童游戏和学校日常，材料和鼓励都容易获得。
成年人空闲时间较少，也可能更苛刻地评价作品。如果觉得
作品必须出色，就容易认为开始没有意义。孩子往往只是想
探索一个想法，就愿意画下来。
judge their results harshly 苛刻地评价作品
3. Why visit galleries or museums when art is
available online?
既然网上能看艺术作品，为什么还去画廊或博物馆？ 从尺寸、
材质和专注环境说明现场价值，不否定线上查阅的便利。
Seeing an original work can reveal its scale, texture and
small details that a screen doesn't convey well. The
setting also encourages people to slow down instead of
scrolling past. Online images are convenient for
discovery and comparison, but standing in front of a
large painting can create a different physical and
emotional experience.
看原作能发现屏幕不易传达的尺寸、材质和细节，现场环境
也鼓励人慢下来，而不是快速滑过。线上图片适合发现作品
和做比较，但站在一幅大画前，会带来不同的身体感受和情
绪体验。
scroll past 滑动略过
4. Should museums and galleries offer free
admission?
博物馆和画廊应该免费开放吗？ 权衡可及性与维护成本，用
常设展免费和特展收费给出具体安排。
I'd support free access to permanent collections where
funding allows, because cost shouldn't prevent people
from exploring culture. Museums still need money for
staff, maintenance and conservation. Charging for
special exhibitions or offering paid extras can help,
alongside public support. The arrangement should keep
an affordable route open for families and people with
limited incomes.
在资金允许时，我支持常设展免费，因为费用不该阻止人接
触文化。博物馆仍需要支付员工、维护和藏品保护费用。特
展收费或提供付费附加服务，加上公共支持，可以帮忙。安
排应让家庭和低收入人群仍有可负担的参观方式。
free access 免费开放
5. How can works of art inspire people?
艺术作品怎样启发人们？ 说明作品让人留意熟悉事物的新角
度，再用创作或谈话的行动承接。
Art can make people notice something familiar in a new
way. A painting of an ordinary kitchen might reveal
interesting light or suggest a story about the person
living there. That can encourage viewers to create
something themselves or start a conversation. Inspiration
doesn't always mean producing art; sometimes it simply
changes what someone pays attention to.
艺术能让人以新方式注意熟悉的事物。一幅普通厨房的画，
可能呈现有趣光线，或让人想象居住者的故事，进而鼓励观
众创作或交谈。启发不一定意味着做艺术，有时只是改变一
个人留意什么。
in a new way 以新的方式
6. How does reading a book differ from visiting a
museum?
读书与参观博物馆有什么不同？ 比较按文字想象和面对实物
观察，也说明两者都可能需要解释。
A book develops ideas through words and usually gives
you a sequence to follow at your own pace. A museum
lets you encounter objects physically and choose your
route through them. Size, material and placement
become part of the experience. Both need interpretation,
though: an unexplained object can be as confusing as an
unfamiliar passage.
书通过文字展开想法，通常提供可按自己速度跟随的顺序。
博物馆让人亲自面对实物，自选路线，尺寸、材料和摆放都
成为体验的一部分。但两者都需要理解：没有解释的物件，
也可能像陌生段落一样令人困惑。
at your own pace 按照自己的节奏
