雅思口语 · 话题与表达
166
话题 104  /  你不喜欢的短途旅行
PART 3
1. What ways of travelling are commonly used?
人们常用哪些出行方式？ 按距离组织交通工具，避免只罗列
名称而没有使用场景。
For short local journeys, people often walk, cycle or take
a bus, while cars and trains are common for longer
distances. Flying becomes useful when travelling very
far or when time is limited. The choice also depends on
cost and connections; a train isn't convenient if reaching
the station takes longer than the journey itself.
本地短途常用步行、自行车或公交，较长距离常用汽车和火
车。路很远或时间有限时，飞机就有用。选择还取决于费用
和接驳；如果去车站比旅程本身还久，坐火车也不方便。
longer distances 较长的距离
2. What problems can occur when travelling at busy
times?
在出行高峰时段可能遇到什么问题？ 围绕延误造成的连锁影
响，并用换乘失败说明不只是人多。
People may face long queues, packed vehicles and
delays that make connections harder to catch. A small
hold-up on one part of the journey can affect everything
afterwards. Travellers may also feel rushed and leave
belongings behind, so allowing extra time and keeping
essential items together can make a busy journey easier
to manage.
可能遇到长队、拥挤车辆和延误，导致难以赶上换乘。前段
一点耽搁就会影响后面安排。匆忙中还可能落下物品，因此
预留时间、把重要物品放在一起，会让高峰出行更容易应对。
leave belongings behind 遗落个人物品
3. What advantages can international travel bring?
出国旅行能带来什么好处？ 重点谈旅行后的所得，用处理陌
生日常事务解释能力变化。
It can help people become more comfortable dealing
with unfamiliar situations. Finding a train platform,
ordering food or asking for help in another country
requires attention and flexibility. Travellers may also
notice different ways of organising everyday life. Those
experiences can challenge assumptions, provided people
look beyond familiar tourist services and actually engage
with the place.
它能让人更从容地应付陌生情境。在别国找站台、点餐或求
助，需要留心并灵活处理。旅行者还可能看见不同的日常生
活安排。只要不局限于熟悉的旅游服务，真正接触当地，这
些经历就能改变一些想当然的看法。
unfamiliar situations 陌生的情境
4. What motivates people to travel to other countries?
人们出国旅行的动机是什么？ 区别动机与上一问的益处，谈
探亲及想看特定事物的理由。
Some go to see relatives or friends, while others are
drawn by particular landscapes, food or cultural events.
There is also the simple appeal of experiencing
something different from home. For instance, someone
may plan a trip around seeing snow for the first time,
rather than travelling with any broad educational purpose
in mind.
有人探望亲友，有人被特定风景、食物或文化活动吸引。体
验与家乡不同的事物，本身也有吸引力。例如，有人围绕第
一次看雪计划旅行，而不一定抱着宽泛的学习目的出发。
be drawn by 被……吸引
5. Is there a short journey you particularly enjoy?
有没有哪段短途出行让你特别喜欢？ 这是个人问句，交代熟
悉路线及途中愉快细节即可直接回答。
Yes, I enjoy walking to the weekend market near my
home. It takes about twenty minutes, and part of the
route follows a narrow canal. I don't have to watch a
timetable or find parking, so the journey feels relaxed.
Sometimes I take a slightly longer route back just to
enjoy being outside a little longer.
有，我喜欢步行去家附近的周末市场，约二十分钟，其中一
段沿着窄运河。不用看时刻表或找停车位，因此路上很轻松。
有时回程故意绕远一点，只为多享受一会儿户外时间。
watch a timetable 留意时刻表

sections.title: 早起的经历
sections.titleEn: An occasion when I got up early
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
旅行计划与出行经历
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
167
话题 105
PART 2
早起的经历
An occasion when I got up early
Describe one occasion when you got up early.
描述一次你早起的经历。
1. When it happened
是什么时候
2. What you did
你做了什么
3. Why you got up early
你为什么早起
4. How you felt about it
你有什么感受
审题与选材：早起经历要有具体的一次和清楚的原因。可先说为了赶清晨火车，再交代前晚准备、起床后的动作与到站结果。
感受允许发生变化：闹钟响时困倦，顺利上车后轻松，能使故事比单纯赞美早起更真实。
叙述顺序
A 交代去年秋天周六清晨 - B 说明为陪母亲出行赶火车 - C 描述前晚准备和闹钟响起 - D 讲述安静出门并顺利到站
- E 比较起床困倦与上车轻松
A Locate one Saturday morning last autumn - B Explain catching a train with mother - C Describe packing and hearing the
alarm - D Recall leaving quietly and reaching station - E Compare initial tiredness with later relief
示例回答
I got up at five one Saturday morning last autumn because my mother and I were catching an early train to visit
my grandparents. We wanted to arrive before lunch, and the early train was the most convenient option. I don't
normally get up that early, so I prepared almost everything the night before. I put our tickets and identification in
my bag, laid out my clothes and made two sandwiches. When the alarm rang, I still wanted to turn over and go
back to sleep. For a few seconds, I couldn't remember why I had chosen such a terrible time to wake up. Once
I'd washed my face and eaten something, I felt more awake. We left the flat quietly and walked to the bus stop.
The street looked unfamiliar without its usual traffic, and one bakery was just opening. I remember the smell of
warm bread as we passed. We reached the station with plenty of time, so there was no need to rush. On the train,
we watched the sky become brighter and shared the sandwiches. I felt pleased that we'd organised ourselves
properly, even though I was still a little sleepy. I wouldn't make five o'clock starts a daily habit, but for that
journey, getting up early was definitely worth it.
中文对照：去年秋天一个周六，我凌晨五点起床，陪母亲赶早班火车去看外祖父母。我们想午饭前到，早班车最方便。我
平常不起这么早，所以前晚几乎把所有东西准备好了：车票和证件放进包，衣服摆好，还做了两个三明治。但闹钟响时，
仍想翻身继续睡。有那么几秒，我甚至想不起为什么要选如此糟的起床时间。洗脸吃点东西后清醒些，我们轻声离开公寓，
走向公交站。没有平日车流，街道显得陌生；一家面包店刚开门，路过时闻到了热面包香。到车站时间充足，不必赶路。
车上我们看天渐渐亮起来，分着吃三明治。虽然还有点困，但很高兴一切安排妥当。我不会把五点起床变成每天的习惯，
不过为了那次出行，早起确实值得。
自然表达
lay out my clothes
把衣服摆好
with plenty of time
留有充足时间
go back to sleep
继续睡觉
be worth it
值得
串题 话题 102 推荐的度假地
可保留陪母亲赶火车的出发片段，但若改成度假经历，须补目的地活动和整体感受，并确认那次探亲确实属于假期。
If that family visit was part of a holiday, the early train could introduce the wider travel story.


25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
旅行计划与出行经历
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
168
话题 105  /  早起的经历
PART 3
1. Do you know someone who enjoys getting up
early?
你认识喜欢早起的人吗？ 直接介绍一个人及其固定活动，用
不受打扰解释他为何喜欢。
Yes, my father likes getting up before the rest of the
family. He makes tea, reads for a while and sometimes
goes out to buy breakfast. He says that quiet hour gives
him time to think without being interrupted. It seems to
suit him, although I don't think I'd enjoy following the
same schedule every day.
认识，我父亲喜欢比家里其他人早起。他泡茶、读一会儿书，
有时出门买早餐。他说安静的一小时让他不受打扰地思考。
这个习惯似乎适合他，不过我不觉得自己会喜欢每天照着同
样时间表生活。
without being interrupted 不受打扰地
2. What makes people get up early?
人们为什么早起？ 区分不得不早起与主动选择，分别给出工
作和独处的场景。
Some have to because of work, school or a long
commute, while others choose to have a quiet start to the
day. Parents may get up early to prepare breakfast before
their children wake. People who exercise outdoors might
also prefer the cooler, less crowded morning hours,
provided they can get enough sleep beforehand.
有人因工作、上学或通勤远而必须早起，有人主动选择安静
地开始一天。父母可能提前准备早餐，等孩子醒来。户外锻
炼者也可能喜欢清晨凉快、人少，但前提是之前能睡够。
a quiet start to the day 安静地开始一天
3. On which occasions is arriving early important?
哪些场合提前到达很重要？ 选择需要登记安检或准备的场合，
并解释预留时间的实际用途。
It's important for events with a fixed starting time and
some preparation, such as flights, examinations or job
interviews. Arriving early gives people room to handle a
queue, find the right room or settle themselves. That
doesn't mean turning up hours before everything; the
useful amount of extra time depends on what could
realistically cause delays.
有固定开始时间且需要准备的活动，提前到很重要，例如航
班、考试或面试。预留时间方便排队、找房间或稳定状态。
但不是所有事都要早几小时，合理余量取决于实际可能出现
什么耽搁。
a fixed starting time 固定开始时间
4. Why do some people enjoy staying awake late?
为什么有些人喜欢熬夜？ 用白天责任与夜间自主时间说明吸
引，再承认也可能是娱乐延长。
For some people, late evening is the only time that feels
completely their own. Work and family responsibilities
are finished, so they can read, play games or talk to
friends without interruption. Others simply get absorbed
in entertainment and lose track of time, which is
different from deliberately choosing a late schedule that
suits them.
有些人只有深夜才觉得时间完全属于自己。工作和家庭责任
结束，就能不受打扰地读书、玩游戏或聊天。另一些只是沉
迷娱乐忘了时间，这与主动选择适合自己的晚作息并不相同。
lose track of time 忘记时间

sections.title: 等待特殊事件发生的经历
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
旅行计划与出行经历
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
169
话题 106
PART 2
等待特殊事件发生的经历
Waiting for a special moment
Describe a time you had to wait for something special.
描述一次你等待特别事情发生的经历。
1. What you were waiting for
你在等待什么
2. Why you had to wait
你为什么必须等待
3. What you did while waiting
等待时你做了什么
4. How waiting made you feel
等待让你有何感受
审题与选材：特别的事不一定宏大，可以是久别后的见面。先明确等待对象，再解释延迟原因，让等待真正构成经历。重点
写等待时反复看消息、转移注意力等动作，以及期待和烦躁并存的心情，不要只讲事情发生以后。
叙述顺序
A 说明等待久未见面的朋友 - B 交代她的火车临时晚点 - C 描述站内反复查看到达屏 - D 讲述买茶并写重逢清单 - E 呈现
焦急转为见面时的欣喜
A Introduce waiting for a returning friend - B Explain that her train was delayed - C Describe checking the station arrivals
board - D Recall buying tea and making notes - E Show impatience turning into happy relief
示例回答
Last year, I waited at the station for a close friend who had been working in another city for almost a year. We'd
kept in touch through messages, but this was the first chance we'd had to meet properly in months. I'd planned to
take her to our favourite noodle shop straight from the station. Her train was delayed by about an hour. She
messaged me before the original arrival time, but I was already there. At first, I stood near the arrivals board and
checked it every few minutes, even though I knew staring at it wouldn't make the train arrive sooner. Eventually,
I bought a cup of tea and found a seat. I wrote a short list of things I wanted to tell her, including a funny story
from work that was too complicated to explain by text. I also checked whether the noodle shop would still be
serving when we arrived. I felt impatient, but it was a pleasant kind of impatience mixed with excitement. The
delay seemed longer because I'd been looking forward to the meeting so much. When she finally came through
the gate, we both started laughing before we'd even said hello. The waiting was annoying, but it disappeared
from my mind almost immediately once we were together.
中文对照：去年，我在车站等一位好友。她在另一座城工作快一年了，我们一直发消息联系，但几个月来，这是第一次有
机会好好见面。我计划从车站直接带她去最爱的面馆。火车晚点约一小时，她在原定到站前发消息，不过我已经在那里了。
起初我站在到达信息屏旁，每几分钟看一眼，明知一直盯着不会让火车早点来。后来买杯茶找座位，列了个想告诉她的事
情清单，包括一件太复杂、不方便发文字解释的工作趣事。我还查面馆到时是否仍供应食物。我有些不耐烦，却又混着兴
奋，是一种愉快的急切。因为太期待见面，延误就显得特别长。她终于出闸，我们还没打招呼就都笑了起来。等待虽恼人，
但一见到彼此，我几乎立刻就把它忘在脑后。
自然表达
keep in touch
保持联系
look forward to
期待
straight from the station
直接从车站出发
a pleasant kind of impatience
带着愉快的急切
串题 话题 56 跟朋友度过的美好夜晚
可保留好友重逢与吃面计划，若见面确在晚上发生，还需讲实际共度的活动与愉快原因，不能把整篇继续写成等车。
If our reunion took place in the evening, I would continue with the meal and conversation after her arrival.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
170
话题 106  /  等待特殊事件发生的经历
PART 3
1. In what everyday situations do people need to
wait?
日常生活中哪些情况需要等待？ 按服务、交通和他人回复举
例，说明等待并不都以排队出现。
People wait for buses, appointments, meals and replies to
messages, so waiting isn't always about standing in a
queue. Sometimes the difficult part is being unable to
plan what comes next. For example, waiting for a
delivery without a clear time window can keep someone
at home even when they have other errands to do.
等公交、预约、饭菜和消息回复都很常见，所以等待不一定
是站着排队。有时困难在于无法计划下一步。例如快递没有
明确送达时段，即使还有别的杂事要办，人也可能只能待在
家。
a clear time window 明确的时间范围
2. Why do many people hate having to wait?
为什么许多人很讨厌等待？ 用失去时间控制感解释烦躁，区
别可预期排队和没有消息。
Waiting can make people feel that they have lost control
of their time, especially when nobody explains the delay.
Ten minutes with a clear update may feel easier than five
minutes of uncertainty. People also become frustrated
when they suspect the queue is unfair, such as when
someone who arrived later is served first without
explanation.
等待让人觉得失去对时间的掌控，尤其没人解释延误时。明
确告知的十分钟，可能比不知情况的五分钟更好忍受。觉得
顺序不公平也会烦，比如后来的人无解释地先得到服务。
lose control of their time 失去对自己时间的掌控
3. Are grown-ups generally better at waiting than
children?
成年人通常比孩子更会等待吗？ 解释成年人理解时间和原因
的优势，再承认压力会削弱耐心。
Often, yes, because adults can understand why a delay is
necessary and estimate how long it might last. They also
have more ways to occupy themselves. Children may
struggle with the idea of an hour, so waiting feels
endless. Still, a stressed adult can be less patient than a
child who is happily drawing or playing.
通常是，因为成年人能理解延误必要性，也能估计多久结束，
打发时间的方法更多。孩子可能不理解一小时有多长，所以
觉得等不到头。但压力大的成年人，也可能不如开心画画或
玩耍的孩子有耐心。
occupy themselves 让自己有事可做
4. How do you feel when something keeps you
waiting?
当你不得不等待时，你会有什么感受？ 以是否知道结束时间
区分感受，避免把个人题泛化成人群讨论。
I'm usually fine if I know roughly how long the wait will
be. I can read or do a small task on my phone. What
bothers me is being told that something will happen any
minute when it keeps being delayed, because I can't relax
or move on to anything else without worrying I'll miss it.
大概知道要等多久时，我通常没问题，可以读书或在手机上
处理一件小事。让我烦的是不断被告知马上就好，却一再延
迟。这样我既不能放松，也不能放心去做别的，总怕错过。
any minute 随时；马上
5. Would you describe yourself as a patient person?
你觉得自己通常有耐心吗？ 用对人和对无说明延误的区别，
给出有分寸的自我判断。
Mostly, yes, particularly when another person needs time
to learn or explain something. I don't mind listening
patiently if it helps them feel comfortable. I'm less
patient with avoidable delays, like a meeting starting late
because nobody checked the room booking, although I
try not to take that frustration out on the wrong person.
大体上有，尤其别人需要时间学习或解释事情时。如果耐心
倾听能让对方自在，我不介意。但可避免的延误让我耐心较
少，比如没人核对会议室预约导致开会迟开始，不过我会尽
量不迁怒无关的人。
take frustration out on someone 把烦躁发泄在某人身上
6. Were you more patient or less patient when you
were a child?
小时候的你比现在更有耐心还是更没耐心？ 用具体等待场景
比较过去和现在，再解释行为改变的原因。
I was less patient, especially when waiting for something
enjoyable. Before a family outing, I'd ask whether it was
time to leave every few minutes. Now I understand that
other people have things to organise, and I can keep
myself busy. I still feel excited, but I'm better at not
making everyone else hear about it constantly.
小时候更没耐心，尤其等有趣事情时。家庭出游前，我每几
分钟就问能否出发。现在理解别人还有事要安排，也能给自
己找事做。我仍会兴奋，只是更能控制，不会一直让周围人
听我催促。
keep myself busy 让自己忙点事情

sections.title: 一本让你兴奋的书
sections.titleEn: A book that kept me excited
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
书籍、影视与音乐感受
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
171
话题 107
PART 2
一本让你兴奋的书
A book that kept me excited
Describe a book you have read that you found exciting.
描述一本你读过并觉得令人兴奋的书。
1. Which book it is
它是哪本书
2. What it is about
它讲了什么
3. Why you chose to read it
你为什么读它
4. Why you found it exciting
你为什么觉得它精彩刺激
审题与选材：书名和主线只需够听者理解，重点是为什么读以及阅读时的具体反应。可以抓住地图与不确定的人物关系两条
线，说明悬念从何而来。不要复述整本书，更不必用抽象赞美替代自己停不下来阅读的过程。
叙述顺序
A 指出读的是金银岛这本书 - B 交代朋友推荐与借阅原因 - C 简述少年随船寻找宝藏主线 - D 解释人物真假难辨带来的悬
念 - E 描写睡前多读几章的反应
A Name the adventure novel Treasure Island - B Explain a friend’s recommendation and borrowing - C Outline a boy’s
dangerous treasure voyage - D Explain the uncertainty around other characters - E Recall reading extra chapters before bed
示例回答
An exciting book I've read is Treasure Island. I borrowed it from the library after a friend said it was far more
gripping than our old school edition looked. I wanted a clear story rather than something to study. It follows a
boy called Jim who becomes involved in a search for buried treasure. There's a map, a sea voyage and people
with hidden intentions, including a pirate who keeps a parrot. I knew the general idea of pirates looking for
treasure, but I didn't know how the story would develop. What kept me interested wasn't just the danger. It was
the uncertainty about whom Jim could trust. Someone could seem helpful in one scene and make me suspicious
a few pages later. That made me pay attention to small conversations as well as the bigger events. I read most of
it in the evenings. One night, I planned to stop after a chapter, then kept going because something had happened
that I wanted explained. By the time I looked at the clock, it was much later than I expected. I wouldn't claim it
made me want to become an adventurer, but it reminded me how enjoyable it is to get completely caught up in a
story.
中文对照：我读过一本很精彩的书是《金银岛》。朋友说它远比旧版学校用书看起来吸引人，我便从图书馆借来。我想读
情节清楚的故事，而不是用来研究的东西。它讲少年吉姆参与寻找埋藏宝藏的经历，有地图、海上航行，还有隐藏意图的
人，其中包括一位养鹦鹉的海盗。我知道海盗寻宝的大致设定，却不知道故事如何发展。吸引我的不只是危险，还有吉姆
究竟能信任谁。有人这一幕似乎热心，几页后又让人怀疑，因此我既关注大事件，也留心短对话。我大多晚上读。有晚本
想读完一章就停，却因想弄清刚发生的事而继续。再看钟时，比预想晚了很多。它并没让我想做冒险家，却让我重新感到，
完全投入一个故事是多么快乐的事。
自然表达
get caught up in a story
沉浸在故事里
pay attention to
留意
keep going
继续下去
a sea voyage
海上航行
串题 话题 108 动物的故事
可保留金银岛的寻宝主线，转而交代书中鹦鹉如何出现、是否还有其他动物，以及阅读时间地点，不能只复述海盗冒险。
The pirate’s parrot gives the same book an animal detail, but I would need to explain its place in the story.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
172
话题 107  /  一本让你兴奋的书
PART 3
1. What kinds of books are people interested in
reading these days?
现在人们喜欢读哪些类型的书？ 不给无依据的流行排名，按
放松和解决问题两类阅读目的回答。
I see interest in both entertaining stories and books that
help with practical problems. Some readers choose crime
novels or romance to relax, while others look for advice
about cooking, work or personal interests. What
someone reads can change with their circumstances, so a
new parent may choose very different books from the
ones they enjoyed last year.
我看到既有人喜欢娱乐故事，也有人读解决实际问题的书。
有些选犯罪小说或爱情故事放松，有些寻找烹饪、工作或个
人兴趣的建议。读什么会随生活变化，新手父母可能与去年
喜欢的书很不同。
practical problems 实际问题
2. How might younger and older readers’ choices
differ?
年轻读者和年长读者的阅读选择可能有什么不同？ 用人生阶
段解释部分偏好，同时指出类型小说能跨年龄吸引。
Younger readers may be drawn to stories about finding
independence or starting relationships, while older
readers might connect with family histories or reflections
on a long life. Those are tendencies rather than rules. A
strong mystery can appeal across generations, and
personal interests often explain someone's reading
choices better than their age alone does.
年轻读者可能被寻找独立或开始恋爱的故事吸引，年长读者
可能更能理解家族历史或人生回顾。但这只是倾向，不是规
定。好的悬疑故事能跨越代际，个人兴趣常比单凭年龄更能
解释选书。
appeal across generations 吸引不同年龄的人
3. Why do certain books stay popular for many
years?
为什么有些书能长期受欢迎？ 从人物处境的持续可理解性切
入，再说明推荐与重读的作用。
Some books deal with feelings people continue to
recognise, such as jealousy, friendship or wanting to
belong. If the characters feel convincing, a story can
remain meaningful even when its setting is old.
Teachers, families and adaptations can introduce it to
new readers, but people still need a reason to enjoy the
actual book itself.
有些书写的是人们一直能理解的感受，如嫉妒、友谊或渴望
归属。人物可信，即使背景久远，故事仍有意义。教师、家
庭和改编作品能带来新读者，但人们仍需在原书本身找到享
受它的理由。
wanting to belong 渴望获得归属感
4. Would you rather read a book before seeing its
film version?
你更愿意先读书还是先看改编电影？ 明确个人顺序，用想象
空间解释选择，同时保留电影吸引读书的可能。
I usually prefer the book first because I can imagine the
characters and places for myself. Once I've seen a film,
the actors' faces tend to stay in my head while I read.
That said, a good film sometimes makes me pick up a
book I would never have noticed, so I don't follow the
order strictly.
我通常先读书，因为能自己想象人物和地方。一旦看了电影，
阅读时脑中常一直是演员的脸。不过好电影有时会让我拿起
原本不会注意的书，所以我也不严格遵守这个顺序。
pick up a book 拿起一本书来读
5. Do readers usually enjoy films adapted from books
they know?
读过原著的人通常喜欢它的电影改编吗？ 解释期待与删减的
冲突，判断标准落在保留人物核心而非照搬。
Their reactions are mixed, because readers arrive with
strong expectations about characters and favourite
scenes. They may dislike changes that remove what
mattered to them. But a film has less time and different
ways to tell a story, so I think an adaptation can work
well if it preserves the characters' essential relationships
and emotional direction.
反应不一，因为读者对人物和喜欢的场景已有期待。改动删
掉自己重视的内容，可能令人失望。但电影时间更短，叙事
方式也不同。只要保留人物重要关系和感情走向，我觉得改
编仍能很好。
strong expectations 强烈的期待

sections.title: 动物的故事
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
书籍、影视与音乐感受
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
173
话题 108
PART 2
动物的故事
A story involving animals
Describe an animal story you encountered in a film or book.
描述一个你从电影或书中了解的动物故事。
1. What the film or book is about
电影或书讲了什么
2. When and where you watched or read it
你何时何地观看或阅读
3. Whether any other animals appear
其中是否还有其他动物出现
4. How you felt about it
你对它有什么感受
审题与选材：动物故事题要兼顾故事、观看时间地点以及其他动物，不能只介绍最喜欢的角色。可以先讲一次家庭观影，再
以寻找孩子为主线介绍海洋动物。感受用紧张到放松的变化展开，同时说明动画里的人性化表达为何有吸引力。
叙述顺序
A 说明上月在家重看海底总动员 - B 简述父亲寻找失踪儿子的故事 - C 介绍同行的多莉和其他海洋动物 - D 描写紧张情节
中幽默带来的缓冲 - E 说明对父子关系产生的共鸣
A Introduce watching Finding Nemo at home - B Outline a father searching for his son - C Mention Dory and other sea
animals - D Describe humour interrupting the tense moments - E Explain connecting with the family relationship
示例回答
The animal story that comes to mind is Finding Nemo, which I watched again at home with my younger cousin
last month. We wanted something we could both enjoy, and she hadn't seen it before. I remembered the bright
underwater scenes, but I'd forgotten some smaller moments. The film is about a clownfish called Marlin trying
to find his son, Nemo, after they become separated. During the search, he travels with Dory, another fish who is
friendly but often forgets things. There are plenty of other sea animals, including sharks, turtles and fish living in
a tank. They make the underwater world feel busy and full of different personalities. I liked the way the film
mixed worrying situations with humour. Just when a scene became tense, a strange conversation or an
unexpected reaction made us laugh. My cousin kept asking whether Nemo would be all right, so watching her
reactions was almost as entertaining as the film itself. What stayed with me was the relationship between a
parent who wants to keep his child safe and a child who wants more independence. The characters are fish, but
that disagreement feels very familiar. By the end, I felt cheerful and slightly moved, and we spent dinner talking
about which character we liked best.
中文对照：我想到的动物故事是《海底总动员》。上个月我在家陪小表妹重看，她之前没看过，我们想找部都能享受的电
影。我记得鲜艳的海底画面，却忘了些小细节。故事讲小丑鱼马林与儿子尼莫失散后寻找他。途中同行的是友善却常忘事
的多莉。片里还有鲨鱼、海龟和鱼缸中的鱼，让海底世界热闹且充满不同个性。我喜欢它把担心与幽默混在一起：场面刚
紧张，奇怪对话或出人意料的反应又逗人笑。表妹不断问尼莫会不会没事，她的反应几乎与电影本身一样有趣。最留在我
心里的是想保护孩子的父亲，与渴望更多独立的孩子之间的关系。角色虽是鱼，这种分歧却很熟悉。结尾让我开心又略感
动，晚饭时我们还在讨论最喜欢哪个角色。
自然表达
become separated
失散
come to mind
浮现在脑海
keep someone safe
保护某人安全
feel familiar
让人觉得熟悉
串题 话题 110 近期观影
可直接沿用在家重看海底总动员的经历，保留时间和表妹，明确选片原因及喜欢之处，其他动物不再需要逐一展开。
I could use the same viewing experience to describe a film I enjoyed, focusing on why we chose it.

书籍、影视与音乐感受
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
174
话题 108  /  动物的故事
PART 3
1. Should schools teach children about animals?
学校有必要教孩子动物知识吗？ 先说明基础学习价值，再用
观察需要解释知识如何影响对待方式。
Yes, because animals are part of the world children
share, and basic knowledge helps them respond more
thoughtfully. They can learn that different animals need
different food, space and care. A lesson comparing a
bird's needs with a fish's can also teach careful
observation, rather than simply asking children to
memorise a list of names.
有必要，因为动物与孩子共享这个世界，基本知识让孩子更
周到地对待它们。他们能学到不同动物需要不同食物、空间
和照护。比较鸟与鱼的需求，也能训练细心观察，而不只是
背名字。
careful observation 细心观察
2. Is learning about animals a waste of children’s
time?
孩子学习动物知识是在浪费时间吗？ 回应家长担忧，用可与
阅读科学结合说明并非挤占核心学习。
I don't agree, provided the learning goes beyond
collecting amusing facts. Studying animals can involve
reading, comparing evidence and asking why living
things behave differently. For example, children could
observe insects and record what they notice. That
combines science and language practice, so it doesn't
have to compete with the subjects parents consider more
important.
我不同意，前提是不只收集有趣小知识。学习动物可以涉及
阅读、比较证据，以及追问生物为何行为不同。例如孩子观
察昆虫并记录所见，就结合了科学和语言练习，未必与父母
看重的学科相冲突。
record what they notice 记录观察所得
3. Why do people always use animals when telling
stories to children?
为什么人们给孩子讲故事时总是使用动物角色？ 讲清鲜明外
形与安全的情感距离如何帮助理解，而非说孩子都爱动物。
Animals are easy to make visually distinctive, and
children can quickly remember a slow turtle or a curious
rabbit. They also create a little distance from real life. A
story about two animals arguing can explore jealousy or
selfishness without making a child feel directly accused,
which may make the message easier to think about.
动物容易有鲜明外形，孩子很快记住慢乌龟或好奇兔子。它
们也与现实留有一点距离。两个动物争吵的故事，可以谈嫉
妒或自私，却不让孩子觉得自己被直接指责，因此可能更容
易思考其中道理。
feel directly accused 觉得自己被直接指责
4. Is keeping pets common in your country?
你们国家养宠物普遍吗？ 用身边常见现象作有限判断，并说
明时间空间让家庭选择不同。
It seems quite common in the urban neighbourhoods I
know, especially to keep cats or dogs. I often see people
walking dogs or discussing pet care with neighbours.
Still, not every household wants an animal. Time, space
and the responsibility of arranging care during holidays
can make some families decide that a pet wouldn't suit
their routine.
在我熟悉的城市社区似乎挺常见，尤其猫狗。我常看到人遛
狗或与邻居讨论照顾宠物。但不是每家都想养。时间、空间
以及假期安排照护的责任，会让一些家庭觉得宠物不适合自
己的作息。
pet care 宠物照护
5. Should people be forbidden to keep pets in cities?
城市应该禁止人们养宠物吗？ 明确反对全面禁止，再把噪声
清洁问题与主人的具体责任对应。
I wouldn't support a blanket ban, because responsible
owners can keep pets without causing serious problems
for neighbours. Rules should deal with specific issues,
such as cleaning up waste, controlling noise and keeping
animals under control in shared spaces. That protects
other residents while recognising that a well-cared-for
pet can be an important companion.
我不支持全面禁止，因为负责任的主人可以养宠物而不严重
影响邻居。规定应处理具体问题，如清理排泄物、控制噪声
以及在公共空间管好动物。这样既保护其他居民，也承认照
料得当的宠物能成为重要伙伴。
a blanket ban 全面禁止

书籍、影视与音乐感受
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
175
话题 108  /  动物的故事
PART 3
6. Are zoos suitable places to visit with young
children?
动物园适合带幼儿去吗？ 以动物照护和参观方式为条件，避
免把娱乐吸引力当成唯一理由。
They can be, if the zoo provides good animal care and
helps children understand what they're seeing. Young
visitors may be fascinated by an animal's size or
movement in a way that pictures can't fully convey.
Adults should keep the visit manageable and explain
respectful behaviour, rather than encouraging children to
bang on glass or demand a reaction.
如果动物园照顾好动物，并帮助孩子理解所见，就可以。真
实动物的体型或动作能吸引幼儿，这种感受图片未必完整传
达。大人应合理安排参观，教孩子尊重动物，而不是鼓励敲
玻璃或逼它反应。
respectful behaviour 尊重他者的行为
7. What can a zoo visit teach children?
参观动物园能让孩子学到什么？ 区别看见动物与真正学习，
用食物运动环境三个可观察点展开。
Children can learn how animals move, eat and use their
surroundings, especially when an adult helps them notice
details. Comparing a climbing animal with one that
swims can lead to useful questions about their bodies. A
good visit should also explain their natural homes, so
children don't assume that life in an enclosure represents
the whole story.
孩子能了解动物如何移动、进食和使用周围环境，尤其有大
人引导观察时。比较攀爬与游泳的动物，可引出关于身体的
好问题。好的参观还应说明自然栖息地，免得孩子以为围栏
里的生活就是全部。
natural homes 自然栖息地
8. What value do stories about animals have?
动物故事有什么益处？ 聚焦故事对情感理解的帮助，并说明
虚构角色不能代替动物事实。
They can make difficult feelings easier to discuss. A
frightened animal or an excluded character gives
children someone to care about, and the story can open a
conversation about kindness or courage. I'd still separate
fiction from facts, though, because a talking fox's
choices don't tell us how real foxes behave or what they
need.
它们能让复杂感受更容易讨论。害怕的动物或被排斥的角色，
让孩子有在意的对象，也能开启关于善意和勇气的对话。但
仍要区分虚构与事实，因为会说话的狐狸如何选择，并不说
明真正狐狸的行为和需求。
open a conversation 开启一段讨论
9. Do you agree with people who describe animals as
very dirty?
有人觉得动物很脏，你同意吗？ 区分动物习性与人的卫生标
准，再把清洁责任落到具体环境。
I think that description is too broad. Animals have their
own ways of keeping clean, but they don't follow human
household rules. Muddy paws don't make an animal bad
or unsuitable for companionship. People still need
sensible hygiene and proper care, especially around food
and shared living spaces, rather than assuming every
animal presents the same problem.
我觉得说得太笼统。动物有自己的清洁方式，却不遵循人类
家居规矩。爪子沾泥并不表示动物不好或不适合陪伴。人仍
需合理卫生和妥善照料，尤其食物及共享生活空间附近，而
不能认定所有动物问题一样。
muddy paws 沾泥的爪子

sections.title: 有趣的视频
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
书籍、影视与音乐感受
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
176
话题 109
PART 2
有趣的视频
A video that interested me
Describe a video you found interesting.
描述一段你觉得有趣的视频。
1. When and where you watched it
你何时何地观看
2. What the video shows
视频讲什么
3. Why you decided to watch it
你为什么观看
4. How you felt about it
你有什么感受
审题与选材：有趣视频不一定是搞笑片段，能让你看懂一个过程也可以。交代观看场景与点击原因后，按画面先后讲两三个
动作，再说明自己是否尝试。感受要来自视频的讲法，例如保留失误比只展示成品更让人愿意动手。
叙述顺序
A 交代上周在厨房看视频 - B 说明为处理剩饭而点开 - C 描述博主分步示范做饭 - D 讲述保留小失误带来的趣味 - E 说明
自己尝试后的具体感受
A Explain watching in my kitchen recently - B Describe clicking for leftover rice ideas - C Outline the cook’s simple
practical demonstration - D Recall a small mistake left onscreen - E Explain trying it and feeling encouraged
示例回答
Last week, I watched a short cooking video in my kitchen while trying to decide what to do with some leftover
rice. It appeared when I searched for an easy lunch, and the picture showed a crisp rice pancake made in an
ordinary frying pan. That looked more useful to me than a complicated recipe with ingredients I didn't have. The
video showed a home cook mixing cold rice with egg and chopped vegetables, pressing it into a pan and turning
it once the bottom had become firm. What made it interesting was that the first attempt at turning the pancake
didn't go perfectly. One edge broke, and the cook simply pushed it back into shape and carried on. There was no
dramatic music or long introduction. The camera stayed close enough for me to see the texture, and short
captions explained what to look for at each stage. I paused it a couple of times while making my own version.
Mine wasn't as neat, but it tasted good and used up the rice. I felt encouraged because the video made cooking
seem manageable rather than something that had to look perfect. The small mistake was actually my favourite
part: it showed me that a slightly messy result didn't mean I had to start again.
中文对照：上周我在厨房发愁怎么处理剩饭，便看了一段做饭短视频。搜索简单午餐时，封面上一张用普通平底锅做的脆
米饭饼吸引了我。比起需要很多我没有的食材的复杂菜谱，它看着更实用。视频里一位家庭厨师把冷饭、鸡蛋和碎蔬菜拌
好，压进锅，等底部成形再翻面。有趣的是第一次翻面不完美，边缘破了一块，他直接推回原形继续做。没有夸张音乐或
冗长开场，镜头够近，能看清质地，短字幕解释各阶段要观察什么。我自己做时暂停了几次。成品没他那么整齐，但好吃，
也用完了剩饭。我很受鼓舞，因为视频让做饭显得可完成，不是必须样样完美的事。小失误其实是最喜欢的部分：它告诉
我，成品稍微乱了点，不等于必须重新开始。
自然表达
leftover rice
剩米饭
carry on
继续
use up
用完
start again
重新开始
串题 话题 83 教你新技能的人
可保留做饭示范，把中心换成视频里的厨师，交代如何认识对方、学会哪一步与尝试感受，不要改写成面对面教学。
The cook in that video also taught me a practical skill through clear demonstrations that I could pause.

书籍、影视与音乐感受
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
177
话题 109  /  有趣的视频
PART 3
1. What sorts of videos do people in your country
enjoy?
你们国家的人喜欢看什么类型的视频？ 从娱乐与实用两类切
入，说明同一人也会随当下需求切换。
People watch a wide range, including comedy, cooking
demonstrations, travel clips and explanations of practical
tasks. The choice often depends on the moment.
Someone may watch a funny clip during a short break,
then search for a detailed repair video at home, so one
person's viewing habits can include both entertainment
and very specific problem-solving.
人们看很多类型，包括喜剧、烹饪示范、旅行片段和实用操
作讲解。选择常取决于当下。一个人休息时看搞笑片，回家
又搜详细维修视频，因此同一人的观看习惯可以同时包括娱
乐和解决具体问题。
a wide range 多种多样
2. Which is more useful: videos or books?
看视频和读书，哪种更有帮助？ 依学习内容判断，动作演示
与长篇解释分别对应两种媒介优势。
It depends on what someone is trying to learn. Videos
are useful when movement matters, such as learning to
fold something or use a tool. Books are often better for
following a detailed explanation at your own pace and
returning to particular sections. Using both can work
well: watch the demonstration, then read the reasons
behind it.
取决于想学什么。折东西或使用工具等需要看动作的内容，
视频有用。跟着详细解释按自己节奏学习、回看特定部分，
书通常更好。两者结合也不错：先看示范，再读背后的原因。
at your own pace 按自己的节奏
3. What can people learn to do by watching videos?
人们能通过视频学会哪些技能？ 给出可观察动作的技能，同
时点明观看必须转为练习才算学会。
They can learn practical skills such as cooking, drawing,
basic repairs or playing a simple piece of music. A video
lets them watch a movement repeatedly and pause at
difficult points. But watching alone isn't enough; they
need to practise and notice their own mistakes,
especially when the finished demonstration looks easier
than the task actually feels.
能学烹饪、画画、基础维修或弹简单曲子等实用技能。视频
让人反复看动作，在难点暂停。但只看不够，还得练习并发
现自己的错误，尤其当成品示范看起来比实际操作容易时。
watch a movement repeatedly 反复观看一个动作
4. Do younger and older viewers tend to choose
different videos?
年轻人和年长者喜欢看的视频有差异吗？ 把生活兴趣与剪辑
节奏分开，并强调内容兴趣不只由年龄决定。
Sometimes their interests differ because they are dealing
with different stages of life. Younger viewers may
follow study tips or new entertainment, while older
viewers may enjoy gardening or familiar performances.
The pace of editing can matter too, but age isn't
everything: a shared hobby can bring people towards
exactly the same detailed instructional videos.
有时有，因为他们处在不同人生阶段。年轻观众可能看学习
技巧或新娱乐内容，年长者可能喜欢园艺或熟悉的表演。剪
辑节奏也有影响，但年龄不是全部：共同爱好会让不同人看
完全相同的详细教学视频。
a shared hobby 共同的爱好

sections.title: 近期观影
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
书籍、影视与音乐感受
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
178
话题 110
PART 2
近期观影
A film I enjoyed recently
Describe a film you watched recently and enjoyed.
描述一部你最近看过并喜欢的电影。
1. When and where you watched it
你何时何地观看
2. Who watched it with you
你和谁一起观看
3. What the film is about
电影讲了什么
4. Why you chose to watch it
你为什么选择这部电影
审题与选材：这题最后一项问为什么观看，不能只回答看完为何喜欢。先交代朋友推荐和适合轻松周末的选择原因，再介绍
故事与观影反应。故事概括控制在必要范围，保留一个具体的笑点类型及人物关系来支持喜欢的判断。
叙述顺序
A 交代两周前在家看的电影 - B 说明与妹妹想找轻松喜剧 - C 讲清朋友推荐促成选择 - D 简述小熊来到伦敦的经历
- E 描述看电影时的笑声和感受
A Introduce watching Paddington at home recently - B Explain wanting a comedy with sister - C Mention the
recommendation behind our choice - D Outline a bear’s arrival in London - E Describe our laughter and warm response
示例回答
Two weeks ago, my sister and I watched Paddington at home on a Sunday afternoon. We'd both had a busy
week and wanted something light that we could enjoy together. A friend had recommended it as a funny film
with a kind heart, so we chose it instead of spending another half hour searching through titles. The story
follows a young bear who arrives in London looking for a home. A family takes him in, and much of the humour
comes from his attempts to understand ordinary human routines. He means well, but simple situations quickly
become chaotic because he doesn't know what everyone else takes for granted. I particularly enjoyed the
physical comedy. My sister and I kept laughing at how a small misunderstanding could lead to a much bigger
mess. At the same time, I cared about whether the bear would find somewhere he truly belonged, so it wasn't
just a string of jokes. Watching it at home suited the mood. We made tea, shared a bowl of popcorn and didn't
look at our phones for most of the film. Afterwards, we agreed that we'd made a good choice. It was cheerful
without feeling empty, and it gave us exactly the relaxed afternoon we'd wanted when we first sat down to
choose something.
中文对照：两周前的周日下午，我和妹妹在家看《帕丁顿熊》。我们都忙了一周，想一起看点轻松内容。朋友说它是部有
趣又温暖的电影，所以直接选了它，免得再花半小时翻片单。故事讲一只小熊来到伦敦寻找家，一家人收留了他。许多笑
点来自他努力理解人类的日常习惯：他本意很好，却不懂别人觉得理所当然的事，简单情境很快变得混乱。我尤其喜欢肢
体喜剧，小误会发展成大麻烦，让我和妹妹不断发笑。同时也关心小熊能否真正找到归属，因此并非只是连续笑话。在家
看很合当时心情：我们泡茶、分一碗爆米花，大部分时间没有看手机。看完都觉得选得好，它欢乐却不空洞，恰好给了我
们最初坐下挑片时想要的那个轻松下午。
自然表达
take him in
收留他
mean well
本意是好的
take for granted
认为理所当然
a string of jokes
一连串笑话
串题 话题 108 动物的故事
可沿用帕丁顿熊的主要故事与家庭观影场景，补清片中是否还有其他动物，把小熊怎样参与故事和个人感受说完整。
Paddington also works as an animal story because the bear’s attempts to find a home drive the film.


25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
书籍、影视与音乐感受
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
179
话题 110  /  近期观影
PART 3
1. What kinds of films tend to succeed in your
country?
你们国家哪些类型的电影容易成功？ 以能被熟人推荐的体验
解释吸引力，不虚构票房类型排名。
Films that give audiences a clear reason to talk about
them can do well, whether that's a funny family story, an
exciting adventure or a moving relationship. I wouldn't
say one genre always succeeds. Viewers may choose a
familiar type initially, but whether they recommend it
often depends on the characters and the overall viewing
experience.
能让观众有明确谈资的电影容易获得好反应，可能是有趣家
庭故事、刺激冒险或感人关系。我不会说某种类型总成功。
观众最初可能选熟悉类型，但会不会推荐，常取决于人物和
整体观影体验。
a clear reason 明确的理由
2. What helps make a movie successful?
哪些因素有助于电影成功？ 区分吸引第一次买票和看后愿意
推荐，让宣传与故事各有作用。
A film needs a story people can follow and characters
they have some reason to care about. Good acting, sound
and pacing help hold their attention. Promotion can bring
the first audience through the door, but positive word of
mouth matters afterwards, because people are more
likely to go when friends explain why they enjoyed it.
电影需要容易跟上的故事，以及让人有理由关心的人物。好
表演、声音和节奏能留住注意力。宣传把第一批观众带进来，
但之后口碑重要，因为朋友能说清为何喜欢，别人更可能去
看。
word of mouth 口碑传播
3. Do Chinese audiences favour films made locally or
overseas?
中国观众更偏爱国产片还是外国片？ 不给统一偏好，比较熟
悉语言生活与新奇场景的两种吸引。
I think both have audiences, and the choice often
depends on the particular film. Domestic stories can
offer familiar language, humour and family situations,
while foreign films may introduce different settings or
storytelling styles. Many viewers switch between them
quite happily, so the country of origin isn't necessarily
the main reason they choose a film.
我觉得两者都有观众，选择常取决于具体影片。国产故事有
熟悉的语言、幽默和家庭情境，外国片能带来不同背景或讲
故事方式。很多人乐意交替观看，所以产地未必是选片的主
要原因。
country of origin 出品国家
4. Can only famous directors make outstanding
films?
只有知名导演才能拍出最好的电影吗？ 明确否定只有名导才
行，把名气产生的关注与实际导演能力区分开来。
No. A famous director may have experience and easier
access to funding, but recognition isn't the same as
ability. A less-known filmmaker can understand a small
story deeply and tell it with great care. Every established
director also had to make early films, so judging only by
reputation would mean overlooking new talent before it
became visible.
不是。名导演可能经验多、更容易获得资金，但被认可不等
于有能力。名气小的创作者也能深入理解小故事、用心拍出
来。成名导演同样拍过早期作品，只按名声判断，会在新人
才被看见前就错过他们。
new talent 新人才能；新人才
5. Do films need famous performers in the lead to be
successful?
电影成功是否需要知名演员担任主角？ 承认明星吸引注意，
再说明角色适配与可信表演决定观后感。
Famous performers can attract attention and make a film
easier to promote, but they aren't essential. The actor
needs to fit the role and make the character believable.
An unfamiliar face can sometimes help viewers focus on
the character rather than the actor, especially in an
ordinary story where the audience is meant to recognise
someone like themselves.
知名演员能吸引关注，也方便宣传，但并非必需。演员需要
适合角色，让人物可信。不熟悉的面孔有时反而能让观众专
注角色而不是演员本人，尤其普通人的故事里，观众应看见
与自己相似的人。
fit the role 适合角色
6. Why do some people choose to see films at the
cinema?
为什么有些人更喜欢在电影院看电影？ 聚焦大银幕和专心观
看的场景，同时说明集体反应如何增加乐趣。
The large screen and strong sound can make a film more
absorbing, especially when its images matter a lot. A
cinema also creates a dedicated period without
household tasks interrupting. Sharing laughter or
surprise with other viewers can add to the experience,
although the appeal depends on having an audience that
doesn't talk through the whole film.
大银幕和有力音效让人更投入，尤其画面非常重要的电影。
电影院也提供一段专门时间，不受家务打断。与其他观众一
起笑或惊讶能增加体验，当然前提是观众别全程不停讲话。
a dedicated period 专门留出的时间

sections.title: 不喜欢的一部电影
sections.titleEn: A film I did not enjoy
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
书籍、影视与音乐感受
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
180
话题 111
PART 2
不喜欢的一部电影
A film I did not enjoy
Describe a film that you did not like.
描述一部你不喜欢的电影。
1. What film it was
是什么电影
2. When you saw it
什么时候看的
3. Who watched it with you
与谁一起看的
4. Why you did not like it
为什么不喜欢
审题与选材：先说明电影类型和观影场景，再用一两个实际情节解释失望。可以承认画面不错，同时指出人物行为或结尾哪
里不合理。把最初期待与看完后的感受连起来，比不断说无聊更有说服力；不必复述整部电影的故事。
叙述顺序
A 交代冬天和朋友在家观影 - B 说明预告片带来的期待 - C 描述角色突然改变的行为 - D 解释结尾为何令人失望 - E 补充
朋友反应与自己感受
A Watch a film at home with friends - B Explain the expectations created by its trailer - C Describe a sudden change in
character - D Show why the ending felt disappointing - E Compare our reactions after the film
示例回答
One film I didn't enjoy was a low-budget science fiction film about a rescue mission in space. I can't remember
its title now, but I watched it at my friend Chen's flat last winter. There were three of us, and we chose it because
the trailer looked tense and exciting. The opening was actually promising. A small spaceship lost contact with
Earth, and the crew had to decide whether to land on an unknown planet. I liked the quiet shots of the empty
control room, so I settled in expecting a clever mystery. After about half an hour, though, the characters stopped
making sense. The captain, who had been extremely careful, suddenly opened a dangerous door without
checking anything. Nobody explained that decision. Later, a machine appeared which could solve almost every
problem, although it hadn't been mentioned before. By the end, I wasn't worried about the crew any more. I was
just waiting for the film to finish. Chen enjoyed the special effects, and I could see his point; some scenes looked
impressive. But for me, attractive pictures couldn't make up for a weak story. We laughed about the strange
ending afterwards, which was probably the most enjoyable part of the evening.
中文对照：我不喜欢的一部电影是讲太空救援的低成本科幻片。我记不起片名了，去年冬天在朋友陈的公寓看的。当时有
三个人，因为预告片紧张刺激就选了它。开头其实不错：一艘小飞船与地球失联，船员要决定是否降落在陌生星球。我喜
欢空荡控制室的安静镜头，期待看到一个巧妙的悬疑故事。但大约半小时后，人物行为就不合理了。一向谨慎的船长突然
未经检查就打开危险的门，没人解释原因。后来又出现一台几乎能解决所有问题的机器，前面却从未提过。到结尾，我已
不担心船员，只等着电影结束。陈喜欢特效，我也理解，因为有些画面确实出色。但漂亮画面弥补不了薄弱的故事。之后
我们笑着讨论那个奇怪结尾，这大概是当晚最有趣的部分。
自然表达
lose contact with
与……失去联系
settle in
安顿下来准备做某事
make sense
合乎情理
make up for
弥补
串题 话题 117 改变观点的经历
可沿用预告片带来的正面期待和看完后的失望，转到改变观点题时明确原先如何判断，并突出哪些剧情问题让判断发生变化。
The trailer gave me a positive impression, but the characters and ending made me change my opinion.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
181
话题 111  /  不喜欢的一部电影
PART 3
1. What types of films are popular with people in
China?
中国人喜欢看哪些类型的电影？ 按放松与寻求刺激两种需求
举例，避免把全国观众说成一种口味。
Comedies and action films seem to attract a broad
audience, because people often want either a laugh or
some excitement after work. Family stories can also
appeal to viewers who recognise the relationships on
screen. Still, taste varies considerably; a busy parent and
a film student may choose completely different things.
喜剧和动作片似乎吸引不少观众，因为人们下班后常想笑一
笑或找点刺激。家庭故事也能吸引在银幕关系中看到自己生
活的人。不过口味差别很大，忙碌的家长和电影专业学生可
能选完全不同的片子。
a broad audience 广泛的观众群体
2. Do younger and older viewers enjoy similar kinds
of films?
年轻人与年长观众喜欢相同类型的电影吗？ 先比较常见兴趣
来源，再用共同欣赏的家庭故事避免年龄定论。
There is some overlap, especially with a well-told family
story. Younger viewers may be more willing to try
unfamiliar styles, while older viewers sometimes prefer
actors or settings they already know. But age isn't the
whole explanation. Someone's hobbies and viewing
habits can matter more than the year they were born.
两者有共同喜好，尤其是讲得好的家庭故事。年轻人可能更
愿尝试陌生风格，年长观众有时偏爱熟悉的演员或背景。但
年龄并不能解释一切，一个人的爱好和观影习惯可能比出生
年份更重要。
viewing habits 观影习惯
3. Why do science fiction films appeal to audiences
today?
为什么现在的观众喜欢科幻电影？ 将技术带来的视觉体验与
未来问题联系，不把特效当作唯一原因。
They let people explore questions that ordinary daily life
can't answer, such as how humans might live on another
planet. Modern visual effects make those imaginary
places easier to believe in. A good science fiction film
also gives the audience familiar emotions, like fear or
loyalty, inside a very unfamiliar world.
它们让人探索日常生活无法回答的问题，比如人类怎样在其
他星球生活。现代视觉效果使这些想象中的地方更可信。好
的科幻片也会把恐惧、忠诚等熟悉情感放进极陌生的世界，
让观众产生共鸣。
visual effects 视觉效果
4. Is watching a film in its original language
preferable?
用电影的原声语言观看更好吗？ 说明原声保留语气的好处，
再考虑阅读字幕有困难的观众。
Usually, yes, because the actors' voices carry humour
and emotion that can be difficult to reproduce. Subtitles
help viewers follow the story while keeping those
voices. But dubbing has a place too. Young children or
people who struggle to read small text may enjoy a film
much more in their own language.
通常是，因为演员声音中的幽默和情感可能难以再现。字幕
让观众理解故事，同时保留原声。但配音也有价值，幼儿或
难以看清小字的人，用自己的语言观看可能会更享受电影。
follow the story 跟上剧情
5. Where do people in China generally watch films?
中国人一般在哪里看电影？ 回答地点时补上居住空间和出行
情境，使家庭与影院各有具体场景。
At home and in cinemas are probably the main answers.
At home, people use a television, laptop or sometimes
just a phone, depending on their space and budget.
Cinemas are common choices for dates or family
outings. Some communities also organise outdoor
screenings, although that isn't an everyday option for
everyone.
家里和电影院大概是主要场所。在家时，人们根据空间和预
算用电视、电脑，有时只用手机。影院常用于约会或家庭出
游。有些社区也组织露天放映，不过这并非每个人每天都有
的选择。
family outings 家庭出游
6. Do people now tend to watch films at home or at
the cinema?
现在人们更倾向在家看电影还是去影院？ 着重解释日常选择
与特殊观影的差别，区别于上一问的地点罗列。
For routine viewing, home is very convenient: people
can pause the film and avoid travelling. The cinema still
offers a sense of occasion, particularly for a visually
impressive release. So I don't see one completely
replacing the other. The same person might watch
casually at home and visit a cinema for something
special.
日常观看在家很方便，可以暂停，也不用出门。影院仍有一
种特别的仪式感，尤其适合视觉效果出众的新片。所以我不
觉得一种会完全取代另一种。同一个人可能平时在家看，遇
到特别想看的片再去影院。
a sense of occasion 特别的仪式感

sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
书籍、影视与音乐感受
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
182
话题 112
PART 2
不享受的音乐活动
A disappointing music event
Describe a music event you attended but did not enjoy.
描述一次你参加过但不喜欢的音乐活动。
1. What the event was
是什么活动
2. Who went with you
与谁同行
3. Why you chose to attend
为什么决定参加
4. Why you did not enjoy it
为什么不喜欢
审题与选材：不喜欢音乐活动，不一定是不喜欢音乐本身。先交代同行者与购票原因，再区分节目内容和现场条件。本例把
宣传中的轻松演出与实际音量、等候时间作比较，结尾保留一个小小的积极感受，让评价具体而不过分抱怨。
叙述顺序
A 交代与室友参加小型演出 - B 解释想听原声歌曲的原因 - C 描述排队与室内声音问题 - D 说明换位置仍然没有改善
- E 讲述提前离场后的实际感受
A Attend a small show with my roommate - B Expect acoustic songs in a relaxed setting - C Describe the queue and
overpowering sound - D Move back without solving the problem - E Explain how leaving early made us feel
示例回答
My roommate and I once went to a small music night in a converted warehouse, and neither of us enjoyed it
very much. It was advertised as an evening of local bands, with a few acoustic performances, so we thought it
would be a relaxed way to spend a Saturday. We'd both been busy with assignments, and one band had posted a
lovely guitar song online. That was the main reason we bought tickets. They weren't expensive, but we were still
looking forward to a proper night out. The trouble started before the music. We stood in a slow queue outside for
nearly forty minutes, and there was nowhere to sit once we got in. Then the first band began, and the speakers
were so loud that I could barely hear the singer's words. We moved towards the back, but the sound was still
uncomfortable. The acoustic band eventually appeared, although their quiet style didn't really suit the noisy
room. After two songs, my roommate suggested leaving, and I agreed immediately. I felt disappointed rather
than angry. The musicians were clearly trying hard, but the setting spoiled the experience. We ended up chatting
over noodles nearby, which suited our mood much better.
中文对照：我和室友曾去一个由仓库改建的场地参加小型音乐之夜，两个人都不太喜欢。宣传说有本地乐队，还有几场原
声演出，我们以为能轻松度过周六。那阵子我们都忙着做作业，其中一支乐队在网上发的吉他歌曲很好听，这是买票的主
要原因。票不贵，但我们很期待好好出去玩一次。问题在演出前就开始了：在外面慢慢排了近四十分钟，进去后又没座位。
第一支乐队开唱时，音量大得几乎听不清歌词。我们移到后面，声音还是很不舒服。原声乐队终于出现，可他们安静的风
格不适合吵闹的房间。听了两首，室友提议走，我马上同意。我是失望而非生气，音乐人明显很努力，只是环境破坏了体
验。后来我们在附近边吃面边聊天，反而更合心情。
自然表达
look forward to
期待
a night out
外出娱乐的晚上
spoil the experience
破坏体验
suit our mood
合乎我们的心情
串题 话题 98 一个你觉得吵闹的地方
同一仓库场地可用于吵闹地点题，保留音箱和人声造成的不适，补位置及到访时间，并诚实说明只去过一次而非经常光顾。
That converted warehouse is also a noisy place I can describe, although I have only been there once.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
183
话题 112  /  不享受的音乐活动
PART 3
1. What sorts of music events are popular nowadays?
现在人们喜欢哪些音乐活动？ 分别说明大型演出与小场地的
吸引力，不把受欢迎等同于规模大。
Large concerts attract people who want to see a favourite
performer and share the excitement with a crowd.
Smaller live shows appeal to listeners who prefer being
close to the musicians. Outdoor festivals offer another
attraction: friends can spend the whole day together,
even if they don't know every band playing.
大型演唱会吸引想看喜欢的歌手、与人群分享兴奋感的人。
小型现场演出适合希望靠近音乐人的听众。户外音乐节还有
另一个吸引力：朋友能一起待上一整天，即使并不认识所有
演出乐队。
live shows 现场演出
2. Should children have some education in music?
儿童应当接受一些音乐教育吗？ 支持基础接触但区分兴趣培
养与专业训练，给出低压力活动。
Yes, at least a chance to sing, keep a rhythm and try
simple instruments. Those activities help children listen
carefully and cooperate with others. It shouldn't mean
forcing everyone to pass difficult examinations. A class
making a short song together can be worthwhile even if
none of the children becomes a musician.
应该，至少让他们有机会唱歌、打节拍、尝试简单乐器。这
些活动帮助孩子仔细倾听并与人合作，但不意味着强迫所有
人考难度很高的等级。一班孩子合写一首短歌就有价值，即
使没人最终成为音乐家。
keep a rhythm 保持节奏
3. How do younger and older people's musical tastes
differ?
年轻人与年长者的音乐喜好有哪些差别？ 从成长经历解释熟
悉感，再说明新的音乐也能跨越年龄界限。
People often feel attached to the songs they heard while
growing up, so different age groups may recognise
different singers immediately. Younger listeners may
discover music through short videos, while older
listeners might return to familiar recordings. Still, a
strong melody or an expressive voice can attract people
of almost any age.
人们常对成长时听过的歌有感情，因此不同年龄群体能马上
认出的歌手不同。年轻听众可能从短视频发现音乐，年长者
可能重听熟悉唱片。不过，动人的旋律或有表现力的声音能
吸引几乎任何年龄的人。
feel attached to 对……有感情
4. What types of music events take place in your
country?
你的国家有哪些音乐活动？ 先列不同形式，再用举办地点和
参与方式把类别讲清楚。
There are stadium concerts, outdoor music festivals and
smaller performances in cafés or live music venues.
Communities also hold singing events, and schools
organise concerts where students perform for their
families. Traditional music appears at some cultural
celebrations. The scale varies a lot, from a few
neighbours to a very large audience.
有体育场演唱会、户外音乐节，以及咖啡馆或音乐场地的小
型演出。社区会办歌唱活动，学校也组织学生为家人演出的
音乐会。一些文化庆祝活动还有传统音乐。规模差异很大，
从几个邻居到大批观众都有。
traditional music 传统音乐
5. Why do many people listen to music while
exercising?
为什么许多人运动时喜欢听音乐？ 把节拍与重复动作联系，
并说明分散注意力在什么情况下有用。
A steady beat can help people keep a regular pace,
especially when running or cycling indoors. Music also
makes repetitive exercise feel less dull, because attention
isn't focused entirely on tired legs. The choice matters,
though. Someone practising careful movements may
need quieter music, or none at all, to concentrate
properly.
稳定的节拍能帮助人保持规律速度，尤其是在室内跑步或骑
车时。音乐也让重复运动不那么乏味，因为注意力不全在疲
惫的双腿上。不过选择很重要，练习精细动作的人可能需要
安静的音乐，甚至不放音乐来集中注意力。
keep a regular pace 保持规律速度
6. How does listening at home differ from attending a
live concert?
在家听音乐与去现场音乐会有什么不同？ 用控制权与共同现
场感比较，再补现场不便以保持评价完整。
At home, you control the volume, choose the songs and
stop whenever you like. A concert gives you the energy
of real performers and an audience reacting together,
which recordings can't fully reproduce. On the other
hand, travel, crowds and poor sound can be tiring. The
better choice depends on the experience you want.
在家可以控制音量、挑歌曲，想停就停。音乐会能感受到真
人演出和观众共同反应的活力，录音无法完全再现。另一方
面，出行、人群和糟糕音效会让人疲惫。哪种更好取决于你
想要怎样的体验。
control the volume 控制音量

sections.title: 你的抱负/梦想
sections.titleEn: An ambition I hope to achieve
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
目标、决定与解决问题
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
184
话题 113
PART 2
你的抱负/梦想
An ambition I hope to achieve
Describe an ambition or dream you have.
描述你的一项抱负或梦想。
1. What you hope to achieve
希望实现什么
2. When you first wanted this
最初何时产生这个愿望
3. Why it matters to you
为什么对你重要
4. What could prevent you from achieving it
什么可能阻碍你实现它
审题与选材：把梦想说成可以看见的生活或工作场景，不必选特别宏大的目标。时间线先回到愿望产生的那一刻，再讲现在
已经做的小事。本例以教成年人读写为目标，最后具体谈资格、时间和经济压力，避免把困难只说成不够努力。
叙述顺序
A 说明希望成为成人识字教师 - B 回到帮助邻居读信的经历 - C 描述目前参加志愿活动的行动 - D 解释独立阅读对生活的
意义 - E 指出时间和收入带来的困难
A Hope to teach adults basic reading skills - B Recall helping a neighbour read a letter - C Describe the volunteering I have
already started - D Explain what independent reading could change - E Identify the practical barriers to this ambition
示例回答
A long-term ambition of mine is to teach adults who find reading difficult. I don't mean teaching advanced
literature. I'd like to help people read everyday things independently, such as a medicine label or a message from
their child's school. The idea first came to me during my second year at university. An older neighbour asked me
to read a letter for her, and she kept apologising for taking up my time. The letter wasn't complicated, but she
was clearly embarrassed. I remember thinking that being unable to read it herself made a small task
unnecessarily stressful. Since then, I've helped at a community homework club. Most of the learners there are
children, so it isn't exactly the work I hope to do, but I'm learning to explain things patiently. When one
explanation doesn't work, I try another instead of simply repeating myself more loudly. This ambition matters to
me because the result would be very practical. Someone could complete a form without having to ask a stranger
for help. The main obstacles are finding suitable training and making enough time for it alongside paid work. I
couldn't simply stop earning money. Still, I could begin with a few evening sessions and build up gradually.
中文对照：我的一个长期目标是教阅读有困难的成年人。我不是想教高深文学，而是帮助他们独立读懂药品标签、孩子学
校发来的信息等日常文字。这个想法始于大学二年级。一位年长邻居请我帮她读信，一直为占用我的时间道歉。信并不复
杂，可她明显很难为情。我当时想，不能自己读，让这样一件小事也变得紧张。之后，我开始在社区作业辅导班帮忙。那
里的学生大多是孩子，与我想做的工作不完全一样，但我正在学习耐心解释。一种说法不行，我就换一种，而不是把相同
的话更大声地重复。这个目标对我重要，因为结果很实用：一个人能自己填表，不必找陌生人帮忙。主要困难是寻找合适
培训，并在有偿工作之外腾出时间。我不能直接停止挣钱，但可以先每周上几次晚课，再慢慢增加。
自然表达
come to me
浮现在我脑海中
take up my time
占用我的时间
alongside paid work
在有偿工作之外同时进行
build up gradually
逐渐增加
串题 话题 114 完美的工作
可把教成年人读写的目标转为理想工作，保留助人的动机和学习计划，但要补充从哪里了解这份工作及需要掌握的具体技能。
My ambition could become a teaching career, provided I gain the training needed to support adult learners properly.

目标、决定与解决问题
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
185
话题 113  /  你的抱负/梦想
PART 3
1. How important is ambition for young people?
抱负对年轻人有多重要？ 说明目标如何影响眼前选择，同时
给探索和改变方向留下空间。
It can give them a reason to keep working when progress
feels slow. A student who wants to design buildings may
take drawing and mathematics more seriously because
those subjects serve a purpose. But ambition needn't be
fixed at sixteen. Exploring different interests is useful,
and changing direction isn't necessarily giving up.
抱负能让年轻人在进展缓慢时仍有努力的理由。想设计建筑
的学生可能更认真学绘画和数学，因为知道它们有用。但不
必十六岁就把目标定死。探索不同兴趣有价值，改变方向也
不一定就是放弃。
serve a purpose 有明确用途
2. What do young people in your country commonly
dream about?
你所在国家的年轻人通常有什么梦想？ 给出常见愿望而不声
称统计多数，兼顾生活安全感与个人兴趣。
I hear a mixture of practical and personal dreams. Many
young people want a stable income and a comfortable
place to live, while others hope to travel, start a small
business or do creative work. These wishes often
overlap. Someone might want a secure job mainly
because it would support their interest in photography.
我听到的梦想既有实际需求，也有个人愿望。许多年轻人想
要稳定收入和舒适住所，也有人想旅行、创业或做创意工作。
这些愿望常有重叠，比如有人想找稳定工作，主要是为了支
持自己的摄影爱好。
a stable income 稳定收入
3. Do people's dreams differ across generations?
不同代际的人有不同的梦想吗？ 从成长时拥有的机会解释差
异，再指出家庭安稳等共同愿望。
They often do, because people grow up with different
opportunities and expectations. Someone who
experienced financial hardship may place security first,
while a younger person might dream of working abroad
or changing careers. There are shared wishes too, such as
supporting family members. It's the route to a satisfying
life that often differs.
往往不同，因为人们成长时的机会与期待不一样。经历过经
济困难的人可能把安稳放在首位，年轻人则可能梦想去国外
工作或转行。共同愿望也存在，比如支持家人。不同的常常
是通往满意生活的道路。
place security first 把安稳放在首位
4. What prevents people from reaching their
ambitions?
哪些因素会阻碍人实现抱负？ 区分个人可调整的计划与外部
资源限制，避免把失败归咎于懒惰。
Sometimes the barrier is practical, such as training costs
or caring responsibilities, rather than a lack of effort. An
unrealistic plan can also cause trouble: someone may
attempt too much at once and burn out. Breaking a goal
into smaller steps helps, but it doesn't remove the need
for money, time or support.
有时阻碍是培训费用或照顾家人的责任等实际问题，并非不
努力。不现实的计划也会添麻烦：一次想做太多可能把自己
耗尽。把目标分成小步骤有帮助，却不能消除对金钱、时间
和支持的需要。
burn out 耗尽精力
5. Are people more ambitious now than they were in
the past?
现在的人比过去更有抱负吗？ 区分抱负更容易被看见与抱负
真的增强，不直接比较整代人的努力。
Their ambitions may be more visible now because
people share career plans and achievements online.
There are also more possible paths to hear about. That
doesn't prove earlier generations lacked ambition,
though. Building a secure home could require enormous
determination. I would say the forms of ambition have
changed more clearly than its overall strength.
现在的抱负可能更容易被看见，因为人们在网上分享职业计
划和成绩，也能了解更多可能的道路。但这不能证明上一代
没有抱负，建立安稳家庭也可能需要极大决心。我觉得抱负
的形式变化，比整体强弱变化更明确。
possible paths 可能的道路
6. Should parents decide what goals their children
pursue?
父母应该为孩子设定目标吗？ 区分协助制定具体习惯与代替
孩子选择人生目标，说明合作方法。
Parents can help children set realistic goals, but they
shouldn't choose every destination for them. A parent
might help a child practise reading for ten minutes each
evening while letting the child select the books. With
major choices, listening becomes even more important.
A goal works better when the child understands and
accepts it.
父母可以帮助孩子制定现实的目标，但不该替他们决定每一
个方向。例如家长帮助孩子每天晚上阅读十分钟，同时让孩
子选书。遇到重大选择，倾听更加重要。孩子理解并接受的
目标，通常更容易真正执行。
set realistic goals 制定现实的目标

sections.title: 完美的工作
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
目标、决定与解决问题
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
186
话题 114
PART 2
完美的工作
My ideal job
Describe the job that would be ideal for you.
描述一份对你来说理想的工作。
1. What the job would involve
是什么工作
2. How you found out about it
从哪里了解到的
3. What you would need to learn
需要学习什么
4. Why it would suit you so well
为什么特别适合你
审题与选材：理想工作要解释日常做什么，不能只说工资高或环境好。先用一次接触说明信息来源，再列两三项真正需要学
习的能力。通过自己的性格与具体工作任务相连接，说明为什么适合；承认工作也有难处，会让理想听起来更真实。
叙述顺序
A 提出想做社区图书馆儿童馆员 - B 说明在活动中认识这份工作 - C 描述帮助孩子选书的日常 - D 列出需要学习的组织与
沟通 - E 结合自身兴趣说明理想之处
A Choose children's work in a community library - B Discover the role during a weekend event - C Describe helping
children find suitable books - D Identify the practical skills I must learn - E Connect the work with my own interests
示例回答
The job that would suit me best is working with children in a community library. I first discovered this kind of
work when I took my little cousin to a Saturday storytelling session. The librarian didn't just read aloud. She
helped a shy child join in and found another book for someone who was already familiar with the story.
Watching her made me realise that the job combined several things I enjoy: books, conversation and organising
small activities. I'd like to plan reading sessions, recommend books and help children feel comfortable asking
questions. I also like the idea of seeing the same families regularly, rather than having brief conversations with
strangers all day. To get there, I'd need to learn how a library organises its collection and how to select books for
different reading levels. Managing a lively group of children would take practice as well. Being friendly isn't
enough when five children want to speak at once. I know it wouldn't be peaceful all the time, and there would be
paperwork and repetitive tasks. Even so, it feels like a good fit. I would enjoy helping a reluctant reader find one
book they genuinely wanted to take home. That small result would make an ordinary working day satisfying.
中文对照：最适合我的工作是在社区图书馆为儿童服务。我带小表弟参加周六故事活动时，第一次了解这种工作。馆员不
只是朗读，还帮助一个害羞的孩子参与，并给已经熟悉故事的孩子找了另一本书。看着她，我发现这份工作结合了我喜欢
的书、交谈和组织小活动。我想安排阅读活动、推荐书，让孩子愿意提问。我也喜欢经常见到同一些家庭，而不是整天只
与陌生人短暂交谈。要做这份工作，我得学会图书馆如何整理馆藏，以及怎样为不同阅读水平的孩子选书。管理活跃的儿
童小组也需要练习，五个孩子同时想讲话时，光友好不够。我知道工作不会一直安静，也有文书和重复任务。即便如此，
它仍很适合我。帮一个不爱阅读的孩子找到真心想带回家的书，就能让普通工作日令人满足。
自然表达
read aloud
大声朗读
join in
参与进来
a good fit
很合适的选择
a reluctant reader
不愿阅读的人
串题 话题 113 你的抱负/梦想
同一份图书馆工作可以成为长期抱负，但要交代愿望何时形成、对自己的意义，以及培训费用或职位机会等可能阻碍实现的
因素。
Working in a library is also a long-term ambition, although I still need training and a suitable opening.

雅思口语 · 话题与表达
187
话题 114  /  完美的工作
PART 3
1. What makes a job a dream job?
怎样的工作可以称为理想工作？ 把适合的任务、生活需要与
可接受的难处分开，不设统一标准。
A dream job should match someone's interests and
abilities while supporting the life they want. It doesn't
have to be glamorous. For one person, repairing bicycles
with regular hours could be ideal; another may want
constant travel. The important thing is that the everyday
tasks feel worthwhile and the disadvantages are
manageable.
理想工作应符合个人兴趣和能力，也支持想要的生活，不一
定光鲜。有人觉得按时上下班修自行车就很理想，另一些人
想经常出差。关键是日常任务值得做，工作带来的不便也能
承受。
regular hours 规律的工作时间
2. What careers do children often imagine having as
adults?
孩子常想象长大后做什么工作？ 从孩子见得到的人物解释选
择，再说明他们对职业了解有限。
Children often choose jobs they can easily picture, such
as teachers, doctors, firefighters or professional athletes.
Their ideas may come from people they meet or
characters they watch. They usually notice the exciting
parts first. A child who wants to be a chef might imagine
making cakes, rather than cleaning a kitchen after
closing.
孩子常选容易想象的职业，如教师、医生、消防员或职业运
动员。想法可能来自认识的人或看过的角色。他们通常先注
意到有趣部分，比如想当厨师的孩子可能想到做蛋糕，而不
是打烊后清洗厨房。
picture 在脑海中想象
3. Do people's ideas of an ideal job change as they get
older?
人们随着成长会改变对理想工作的看法吗？ 用了解真实任务
和生活责任的变化解释调整，避免说年龄必然降低追求。
Yes, because experience reveals what a job actually
involves. A teenager may love the idea of travelling for
work, then later realise that frequent nights away are
exhausting. Priorities can change when people have
caring responsibilities too. That doesn't mean they lose
ambition; they may simply want a different balance
between work and home.
会，因为经历让人知道一份工作实际上包含什么。青少年可
能喜欢工作出差，后来却发现经常在外过夜很累。有照护责
任时，重点也会改变。这不代表失去抱负，只是可能希望工
作与家庭有不同的平衡。
caring responsibilities 照护责任
4. What should someone think about when choosing a
job?
选择工作时应该考虑什么？ 让薪资、实际任务与成长机会形
成可比较的选项，并提醒了解日常工作。
They should look at the actual duties, pay, working
hours and chances to learn. The manager and team
matter as well, because a pleasant job description can
hide a stressful workplace. If possible, talking to
someone already doing the work is useful. They can
explain what an ordinary Tuesday looks like, not just the
highlights.
应看实际职责、薪酬、工时和学习机会。主管与团队也重要，
因为好看的职位描述可能掩盖紧张环境。如果可能，和正在
做这份工作的人聊聊很有用。他们能说明普通周二是什么样，
而不只是光鲜部分。
job description 职位描述
5. Is pay the main reason people select particular
jobs?
薪酬是人们选择某些工作的主要原因吗？ 先承认基本开支决
定底线，再区分收入充足后可能更在意的条件。
For someone struggling to cover basic expenses, salary
may be the deciding factor, and that's understandable.
Once those needs are met, other things can become more
important, such as reasonable hours or interesting work.
A slightly lower salary might be acceptable if the job
removes a long commute and leaves more time for
family.
对难以支付基本开支的人，薪酬可能决定选择，这可以理解。
基本需求满足后，合理工时或有趣任务等条件可能更重要。
如果工作免去漫长通勤，留下更多陪家人的时间，稍低的工
资也可能可以接受。
the deciding factor 决定性因素
6. Which kinds of jobs are popular in your country?
你的国家哪些工作比较受欢迎？ 说明不同求职者各自看重什
么，不用未经证实的排名概括全国。
Stable positions in education or public services appeal to
people who value predictable employment. Technology
and design roles attract others who want to develop
specialised skills. I wouldn't give one national ranking,
though. A job's popularity depends heavily on the city,
available opportunities and whether applicants care more
about security, income or personal interest.
教育或公共服务领域的稳定岗位吸引重视工作可预期性的人。
技术和设计岗位吸引希望发展专业技能的人。不过我不会给
全国排一个名次。工作受欢迎程度很受城市、机会以及求职
者更重稳定、收入还是兴趣的影响。
specialised skills 专业技能

sections.title: 重要的决定
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
目标、决定与解决问题
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
188
话题 115
PART 2
重要的决定
An important choice I made
Describe an important decision you made.
描述你做过的一个重要决定。
1. What you decided
做了什么决定
2. How you reached the decision
怎样作出决定
3. What happened as a result
结果如何
4. Why the decision mattered
为什么重要
审题与选材：重要决定不必是人生巨变，可以是影响后来生活的一次实际选择。先说清两条可选的路，再讲自己查了什么、
问了谁以及怎样比较。本例用课程与兼职的取舍展开，结果既有收入变化也有学习收获，最后解释重要性。
叙述顺序
A 交代减少周末兼职的决定 - B 解释工作与课程发生冲突 - C 比较预算并咨询任课老师 - D 描述调整后完成小组项目
- E 说明此事如何改变选择习惯
A Decide to reduce my weekend work - B Explain the clash with a practical course - C Compare my budget and ask for
advice - D Complete a project after changing my schedule - E Explain why this choice mattered afterwards
示例回答
An important decision I made was to reduce my weekend hours at a café so I could take a practical design
course. This happened during my second year at college. The extra income was useful, but I was spending
nearly every Saturday working and missing activities connected with my studies. I didn't decide immediately.
First, I wrote down my basic monthly expenses and worked out how much I could earn from one shorter shift. I
also asked the course teacher what students would actually produce. When she showed me a project involving a
local shop, I felt it was worth making room for. Then I spoke to my manager and arranged to work on Sunday
mornings instead of both weekend days. For a while, I had to cut back on takeaway meals and other small treats.
That wasn't especially enjoyable, but it was manageable. The course gave me a chance to work with two
classmates on a real-looking shop display. We made mistakes, adjusted our plan and eventually produced
something I was proud to photograph. The decision mattered because it was the first time I'd weighed short-term
earnings against something that could help me later. I didn't stop working; I simply made a more deliberate
choice about where my time went.
中文对照：我做过的一个重要决定，是减少周末在咖啡馆的工时，去上一门实践设计课。这是大学二年级的事。额外收入
很有用，但我几乎每个周六都工作，错过了与学习有关的活动。我没有马上决定，而是先列出每月基本开支，算只做一个
短班能赚多少，也问老师学生具体要做什么。她展示了一个与当地商店有关的项目，我觉得值得腾时间。之后我与经理商
量，改成周日上午上班，不再两天都做。那阵子我减少了外卖和小享受，虽然不太愉快，却也能适应。课程让我和两位同
学一起做了一个像真正商店那样的陈列。我们犯错、修改计划，最后做出了让我愿意拍照留念的作品。这个决定重要，因
为我第一次权衡眼前收入与未来可能的帮助。我没停止工作，只是更有意识地选择时间花在哪里。
自然表达
work out
算出；弄清
make room for
为……腾出空间或时间
cut back on
减少
weigh against
权衡……与……
串题 话题 116 对结果开心的重要决定
这一决定也能用于满意结果题，保留比较预算和调班过程，但应突出作品完成后的开心，并交代作出选择时到底难在哪里。
I was pleased with the result because the new schedule let me finish a project I cared about.


25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
目标、决定与解决问题
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
189
话题 115  /  重要的决定
PART 3
1. Do children sometimes need to make important
decisions?
孩子有时也需要做重要决定吗？ 用友谊与求助说明影响不只
在金钱，强调成人支持仍然必要。
Yes, although their decisions may look small to adults.
Choosing whether to tell someone about bullying, for
example, can strongly affect a child's safety and
friendships. Children also make choices about activities
and who to trust. They need support with these
decisions, rather than being told that only adults have
important things to consider.
会，尽管在成年人看来那些决定可能很小。例如是否告诉别
人自己遭到欺负，能很大程度影响孩子的安全和友谊。他们
也要选择活动、判断信任谁。这些决定需要支持，而不是被
告知只有大人才有重要事情要考虑。
who to trust 该信任谁
2. What major decisions do teenagers face after
graduating?
青少年毕业后会面对哪些重大决定？ 同时考虑继续学习和开
始工作两条路，解释费用与兴趣怎样影响选择。
They may need to choose between further education,
vocational training and starting work. If they continue
studying, the subject and location are major choices too.
These decisions involve interests, costs and available
support. A teenager might love a course in another city
but need to consider accommodation expenses before
accepting a place there.
他们可能要在继续升学、职业培训和开始工作之间选择。若
继续学习，专业和地点也是大事。这些决定涉及兴趣、费用
和可获得的支持。一个学生可能很喜欢外地的课程，但接受
录取前还得考虑住宿开支。
vocational training 职业培训
3. Who can help children when they are making
decisions?
孩子做决定时可以向谁求助？ 按问题类型选择熟悉情况的人，
而不把一个成人当成所有问题的答案。
Parents are useful because they know the child's
circumstances, while teachers can explain school-related
options. A coach or another trusted adult may help with a
particular activity. The best person depends on the
question. For a course choice, a student already taking it
can also offer details that official descriptions don't
mention.
父母了解孩子的处境，教师能解释学校相关选择，教练或其
他可信任成人可以帮助处理具体活动。找谁最好取决于问题。
选择课程时，正在上这门课的学生还能提供正式介绍中没有
提到的细节。
trusted adult 可信任的成年人
4. Can advertisements affect what we decide to buy?
广告会影响我们的购物决定吗？ 解释熟悉感和限时信息怎样
影响选择，而不是只断言广告很强大。
Definitely. Repeated advertising makes a brand feel
familiar, so people may reach for it without comparing
alternatives carefully. A limited-time offer can also
create pressure to buy immediately. For instance,
someone looking for one plain shirt might add another
because an advertisement makes a discount seem like an
opportunity they shouldn't miss.
当然。重复广告让品牌显得熟悉，人们可能没仔细比较就选
它。限时优惠也会制造马上购买的压力。例如只想买一件普
通衬衫的人，可能因为广告把折扣说成不能错过的机会，而
多买一件。
a limited-time offer 限时优惠
5. Is the influence of advertising generally beneficial?
广告的影响总体上是有益的吗？ 分清有用产品信息与制造不
必要需求，用信息是否清楚作为判断依据。
It can be helpful when it introduces a useful product or
clearly explains a genuine price reduction. The problem
comes when it encourages people to buy things they
can't afford or hides important conditions. I would judge
the influence by the quality of the information, rather
than assuming every advertisement helps or harms
consumers.
如果广告介绍有用产品，或清楚说明真实降价，它会有帮助。
问题是鼓励人们买负担不起的东西，或隐瞒重要条件。我会
根据信息质量判断其影响，不会认为每个广告都帮助或伤害
消费者。
price reduction 降价
6. How do people usually reach major decisions?
人们通常怎样作出重大决定？ 把收集资料、比较后果与听取
建议连成具体过程，并承认时间限制。
They often gather information, compare a few options
and talk to people they trust. With a major purchase, that
might mean checking the total cost and imagining how
they would use it. Some people also need time away
from the problem. Still, urgent decisions may require
choosing with incomplete information rather than
waiting indefinitely.
人们常先收集信息、比较几个选项，再和信任的人讨论。大
额购物时，可能会核对总费用，并想象实际怎么使用。有些
人还需要暂时放下问题。不过紧急决定可能只能在信息不完
整时作出，不能无限等待。
gather information 收集信息

sections.title: 对结果开心的重要决定
sections.titleEn: A decision with a satisfying result
sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
目标、决定与解决问题
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
190
话题 116
PART 2
对结果开心的重要决定
A decision with a satisfying result
Describe an important decision whose result made you happy.
描述一次结果让你开心的重要决定。
1. What you decided
做了什么决定
2. Why you made that choice
为什么这样选择
3. How easy or difficult choosing was
作出选择容易还是困难
4. Why the result pleased you
为什么对结果开心
审题与选材：这题必须同时讲重要性、选择难易和满意结果。可用自己犹豫的具体原因代替一句很难决定，再用决定后的生
活变化证明开心。本例选择住近学校的小房间，代价与好处都清楚，满意来自每天省下的时间而不是笼统的成功。
叙述顺序
A 决定搬进离学校较近的小房间 - B 说明原先通勤带来的疲惫 - C 比较较高租金与节省的时间 - D 描述搬家后的日常明显
变化 - E 用参加晚间活动解释满意
A Choose a smaller room near my college - B Explain how the old commute affected me - C Compare higher rent with time
saved - D Describe ordinary days after the move - E Show why the result made me happy
示例回答
I was really happy with my decision to move into a smaller room near my college. Before that, I lived in a
cheaper flat much further away. Getting to class involved two buses, and if I missed the connection, my whole
morning felt rushed. After one especially tiring week, I started looking at rooms within walking distance. I
found one above a small grocery shop. It was plain, and the desk was squeezed beside the bed, but I could reach
campus in ten minutes. The choice wasn't easy because the rent was higher. I spent several evenings comparing
costs, including bus fares, and discussed it with my parents. I also visited the street after dark to see whether I
felt comfortable there. Eventually, I decided the extra cost was manageable if I cooked more often. Once I
moved, the difference was immediate. I could have breakfast properly instead of carrying it onto a crowded bus.
More importantly, I could stay for the evening study group without worrying about the last convenient
connection home. I was pleased because the decision improved ordinary days, not just one special occasion. My
room had less space, but my schedule had more. I felt less tired and had time to get to know classmates outside
lessons.
中文对照：我很满意自己搬到学校附近一个较小房间的决定。之前我住在远处便宜些的公寓，上课要换两趟公交，错过接
驳车，整个早晨就很赶。一个特别累的星期过后，我开始找步行可到学校的住处，找到杂货店楼上的房间。房间普通，桌
子挤在床边，但到校园只要十分钟。决定并不容易，因为租金更高。我花了几个晚上比较包括车费在内的各项费用，也与
父母讨论，还在天黑后到街上看看是否感觉安心。最后我认为，多自己做饭就能承担额外费用。搬家后区别马上显现：我
能好好吃早餐，不必带到拥挤公交上。更重要的是，我可以参加晚间学习小组，不再担心错过最后一班方便的接驳车。我
开心，是因为这个决定改善了普通日子，不只是某个特别时刻。房间小了，日程却宽裕了。我不那么累，也有时间在课外
认识同学。
自然表达
within walking distance
步行可达
compare costs
比较费用
the extra cost
额外费用
get to know
逐渐认识
串题 话题 115 重要的决定
可直接保留搬家选择与结果，改答重要决定题时增加它怎样影响学习及人际交往；选择难易仍可讲，但不要只停留在开心的
感受。
Moving closer to college mattered because it changed how much time I could devote to study and friendships.

目标、决定与解决问题
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
191
话题 116  /  对结果开心的重要决定
PART 3
1. How can we distinguish an important decision
from an easy one?
怎样区分重要决定和容易的决定？ 指出重要与容易并非相反
概念，再分别看后果大小和比较难度。
Importance concerns the consequences, while ease
concerns how difficult it is to choose. An important
decision can be easy when one option clearly fits your
needs. Choosing an urgent repair might be obvious, for
example. A small decision, like selecting a birthday card,
can take ages even though the consequences are quite
limited.
重要看的是后果，容易看的是选择有多难。如果某个选项明
显符合需求，重要决定也可以很容易，例如决定做紧急维修
可能毫无悬念。挑生日卡这种小决定却可能花很久，尽管后
果其实很有限。
fits your needs 符合你的需求
2. Is making a small decision each day a useful habit?
每天做一个小决定是好习惯吗？ 强调主动选择可练习负责，
同时避免把每日次数说成硬性要求。
Yes, especially for someone who usually lets others
choose everything. Picking a meal or planning a short
walk gives them practice in noticing preferences and
accepting an outcome. But it shouldn't become another
daily target to worry about. The value comes from
making thoughtful choices, not from counting how many
decisions you complete.
是，尤其对习惯让别人决定一切的人。选择一顿饭或安排短
途散步，能练习发现自己的偏好并接受结果。但它不应成为
另一个令人担忧的每日指标。价值在于认真作选择，不在于
数自己完成多少决定。
accepting an outcome 接受结果
3. What small decisions do people make in everyday
life?
人们每天会做哪些小决定？ 选出穿衣、交通和任务顺序，并
说明这些小选择为何仍有实际作用。
People decide what to wear, what to eat and which route
to take to work. They also choose the order of small
tasks, such as answering a message before doing the
washing. These choices rarely change a whole life, but
they affect comfort and time. A sensible lunch choice
can make an afternoon easier.
人们会决定穿什么、吃什么、走哪条路上班，也会安排小任
务的顺序，比如先回消息还是先洗衣。这些选择很少改变整
个人生，却影响舒适程度和时间安排。午餐选得合适，下午
可能就轻松一些。
the order of small tasks 小任务的先后顺序
4. What should a group do when members disagree
about a decision?
小组成员对决定意见不一时该怎么办？ 先找分歧背后的需要，
再提出可试行或可表决的做法避免空谈合作。
They should first find out what each person is trying to
protect, such as cost, time or quality. Sometimes the
disagreement disappears when those needs are clear. If
not, they can compare options against agreed priorities
or try a small test. Voting is useful too, provided
everyone understands the rules before the vote happens.
应先弄清每个人想保住什么，比如成本、时间或质量。有时
这些需求明确后，分歧就消失了。否则可以按共同认可的重
点比较选项，或先小范围试一下。投票也有用，前提是大家
在投票前理解规则。
agreed priorities 共同认可的重点
5. Do people make most of their decisions in their
twenties?
人们大多数决定都是在二十多岁时作出的吗？ 承认初入社会
时重大选择集中，再用中年生活变化说明决定持续发生。
A lot of major first choices happen then, including
starting a career or deciding where to live. But I wouldn't
say most decisions belong to that decade. People
continue choosing as their circumstances change.
Someone in their forties may change careers, care for a
parent or move home, with consequences just as
significant.
很多首次重大选择发生在那时，比如开始职业生涯或决定住
哪里。但我不会说大多数决定都属于那十年。处境变化时，
人们仍不断选择。四十多岁的人也可能转行、照顾父母或搬
家，后果同样重大。
circumstances change 处境发生变化
6. Is it better to make decisions quickly or take more
time?
做决定快一些还是多花时间更好？ 按能否撤回和影响大小判
断速度，再说明拖延也有成本。
It depends on the risk and whether the choice can be
reversed. Choosing a café rarely needs a long discussion,
while signing a housing contract deserves careful
checking. More time is useful only if it brings better
information. Repeating the same worries for days can
delay action without making the eventual decision any
wiser.
取决于风险和选择能否撤回。挑咖啡馆很少需要长谈，签住
房合同却值得仔细核查。多花时间只有带来更好信息才有用。
连续几天重复相同担忧，可能只是推迟行动，并不会让最终
决定更明智。
can be reversed 可以撤回

sections.text:
25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
目标、决定与解决问题
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
192
话题 117
PART 2
改变观点的经历
A change of opinion
Describe an occasion when you changed your opinion.
描述一次你改变看法的经历。
1. When it happened
何时发生
2. What you originally thought
原本怎样想
3. What made you change your mind
为什么改变看法
4. How you felt about the change
改变后感觉如何
审题与选材：先把原观点说得清楚，后面的新信息才能形成真正变化。不要只写别人劝我，而要说明亲自观察到什么，与原
来想法哪里不符。本例以二手物品为线索，用检查、试用和实际效果改变判断，最后表达意外与轻松。
叙述顺序
A 交代原来不愿购买二手物品 - B 说明去年帮朋友搬家的场景 - C 观察朋友检查并试用旧书桌 - D 描述自己后来实际使用
的结果 - E 解释改观后既惭愧又高兴
A Recall my distrust of second-hand furniture - B Visit a friend during a move - C Watch her inspect a used wooden desk
- D Describe using a similar desk myself - E Explain how my opinion and feelings changed
示例回答
Until last year, I thought buying second-hand furniture was usually a false economy. I imagined loose legs,
unpleasant smells and a lot of trouble getting things home. If I needed something, I'd normally look for the
cheapest new version instead. My opinion changed when I helped a friend move into a rented flat. She had
found a used wooden desk nearby and asked me to collect it with her. I expected something rather worn out, but
the desk was solid and only had a few marks on its surface. What impressed me was how carefully she checked
it. She opened every drawer, pressed gently on the corners and measured the space underneath. Then she
explained that she could see exactly what she was getting, rather than guessing from a photograph online. A
month later, I needed a desk myself. I followed her approach and bought one from another student. After a quick
clean, it worked perfectly in my room, and it cost much less than the new desks I'd considered. I felt slightly
embarrassed about my earlier attitude, but mostly pleased. I still wouldn't buy something without checking its
condition. The difference is that I no longer assume used means unreliable. That change has made shopping feel
less expensive and a bit less wasteful.
中文对照：直到去年，我都觉得买二手家具往往是假省钱。我想到的是松动的桌腿、异味，以及搬回家的麻烦。需要东西
时，我通常找最便宜的新货。后来帮朋友搬进出租屋，我改变了看法。她在附近找到一张旧木桌，让我一起去取。我以为
会很破旧，结果桌子结实，表面只有几道痕迹。让我印象深的是她检查得很仔细：打开每个抽屉、轻压各个角，还量了桌
下空间。她解释说，这样能确切看到买的是什么，不用对着网上照片猜。一个月后我也需要书桌，就照她的办法从另一个
学生手里买了一张。简单清洁后，放在房间里很好用，价格比考虑过的新桌低很多。我对原先的态度有点不好意思，但更
多是高兴。我仍不会不检查状况就买东西，只是不再认定旧的就不可靠。这让购物便宜些，也少浪费些。
自然表达
a false economy
表面省钱却不划算的做法
worn out
破旧不堪的
check its condition
检查它的状况
follow her approach
采用她的方法
串题 话题 115 重要的决定
可以把检查二手书桌的过程用于重要决定，但必须说明实际选择影响了什么；改观点题仍要突出原先偏见与新观察之间的差
别。
That experience also helped me decide how to furnish my room without spending more than I could afford.

目标、决定与解决问题
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
193
话题 117  /  改变观点的经历
PART 3
1. When do children start forming opinions of their
own?
孩子从什么时候开始形成自己的观点？ 区分早期偏好与能解
释理由的观点，避免武断给出统一年龄。
They show preferences very early, for example choosing
one game over another. More developed opinions grow
as they gain language, experience and chances to explain
themselves. There isn't one exact age. A child may have
a clear view about playground fairness while still
repeating an adult's opinion about a subject they don't
understand.
孩子很早就表现出偏好，比如选某个游戏。随着语言、经验
和解释机会增加，观点会更成熟，没有统一的准确年龄。一
个孩子可能对操场上的公平有明确想法，却仍在不懂的事情
上重复成人的看法。
explain themselves 说明自己的想法
2. Whose opinions matter more to children, parents'
or teachers'?
对孩子来说，父母还是老师的意见更重要？ 以家庭生活与课
堂任务区分可信来源，不做绝对高低排序。
It depends on the subject and the relationship. Parents
may carry more weight in family matters because
children know them well. Teachers often have greater
influence on classroom tasks, where their expertise is
obvious. If the adults disagree, children can feel
confused, so explaining the reasons behind advice is
more useful than demanding loyalty.
取决于问题和关系。家庭事务中，孩子熟悉父母，父母的话
可能分量更大。课堂任务上，教师的专业能力明显，影响往
往更强。若成年人意见不一，孩子可能困惑，所以解释建议
的理由比要求孩子站队更有用。
carry more weight 更有分量
3. Should teachers hear students' opinions during
lessons?
老师应该在课堂上听取学生意见吗？ 说明倾听能发现理解困
难，同时保留教师安排时间和纠错的责任。
Yes, because students can reveal problems a teacher
hasn't noticed, such as instructions that sound clear but
are confusing in practice. Listening also makes
discussion more meaningful. That doesn't require
accepting every suggestion or letting one student
dominate. A teacher can invite several views, explain the
final choice and then keep the lesson moving.
应该，因为学生能指出老师没发现的问题，比如指令听来清
楚，实际做却让人困惑。倾听也使讨论更有意义，但不代表
接受所有建议或让一个学生占满时间。教师可以听几种意见、
解释最终选择，再继续课堂。
keep the lesson moving 让课堂继续推进
4. Should children develop their opinions at home or
at school?
孩子应在家还是在学校形成自己的观点？ 把两种环境当成互
补机会，说明家庭安全感与同学不同经验的作用。
Both settings are important. Home can offer a safe place
to ask awkward questions, while school exposes children
to classmates with different experiences. They need
chances to explain a view and hear another one in both
places. If only one setting encourages discussion,
children may learn to speak freely there but stay silent
elsewhere.
两个环境都重要。家能提供安心提出难答问题的地方，学校
让孩子接触经历不同的同学。他们在两处都需要解释看法和
听别人观点的机会。如果只有一个地方鼓励讨论，孩子可能
只在那里敢说，到了别处就沉默。
speak freely 自由表达


25-17  /  SPEAKING BOOK
目标、决定与解决问题
雅思口语 · 话题与表达
194
话题 117  /  改变观点的经历
PART 3
5. Why do children sometimes disagree with their
parents?
为什么孩子有时与父母观点不同？ 用不同经历与独立尝试解
释分歧，不把所有不同意见视为叛逆。
They encounter different people, technology and
expectations, so the same situation may look different to
them. They are also practising independence and may
question rules that once seemed automatic. For example,
parents might see an online game as wasted time, while a
child sees an activity shared with friends. Both
perspectives contain information worth hearing.
他们接触的人、技术和期待不同，所以看同一件事可能不一
样。孩子也在练习独立，会质疑曾经理所当然的规则。例如
父母把网络游戏看成浪费时间，孩子却视为和朋友共同参与
的活动，两种观点都有值得听的信息。
practising independence 练习独立
6. How do children decide whether management is
good or bad?
孩子怎样判断管理是好是坏？ 保留管理这一提问范围，用班
级和活动组织说明公平、一致与倾听。
They often judge it through everyday treatment: whether
instructions are clear, rules apply equally and adults
listen when something goes wrong. In a class or club, a
child may call management unfair if favourites escape
consequences. They may overlook less visible planning,
though, so adults can explain why particular
arrangements are necessary.
他们常根据日常待遇判断：指令是否清楚、规则是否平等、
出了问题成人是否听取意见。在班级或社团中，若受宠的人
不用承担后果，孩子可能觉得管理不公平。不过他们可能忽
略背后的安排，成人可以解释某些做法为何必要。
rules apply equally 规则一视同仁
7. In which places can children develop independent
opinions?
孩子可以在哪些地方发展独立观点？ 区别于家庭和学校二选
一，扩展到图书馆、社团和公共生活中的观察。
Libraries, sports clubs and community activities can all
help, as well as home and school. Children meet people
who approach problems differently and can compare
ideas with their own experience. Even discussing a story
after reading it is useful. The key is having room to ask
questions, rather than simply being told the correct
opinion.
除了家庭和学校，图书馆、运动社团及社区活动也有帮助。
孩子会遇到处理问题方式不同的人，并拿自己的经验比较想
法。读完故事后讨论也有用。关键是能提问题，而不是只被
告知什么才是正确观点。
ask questions 提出问题
